{
  "abstract_verbatim": "We prove the three-dimensional Bochner–Riesz conjecture in its strict-order formulation. The main result is boundedness of the Bochner–Riesz multipliers on $`L^3(\\mathbb R^3)`$ for every positive order. Interpolation and duality then give the full conjectured strict range.",

<a id="pm-s1"></a>
## 1. Abstract and result contract

> We prove the three-dimensional Bochner–Riesz conjecture in its strict-order formulation. The main result is boundedness of the Bochner–Riesz multipliers on $`L^3(\mathbb R^3)`$ for every positive order. Interpolation and duality then give the full conjectured strict range.

- **claim-positive-order-multiplier** (theorem, [source](#stmt-thm-bochner-riesz)): For every $\delta>0$, there is a finite constant $C_\delta$ such that $$\norm{T_\delta f}_{L^3(\mathbb R^3)} \le C_\delta\norm f_{L^3(\mathbb R^3)} \qquad(f\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^3)). \label{eq:main-bound}$$ Consequently $T_\delta$ has a unique bounded extension to $L^3(\mathbb R^3)$.
  - Explanation: Every fixed positive smoothing order gives a bounded multiplier and a unique bounded extension on the stated Lebesgue space.
- **claim-entropy-restriction** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-entropy-restriction)): Let $A,B,D,T$ be finite observations. Then $$\begin{aligned} \mathsf I_{\mathrm{nat}}(T;B)&\le\mathsf I_{\mathrm{nat}}(T;A)+\mathsf H_{\mathrm{nat}}(B\mid A),\label{eq:entropy-determination}\\ \|\mathsf H_{\mathrm{nat}}(B\mid T)-\mathsf H_{\mathrm{nat}}(A\mid T)\| &\le\mathsf H_{\mathrm{nat}}(B\mid A)+\mathsf H_{\mathrm{nat}}(A\mid B).\label{eq:entropy-change} \end{aligned}$$ If, outside an event of probability $\zeta$, $B$ has at most $N$ possible values given $A$, and $\|\mathcal B\|\le M$, then $$\mathsf H_{\mathrm{nat}}(B\mid A)\le\log2+\log N+\zeta\log M. \label{eq:entropy-ambiguity}$$ For nonnegative numbers $m_b$ with $m_b>0$ on the support of $B$, $$\mathsf H_{\mathrm{nat}}(B)+\mathbb E\log m_B\le\log\sum_bm_b. \label{eq:entropy-masses}$$ Finally, let $\mathsf P,\mathsf Q$ be laws on the same space with $\mathsf Q\le K\mathsf P$, $K\ge1$. For arbitrary $B,D$, $$\begin{aligned} \mathsf H_{\mathrm{nat}}^{\mathsf Q}(D\mid B) &=\mathbb E_{\mathsf Q}[-\log\mathsf P(D\mid B)] -\mathbb E_{\mathsf Q_B} \mathop{\mathrm{KL}}(\mathsf Q_{D\mid B}\Vert\mathsf P_{D\mid B}),\label{eq:conditional-kl}\\ \mathbb E_{\mathsf Q_B} \mathop{\mathrm{KL}}(\mathsf Q_{D\mid B}\Vert\mathsf P_{D\mid B}) &\le\log K.\label{eq:conditional-kl-bound} \end{aligned}$$ In particular, restriction to an event of $\mathsf P$-mass $m>0$ costs at most $\log(1/m)$ in <a href="#eq:conditional-kl-bound" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:conditional-kl-bound">[eq:conditional-kl-bound]</a>. None of these estimates depends on the cardinality of $B$ or $T$.
  - Explanation: Chain rules, support counts, log-sum, and relative entropy control determination and restriction without bounding the parent alphabet.
- **claim-typical-conditioning** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-typical-conditioning)): Let $\mathsf U,\mathsf V$ be probability laws on the same finite space with $\mathsf U\le A\mathsf V$, $A\ge1$, and let $C$ be a finite observation. For $0<\eta<1$, $$\mathsf U_C\{c:\mathsf U_C(c)<\eta\mathsf V_C(c)\}\le\eta. \label{eq:conditioning-likelihood}$$ At every other $\mathsf U_C$-positive value, $$\mathsf U(\,\cdot\mid C=c) \le \frac A\eta\,\mathsf V(\,\cdot\mid C=c).$$ The estimate is independent of the number of values of $C$.* *In particular, let $\mathsf P$ be a finite law, let $\mathcal E$ have mass $m=\mathsf P(\mathcal E)>0$, and put $\mathsf U=\mathsf P(\,\cdot\mid\mathcal E)$ and $r_C(c)=\mathsf P(\mathcal E\mid C=c)$. Then $$\begin{gathered} \mathsf U_C(c)=\frac{\mathsf P_C(c)r_C(c)}m,\qquad \mathsf U_C\{r_C<t\}\le\frac tm\quad(t>0),\\ \mathsf U(\,\cdot\mid C=c) \le r_C(c)^{-1}\mathsf P(\,\cdot\mid C=c). \end{gathered} \label{eq:retention-fibers}$$ The last inequality is asserted on positive $\mathsf U_C$ fibers. Thus for $0<\eta_0<1$, outside $\mathsf U_C$-mass $\eta_0$, their domination constants are at most $(m\eta_0)^{-1}$.* *Suppose further that $C$ is a function of a finite parent observation $X$, and write $r_X(x)=\mathsf P(\mathcal E\mid X=x)$. On every positive $C=c$ fiber, for $0<\eta_1<1$, $$\mathsf U\{r_X(X)<\eta_1r_C(c)\mid C=c\}\le\eta_1. \label{eq:nested-retention-fibers}$$ Removing these parent values does not change a conditional law given $X$. Let $d_-\le d_+$ be real numbers. If a finite child $Y$ satisfies, on every $(X,Y)$ value attained in $\mathcal E$, $$d_-\le-\ell^{-1}\log\mathsf P(Y\mid X)\le d_+, \qquad \ell=\log(1/\epsilon),$$ then there are at most $\epsilon^{-d_+}$ retained children over each parent, and, with $\mathsf U_c=\mathsf U(\,\cdot\mid C=c)$, $$d_- -\frac{\log(1/r_C(c))}{\ell} \le \mathsf H^{\mathsf U_c}(Y\mid X)\le d_+. \label{eq:typical-cell-entropy}$$ More precisely, outside $\mathsf U_c$-mass at most $\eta_1+\eta_2$, $$d_- -\frac{\log(1/(\eta_1r_C(c)))}{\ell} \le-\ell^{-1}\log\mathsf U_c(Y\mid X) \le d_+ +\frac{\log(1/\eta_2)}{\ell}, \qquad 0<\eta_2<1. \label{eq:typical-cell-surprise}$$ These conclusions concern the retained support and sampled conditional values. They assert no lower mass bound for every untrimmed child.
  - Explanation: Typical conditioning preserves named domination bounds and yields entropy, surprise, and support estimates on retained children.
- **claim-finite-splitting-resampling** (construction, [source](#stmt-lem-entropy-splitting)): For any finite tag $Q$, $$\begin{aligned} 0\le\mathsf H_{\mathrm{nat}}(D\mid B)-\mathsf H_{\mathrm{nat}}(D\mid B,Q)&\le\mathsf H_{\mathrm{nat}}(Q),\\ \|\mathsf I_{\mathrm{nat}}(T;D\mid Q)-\mathsf I_{\mathrm{nat}}(T;D)\|&\le\mathsf H_{\mathrm{nat}}(Q),\\ \mathsf I_{\mathrm{nat}}(U;V\mid Z,Q)&\le\mathsf I_{\mathrm{nat}}(U;V\mid Z)+\mathsf H_{\mathrm{nat}}(Q). \end{aligned}$$ The conditional quantities on the left are averages of the quantities on the individual tag fibers. If $U,V$ are conditionally independent given $Z$ under $\mathsf P$, and $\mathsf R\le K\mathsf P$, then $$\mathsf I_{\mathrm{nat}}^{\mathsf R}(U;V\mid Z)\le\log K.$$ Given a joint law of $(T,C,V)$ and a kernel $\kappa(u\mid T,C)$, one may adjoin $U$ by this kernel while preserving that entire joint law. The new $U$ is conditionally independent of $V$ given $(T,C)$, and its joint law with $(T,C)$ is the prescribed kernel law.
  - Explanation: Finite tags control information changes, and conditional kernel resampling preserves the entire specified original joint law.
- **claim-finite-homogenization** (construction, [source](#stmt-lem-homogenization)): Fix a law $\mathsf P$, a finite list $(X_j,Y_j)$, $1\le j\le q$, and numbers $A_j\ge0$ such that $\|\mathcal Y_j\|\le\epsilon^{-A_j}$. There is no cardinality assumption on $X_j$. For $a,\sigma,\theta>0$, there are disjoint events $E_z$ whose union has probability at least $1-q\epsilon^\sigma-\theta$, with the following properties. The number of events is at most $$J=\prod_{j=1}^q\left(1+\left\lceil\frac{A_j+\sigma}{a}\right\rceil\right), \qquad m_z:=\mathsf P(E_z)\ge\theta/J.$$ For each $z,j$ there is $d_{j,z}\in[0,A_j+\sigma]$ such that, on $E_z$, $$d_{j,z}\le -\ell^{-1}\log\mathsf P(Y_j\mid X_j) \le d_{j,z}+a. \label{eq:homogeneous-bin}$$ If $\mathsf R$ is any law supported on $E_z$ satisfying $\mathsf R\le K\mathsf P(\,\cdot\mid E_z)$, then $$d_{j,z}-\frac{\log(K/m_z)}\ell \le\mathsf H_{\mathsf R}(Y_j\mid X_j)\le d_{j,z}+a. \label{eq:homogeneous-entropy}$$ More precisely, for every $0<\eta<1$, outside a set of $\mathsf R$-probability at most $2\eta$, $$d_{j,z}-\frac{\log(K/(m_z\eta))}\ell \le-\ell^{-1}\log\mathsf R(Y_j\mid X_j) \le d_{j,z}+a+\frac{\log(1/\eta)}\ell. \label{eq:homogeneous-surprise}$$ There are at most $\epsilon^{-(d_{j,z}+a)}$ retained $Y_j$ values over each fixed $X_j$ value. The support-count assertion and <a href="#eq:homogeneous-bin" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:homogeneous-bin">[eq:homogeneous-bin]</a> are uniform on the retained support, before any further restriction is chosen.
  - Explanation: Uniform surprise bins produce retained events with controlled mass, conditional entropy, conditional surprise, and child counts.
- **claim-likelihood-trimming** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-zero-information)): Let $\pi$ be a law and let $\Lambda$ be a comparison probability law with $\pi\ll\Lambda$. Write $L=d\pi/d\Lambda$ and $D=\mathop{\mathrm{KL}}(\pi\Vert\Lambda)$. For every $v>0$, $$\pi(\log L>v)\le\frac{D+1/e}{v}. \label{eq:likelihood-tail}$$ Consequently, if $D=o(\ell)$, there is $v=o(\ell)$ such that $\pi(\log L>v)=o(1)$, and the remaining subprobability is bounded by $e^v\Lambda$. This applies in particular to $$\Lambda(a,b,c)=\pi_C(c)\pi_{A\mid C}(a\mid c) \pi_{B\mid C}(b\mid c), \qquad D=\mathsf I_{\mathrm{nat}}^\pi(A;B\mid C).$$ Conversely, if a probability law $\rho$ satisfies $\rho\le K\prod_{i=1}^k\mu_i$, then $$\mathop{\mathrm{KL}}\left(\rho\middle\Vert\prod_i\rho_i\right)\le\log K. \label{eq:product-information}$$
  - Explanation: Small relative entropy gives domination after trimming; product domination bounds information relative to actual marginals.
- **claim-simultaneous-marginal-core** (construction, [source](#stmt-lem-marginal-core)): Let $\nu$ be a subprobability of mass $m>0$ on a finite space. For $1\le l\le r$, suppose a tuple of observations $(F_{l1},\ldots,F_{lk_l})$ satisfies $$\nu_{F_{l1},\ldots,F_{lk_l}} \le A_l\prod_{j=1}^{k_l}\mu_{lj}, \label{eq:core-comparison}$$ where every $\mu_{lj}$ is a specified probability law. Put $q=\sum_l k_l$. Repeated occurrences of an observation with different comparison laws are counted separately. For $0<\eta<m/q$ there is a restriction $\nu'$ of $\nu$, of mass $M\ge m-q\eta$, such that $\rho=\nu'/M$ satisfies all the bounds $$\rho_{F_{l1},\ldots,F_{lk_l}} \le A_l M^{k_l-1}\eta^{-k_l} \prod_{j=1}^{k_l}\rho_{F_{lj}}. \label{eq:core-actual}$$ Support counts persist, and every marginal mass upper bound for $\nu$ persists for $\rho$ with the factor $M^{-1}$. In particular, taking $\eta=m/(2q)$ retains mass at least $m/2$.
  - Explanation: Repeated marginal deletions retain a common core on which every listed product comparison uses actual retained marginals.
- **claim-finite-star-conditioning** (construction, [source](#stmt-thm-finite-conditioning)): Let $\pi(p,b)$ be a probability law with $\mu=\pi_P$, $\lambda=\pi_B$. Let $E$ be an allowed set with $\pi(E)\ge1-\zeta$ and suppose $$\boldsymbol1_E(p,b)\pi(p,b)\le K\mu(p)\lambda(b),\qquad K\ge1. \label{eq:pair-product}$$ Choose $0<\alpha<1$ with $\zeta<1-\alpha$, retain only point fibers with $r(p):=\pi(E\mid P=p)\ge\alpha$, and normalize the pairs in these fibers and in $E$ to a law $q$. Its retained mass $M_0$ satisfies $$M_0\ge1-\frac{\zeta}{1-\alpha},\qquad q(p,b)\le M_0^{-1}\pi(p,b),\qquad q(b\mid p)\le c\lambda(b),\quad c:=K/\alpha. \label{eq:star-kernel}$$ For a fixed integer $n\ge1$, sample $B_1,\ldots,B_n$ independently given $P$ with kernel $q(b\mid p)$, and let $$S(p,b_1,\ldots,b_n)=q_P(p)\prod_{i=1}^nq(b_i\mid p).$$ The following are comparison probability laws on the whole star: $$\begin{aligned} \Lambda_0&=q_P\otimes\lambda^{\otimes n}, &S&\le c^n\Lambda_0,\label{eq:star-independent}\\ \Lambda_i&=q_{P,B_i}\otimes\bigotimes_{j\ne i}\lambda_{B_j}, &S&\le c^{n-1}\Lambda_i\quad(1\le i\le n). \label{eq:star-pair} \end{aligned}$$ Here $q_{P,B_i}$ is a copy of the retained pair law $q$. It may be replaced by the original $\pi$ in <a href="#eq:star-pair" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:star-pair">[eq:star-pair]</a> at the additional cost $M_0^{-1}$.* *Let $R=wS/m$, where $0\le w\le1$ and $m=\mathbb E_Sw>0$. Fix an index set $J\subset\{1,\ldots,n\}$ of *fixed labels*; write $F=\{1,\ldots,n\}\setminus J$ for the *free labels*. Choose any observation $$C=(B_J,Z),\qquad Z=f(P,B_J).$$ Thus the function defining $Z$ involves the point and the fixed labels only. For every $0<\eta<1/(n+1)$, there is a set of $C$ values of $R_C$-mass at least $1-(n+1)\eta$ on which, simultaneously, $$\begin{aligned} R(\,\cdot\mid C)&\le\frac{c^n}{m\eta}\Lambda_0(\,\cdot\mid C), \label{eq:conditional-independent}\\ R(\,\cdot\mid C)&\le\frac{c^{n-1}}{m\eta} \Lambda_i(\,\cdot\mid C),\quad1\le i\le n. \label{eq:conditional-pair} \end{aligned}$$ For a fixed value $C=(b_J,z)$, put $z_{b_J}(p)=f(p,b_J)$. Ignoring the deterministic coordinates $B_J$, these comparison laws are exactly $$\begin{aligned} \Lambda_0(\,\cdot\mid b_J,z) &=q_P(\,\cdot\mid z_{b_J}(P)=z) \otimes\bigotimes_{j\in F}\lambda_{B_j}, \label{eq:fixed-comparison-zero}\\ \Lambda_i(\,\cdot\mid b_J,z) &=q_P(\,\cdot\mid B_i=b_i,z_{b_J}(P)=z) \otimes\bigotimes_{j\in F}\lambda_{B_j}, &&i\in J,\label{eq:fixed-comparison-pair}\\ \Lambda_i(\,\cdot\mid b_J,z) &=q_{P,B_i}(\,\cdot\mid z_{b_J}(P)=z) \otimes\bigotimes_{j\in F\setminus\{i\}}\lambda_{B_j}, &&i\in F.\label{eq:free-comparison-pair} \end{aligned}$$ Conditionals in this display need only be defined when their conditioning event has positive comparison mass; the inequalities hold at every $R$-positive value under consideration.* *There is also a direct comparison using the actual point marginal. There is a set $G$ of $(P,C)$ values with $R(G)\ge1-\eta$ such that, for every $C$ value, as an inequality of subprobabilities, $$\boldsymbol1_G(p,C)R(p,b_F\mid C) \le\frac{c^{\|F\|}}{m\eta}R_P(p\mid C) \prod_{j\in F}\lambda(b_j). \label{eq:actual-point-free}$$ For $0<\tau<1$, outside $C$ values of $R_C$-mass at most $\eta/\tau$, the subprobability on the left has mass at least $1-\tau$. In any of these conditionals, all applicable product comparisons, including product comparisons for coordinate tuples at several fixed labels, may be converted *simultaneously* to comparisons using their actual retained marginals by Lemma <a href="#lem:marginal-core" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:marginal-core">7</a>. If the subprobability after all prior trims, including intersection with $G$ when used, has conditional mass $u$ and the resulting list has $N_{\mathrm{fac}}$ factor occurrences, its core has conditional mass at least $u/2$ and each $k$-factor comparison constant $A$ becomes at most $A(2N_{\mathrm{fac}}/u)^k$. All exceptional-mass and domination estimates above are independent of the number of possible values of $C$, $P$, and the labels.
  - Explanation: Conditional star sampling and explicit comparison laws control fixed-label conditioning, free labels, and simultaneous marginal replacement.
- **claim-point-slicing** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-cor-point-slicing)): Fix the values of some labels. On that fiber let $\nu$ be a retained probability law of a point $P$ and free labels $(B_j)_{j\in F}$, with $$\nu\le A\nu_P\otimes\bigotimes_{j\in F}\lambda_j.$$ The comparison laws $\lambda_j$ may be the actual marginals obtained by a simultaneous core on this fiber. If $Z=f(P)$, then on every positive $Z$ fiber, $$\nu(p,b_F\mid Z=z) \le A\nu_P(p\mid Z=z)\prod_{j\in F}\lambda_j(b_j).$$ Thus the comparison label populations are those *before* the point slice, and any mass upper bounds already proved for them remain available. After a further restriction and core of conditional mass $M>0$, each new actual label marginal is bounded by $A/M$ times its respective $\lambda_j$.
  - Explanation: Point-only slicing preserves the named pre-slice label populations, and later restriction has an explicit marginal mass cost.
- **claim-profile-diagonals** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-lem-profile-diagonal)): The following three statements hold.* 1. *Suppose for each $\epsilon\to0$ there is a countable list $(X_j,Y_j)_{j\ge1}$, with $\|\mathcal Y_j\|\le\epsilon^{-A_j}$ for each fixed $j$. One can partition all but $o(1)$ of the law into $\epsilon^{-o(1)}$ parts, each of mass at least $\epsilon^{o(1)}$, such that the following holds. From any choice of one retained part at each scale, a subsequence can be extracted on which every listed observation is homogeneous. The same exponents are inherited by every sequence of laws supported on those parts whose density relative to their normalized laws is at most $\epsilon^{-o(1)}$. The assertion is simultaneous for joint observations and observations conditional on an exact particle index, when these are included in the list.* 2. *Let $v$ range over a compact rectangle of depth parameters. Suppose observations $Y_v$, conditional on any $X$, obey, uniformly for fixed $u,v$, the two ambiguity bounds $$\log N(Y_v\mid Y_u,X),\ \log N(Y_u\mid Y_v,X) \le C\ell\\|u-v\\|_1+o(\ell),$$ and have bounded normalized alphabet sizes at one reference depth. Their normalized entropy profiles have subsequences converging on all depths to a $C$-Lipschitz function, after extraction on a countable dense set. Homogeneous surprise exponents on that dense set extend to the same function at every fixed depth, provided the ambiguity bounds also hold on the retained support.* 3. *Suppose a finite construction at each fixed $h>0$ has finitely many normalized errors tending to zero as $\epsilon\to0$. Given any sequence of permissible $h_k\downarrow0$, and any countable sequence of such requirements, a diagonal can be chosen so that the first $k$ requirements have errors at most $h_k/k$ and $h_k\log(1/\epsilon_k)\to\infty$. Thus errors may be made $o(h)$ before passing to the scale $\epsilon^h$. This assertion supplies no rate uniform in $h$ or in the limiting profile.
  - Explanation: Countable homogenization, ambiguity-controlled profile limits, and successive diagonals preserve the required order of limits.
- **claim-discrete-furstenberg** (bound, [source](#stmt-thm-ren-wang)): Fix $0<s\le1$, $0<d\le2$, and $\alpha>0$. There are $\eta_0=\eta_0(\alpha,s,d)>0$ and $\rho_0=\rho_0(\alpha,s,d)>0$ with the following property. Suppose $\mathcal P$ is a nonempty $(\rho,d,\rho^{-\eta_0})$-set of squares, with $0<\rho<\rho_0$. For each $p\in\mathcal P$, let $\mathcal T(p)$ be a family of tubes meeting $p$, of cardinality comparable to $M$, and forming a $(\rho,s,\rho^{-\eta_0})$-set. Then $$\#\bigcup_{p\in\mathcal P}\mathcal T(p) \gtrsim_\alpha \rho^{-\min\{1,d,(d+s)/2\}+\alpha}M . \label{eq:ren-wang-discrete}$$ The statement is unchanged by fixed bounded domains, finitely many coordinate charts, or fixed-factor enlargements of the grids and tubes, after decreasing $\eta_0,\rho_0$ if necessary.
  - Explanation: Nonconcentrated point squares carrying nonconcentrated tube families force a lower bound on the tube union.
- **claim-weighted-tagged-projection** (bound, [source](#stmt-thm-planar-projection)): Fix $0<d\le2$, $0<s\le1$, and $\alpha>0$, and fixed bounded point and slope domains. There are $\eta>0$ and $\rho_1>0$ such that the following holds for $0<\rho<\rho_1$. Let $\mu$ be a finite probability population of points in $\mathbb R^2$. Let $\nu$ be a finite probability population of tags $b$, with a slope $a(b)$ assigned to each tag. Suppose $$\begin{aligned} \mu(B(z,r))&\le \rho^{-\eta}r^d, & (a_*\nu)(I)&\le \rho^{-\eta}r^s \label{eq:projection-populations} \end{aligned}$$ for all balls and intervals of radius or length comparable to $r\in[\rho,1]$. Let $G$ be a graph of point–tag incidences with $(\mu\times\nu)(G)\ge\rho^\eta$. For each tag $b$, suppose that the projection $\pi_{a(b)}(x)$ of its neighbors can be covered by at most $M$ intervals of length $\rho$. Here $\pi_a(x_1,x_2)=x_2-a x_1$. One may multiply these maps by scalars whose absolute values have fixed positive lower and upper bounds. Then $$M\ge \rho^{-\min\{1,d,(d+s)/2\}+\alpha}. \label{eq:weighted-projection-finite}$$ Changing the implicit fixed factors in the domains, projections, and interval lengths changes only $\eta,\rho_1$.* *In particular, along any sequence with subpower nonconcentration constants, graph product mass $\rho^{o(1)}$, and conditional projection count at most $\rho^{-l-o(1)}$, one has $$l\ge \min\{1,d,(d+s)/2\}. \label{eq:weighted-projection-limit}$$ The limiting assertion for $d=0$ is immediate.
  - Explanation: Weighted point and slope populations with a dense incidence graph force projection expansion even when tags share slopes.
- **claim-classical-growth** (bound, [source](#stmt-thm-classical-growth)): For the aperture systems of Definition <a href="#def:classical-aperture" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="def:classical-aperture">14</a>, the rate in <a href="#eq:classical-score" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:classical-score">[eq:classical-score]</a> satisfies $\beta\le\gamma$.
  - Explanation: The universal positive-transport score growth is bounded by the aperture eccentricity penalty.
- **claim-saturated-splitting** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-classical-splitting)): Let $Z$ be a finite tag. If $\Delta=\beta t+\tau_L(T)-\mathcal F_t(G)$, and $\Delta_z$ is the corresponding deficit for the law conditional on $Z=z$, then $$\mathbb E\Delta_Z\le\Delta+3\mathsf H(Z).$$ In particular subpower splittings preserve saturation on typical parts, simultaneously for any fixed finite list of saturated observations.
  - Explanation: The mean conditional saturation deficit is controlled by the original deficit and tag entropy.
- **claim-greedy-cap-regularization** (construction, [source](#stmt-lem-classical-cap-regularization)): After a subpower splitting and removal of probability $o(1)$, a particle law can be restricted to classes with a bounded number $h$ such that $$\Pr_T(\operatorname{cap}(D)) \le\epsilon^{w(D)-h-o(1)},\qquad \tau_L(T)=h+o(1). \label{eq:classical-cap-bounds}$$ The cap bound is uniform over the root menu and its fixed enlargements. For a further law $Q\le\epsilon^{-\eta}\Pr_T$ on such a class, $\tau_L(Q)\le h+\eta+o(1)$. Hence a subpower restriction or tilt preserving the displayed score profiles preserves saturation.
  - Explanation: Greedy cap classes align a uniform cap probability bound with the root supremum and preserve saturation under controlled tilts.
- **claim-classical-localization** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-lem-classical-localization)): Let $G$ have fixed shape $(b,a)$ at $t$, put $e=a-b$, and fix $0\le r<t$, $0\le d\le e$. Let $J$ be the aperture at $r$ of shape $(b,b+d)$ whose frame is the depth-$d$ prefix of the frame of $G$. Set $\zeta=\mathsf H(R_d\mid T,C_r)$. Conditional on $J$, there are bounded line systems with final shape $(0,e-d)$, duration $t-r$, and horizon $L'=e-d+t-r$. With $\tau'_J$ their root suprema, $$\begin{aligned} \mathcal F_t(G) &\le\beta(t-r)+w(b,b+d)-\mathsf I(T;J)\notag\\ &\qquad{}+2S_r+\mathbb E\tau'_J+2\zeta+o(1), \label{eq:classical-local-first}\\ w(b,b+d)-\mathsf I(T;J)+2S_r+\mathbb E\tau'_J &\le\beta r+\tau_L(T)+o(1). \label{eq:classical-local-second} \end{aligned}$$ Here parameters are fixed before $\epsilon\to0$. Uniform versions have errors $C\xi+C\log(C_0)/\log(1/\epsilon)+\omega_\epsilon$ for depth-rounding mesh $\xi$, fixed enlargement bound $C_0$, and the compact parameter bounds in <a href="#eq:classical-uniform" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:classical-uniform">[eq:classical-uniform]</a>. If $\zeta=o(1)$ and $G$ is saturated, typical conditional systems are saturated and near-maximizing compositions give a saturated predecessor at $r>0$.
  - Explanation: Anisotropic rescaling yields local line systems whose root tests compose into global predecessor apertures.
- **claim-least-aspect-extremizer** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-prop-least-aspect)): There exists a saturated sequence at duration one with $b=0$, endpoint aspect $e=m$, and horizon $1+m$, where $m\ge0$ is the least aspect of any such saturated sequence. One may moreover require $Y_j$ conditional on $X_j$ to be homogeneous for a prescribed countable list of finite pairs $(X_j,Y_j)$, provided that for each fixed $j$ there is $0\le A_j<\infty$, independent of $\epsilon$, such that $\|\mathcal Y_j\|\le\epsilon^{-A_j}$ for all sufficiently small $\epsilon$. No cardinality bound is imposed on $X_j$, which may include the exact particle $T$.
  - Explanation: Subsequence selection and homogenization produce a saturated limiting sequence with least possible aspect.
- **claim-saturated-coherent-path** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-prop-saturated-path)): The sequence in Proposition <a href="#prop:least-aspect" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="prop:least-aspect">19</a> can carry, on one joint law of $(T,c)$, saturated observations $G_u$ at every positive dyadic time $u\le1$. Their shapes satisfy $$b(1)=0,\quad a(1)=m,\quad b(r)\ge b(t),\quad a(r)+r\le a(t)+t\quad(r<t), \qquad e(u):=a(u)-b(u)\ge mu.$$ They can be constructed so that $\mathsf H(R_{e(u)}\mid T,C_u)=o(1)$. There is a constant $K_\gamma$, independent of $r,t$, for which the orientations at $r<t$ agree with probability tending to one at every positive depth $$d<\min(e(r),e(t))-K_\gamma \bigl(\|b(r)-b(t)\|+\|a(r)-a(t)\|+t-r\bigr). \label{eq:classical-coherence}$$ All statements refer to the inner $\epsilon$ limit with the times fixed.
  - Explanation: Saturated predecessors can share one underlying particle-time law and have coherent orientations at fixed times.
- **claim-tangent-dichotomy** (classification, [source](#stmt-prop-isotropic-reduction)): One of the following alternatives holds for the least aspect $m$.* 1. *If $m=0$, there is a saturated sequence of duration and horizon one, with isotropic endpoint $(b,a)=(0,0)$ and homogeneous conditional time profile $$\mathsf H(C_u\mid T)=su+o(1),\qquad 0\le u\le1, \quad 0\le s\le1.$$* 2. *If $m>0$, the saturated path can be represented by a single orientation $R$ with depth-$mu$ prefixes at time $u$, for every $0<u\le1$, and $\mathsf H(R_{mu}\mid T,C_u)=o(1)$. Its shapes satisfy $$e(u)=mu,\qquad b(u)\text{ is Lipschitz},\qquad 0\le-b'(u)\le1+m\quad\text{a.e.}$$ There is $\kappa>0$ such that its limiting conditional orientation entropies obey $$\mathsf H(R_{m(u+h)}\mid T,C_u)\ge\kappa h, \qquad 0<u<u+h<1. \label{eq:orientation-growth}$$ The alternatives and the positive lower bound persist after homogeneous splittings that preserve the saturated path.
  - Explanation: A least-aspect path has either an isotropic tangent or matched positive aspect with persistent orientation growth.
- **claim-isotropic-exclusion** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-prop-isotropic-exclusion)): Suppose that $0<\gamma<1$ and that the classical universal growth rate satisfies $\beta>\gamma$. There is no saturated isotropic system of duration and horizon $1$ furnished by Proposition <a href="#prop:isotropic-reduction" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="prop:isotropic-reduction">21</a>, with homogeneous conditional time profile $\mathsf H(C_u\mid T)=su$, $0\leq u\leq1$.
  - Explanation: Excess classical growth contradicts the existence of a saturated isotropic system with a homogeneous linear time profile.
- **claim-retained-intercept-count** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-isotropic-intercepts)): Suppose an incidence population uses at most $N$ point cells. For every retained exact particle and slope bin incident to it, suppose there are at least $m$ distinct retained time children in the same base cell and slope bin. Suppose further that these children lie on one line of true slope within $O(\rho)$ of the bin representative. Then, for each slope bin, all its retained incidences use at most $CN/m$ intercept cells of side $\rho$.
  - Explanation: Rich retained time fibers bound the number of occupied intercept cells by a double-counting argument.
- **claim-grid-projection-counts** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-isotropic-grid-projections)): Let $E$ be a set of occupied $\rho$-cells in a fixed bounded region.* 1. *In $\mathbb R^3$, let $v_1,v_2,v_3\in\mathbb R^2$ be bounded slopes and put $D=\abs{\det((1,v_1),(1,v_2),(1,v_3))}>0$. If $\pi_{v_i}(E)$ uses at most $N_i$ cells, with bounded enlargements permitted, then $$\abs E^2\leq C D^{-6}N_1N_2N_3. \label{eq:isotropic-lw}$$* 2. *In $\mathbb R^2$, for two bounded scalar slopes $v_1,v_2$ with $\abs{v_1-v_2}\geq\rho^a$, if their intercepts use at most $N_1,N_2$ cells, then $$\abs E\leq C\rho^{-2a}N_1N_2. \label{eq:isotropic-two-projections}$$
  - Explanation: Separated slopes give discrete projection bounds through an invertible coordinate change and Loomis–Whitney.
- **claim-characteristic-plane-traces** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-thm-characteristic-trace)): Suppose $f$ is locally Lipschitz on $\mathcal D$, and, in its interior, $$0\le f_j\le d_j,\qquad 0\le f_v\le d_v, \qquad f_{jk}\le0\ (j\ne k),\qquad f_{jv}\le0$$ in the distributional sense. The derivative bounds may instead be local bounds on each compact neighborhood under consideration; in that case all conclusions concerning boundedness are local. Then there are, up to null sets, uniquely determined locally bounded fields $a_1,\ldots,a_n,D$ on $\mathbb R\times I$, with $0\le a_j\le d_j$ and $0\le D\le d_v$, having the following properties.* 1. **Strong traces.* For almost every interior offset $\eta\in\mathcal K^\circ$, the restrictions of the ambient gradients to $\Pi(\cdot)+\eta$ are defined almost everywhere. As $\eta\to0$ through such offsets, they converge strongly in $L^1_{\rm loc}(di\,du)$ to $(a_1,\ldots,a_n,D)$. For $Q\Subset Q'\Subset\mathbb R\times I$ this convergence has the bound $$\label{eq:trace-quantitative-slices} \\|f_\alpha(\Pi(\cdot)+\eta)-A_\alpha\\|_{L^1(Q)} \le C_Q\|\eta\|+\omega_{\alpha,Q'}(C_Q\|\eta\|), \qquad A=(a_1,\ldots,a_n,D),$$ where $\omega_{\alpha,Q'}(r)\to0$ is the $L^1$ translation modulus of $A_\alpha$ on $Q'$. The constant depends only on the local derivative bounds, the clock speeds, and the two patches.* 2. **Measure identities.* There exist locally finite nonnegative measures $\nu_{jk}=\nu_{kj}$, $j\ne k$, and $\nu_{jv}$ on the plane such that $$\label{eq:trace-mixed-measures} V_j a_j=-\nu_{jv}-\sum_{k\ne j}(c_k-c_j)\nu_{jk}, \qquad \partial_iD=-\sum_j\nu_{jv}.$$ For $F=f\circ\Pi$, the weak derivatives are $$\label{eq:trace-plane-derivatives} F_i=\sum_j a_j,\qquad F_u=\sum_j c_ja_j+D.$$ In particular, $$\label{eq:trace-distribution-inequality} V_n a_n\ge\partial_iD$$ as measures. With $q_j=1+c_n-c_j$, the full flux identity is $$\label{eq:trace-measure-flux} -\sum_jq_jV_ja_j =\sum_{j<k}(c_k-c_j)^2\nu_{jk}+\sum_jq_j\nu_{jv}.$$* 3. **Affine approximation.* There is a sequence $h_\ell\downarrow0$ and a single null set $N\subset\mathbb R\times I$ such that, for every $(i,u)\notin N$ and every finite $R$, $$\label{eq:trace-affine-blowup} \lim_{\ell\to\infty}\sup_{\xi\in\mathcal K,\ \|\xi\|\le R} \left\| \frac{f(\Pi(i,u)+h_\ell\xi)-f(\Pi(i,u))}{h_\ell} -\sum_j a_j(i,u)\xi_j-D(i,u)\xi_v \right\|=0.$$ Only sufficiently large $\ell$, for which the displayed label times belong to $I$, are used. The sequence may depend on $f$.
  - Explanation: Mixed derivative signs give strong traces on the selected plane, measure identities, and subsequential affine approximation.
- **claim-finite-trace-approximation** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-cor-finite-characteristic-trace)): Assume Theorem <a href="#thm:characteristic-trace" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:characteristic-trace">26</a>, and let $f_\epsilon\to f$ locally uniformly on $\mathcal D$ along the sequence of finite systems under consideration. Fix a bounded measurable base patch $Q$ of positive measure with compact closure in $\mathbb R\times I$, a radius $R\ge1$, an error $\eta>0$, an exceptional proportion $0<\tau<1$, and a maximum block length $h_*>0$. There exist $$0<h<h_*,\qquad G\subset Q,\qquad \|Q\setminus G\|\le\tau\|Q\|,$$ and a compact neighborhood $K_0\subset\mathcal D$ containing all $\Pi(q)+h\xi$ with $q\in\overline Q$, $\xi\in\mathcal K\cap B_R$, such that the following holds. If $$\label{eq:trace-finite-tolerance} \\|f_\epsilon-f\\|_{L^\infty(K_0)}\le\eta h/4,$$ then, simultaneously for every $q\in G$ and every $\xi\in\mathcal K\cap B_R$, $$\label{eq:trace-finite-affine} \|f_\epsilon(\Pi(q)+h\xi)-f_\epsilon(\Pi(q))-hA(q)\cdot\xi\| \le\eta h.$$ In particular, for every finite family of such displacements, every information increment between two of them differs from its affine value by at most $2\eta h$. An alternating sum of $r$ profile values whose affine contributions cancel has absolute value at most $r\eta h$.* *All dependencies have the order $$f,\ Q,R,\eta,\tau,h_*\quad\longrightarrow\quad h,G,K_0 \quad\longrightarrow\quad\epsilon_0.$$ For every member of the converging finite sequence with $\epsilon<\epsilon_0$, <a href="#eq:trace-finite-tolerance" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:trace-finite-tolerance">[eq:trace-finite-tolerance]</a> holds. If finitely many entropy identities also incur a total normalized ambiguity error at most $B/\log(1/\epsilon)$, one may, after choosing $h$, require in addition $$\log(1/\epsilon)\ge B/(\eta h).$$ Each such combined identity then has at most one additional $\eta h$ of error. More generally one may prescribe any sequences $\eta_\ell,\tau_\ell\downarrow0$ and $h_{*,\ell}\downarrow0$ and select successively $h_\ell<h_{*,\ell}$, then the inner approximation thresholds. If $\sum_\ell\tau_\ell<\infty$, almost every point of $Q$ belongs to all but finitely many of the resulting $G_\ell$.
  - Explanation: After selecting the limiting profile and block scale, local uniform convergence gives simultaneous finite affine estimates.
- **claim-transverse-curve-traces** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-lem-curve-traces)): Let $b$ be Lipschitz on an interval $J$, and let $\Gamma=\{(b(u),u):u\in J\}$ lie in an open plane region. Suppose bounded fields $a_j,D$ in this region satisfy $V_ja_j\in\mathcal M_{\rm loc}$ and $\partial_iD\in\mathcal M_{\rm loc}$, where $\mathcal M_{\rm loc}$ denotes locally finite signed measures. Put $p(u)=-b'(u)$ at points where this derivative exists. For almost every $u\in J$ the field $D$ has two strong traces $D^-,D^+$ and every $a_j$ with $c_j\ne p(u)$ has two strong traces $a_j^-,a_j^+$. Specifically, at $q_0=(b(u_0),u_0)$ the mean of $\|a_j-a_j^\pm(u_0)\|$ tends to zero on the corresponding tangent half-ball $$B_\rho(q_0)\cap \{\ \pm(i-b(u_0)+p(u_0)(u-u_0))>0\ \}, \qquad\rho\downarrow0,$$ and likewise for $D$. The same assertion holds with the actual sides $\pm(i-b(u))>0$. No assertion is made about the field whose speed equals $p(u_0)$.* *If, in addition, $V_na_n\ge\partial_iD$, then at almost every transverse point $p\ne c_n$, $$\label{eq:trace-curve-jump} D^- -D^+\ge(c_n-p)(a_n^+-a_n^-).$$ These conclusions apply to curves on the boundary of an aperture region whenever the fields are defined in an ambient neighborhood; one then retains only the side lying in that region.
  - Explanation: Directional measure derivatives give strong curve traces at transverse speeds and a signed jump inequality.
- **claim-matched-rate-transfer** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-prop-rate-transfer)): For almost every point $(i,u)$ of the characteristic plane with $i>0$ and $0<u<1$, put $s=S'(u)$. There is a constant $\sigma>0$, depending only on the matched process and $m$, for which $0<s\le1$ and the following assertions hold.* 1. *If $m\ne1$, each of the chains $x\longrightarrow y$ and $w\longrightarrow z$ has the rule $$d>0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad e\ge\min(1,d+s),$$ where $d,e$ are its source and target rates. Each of $x\longrightarrow w$ and $y\longrightarrow z$ has the same rule with $\sigma$ in place of $s$.* 2. *If $m=1$, then $$x>0\Longrightarrow q\ge s,\qquad x>0,\ z<1\Longrightarrow z\ge x+s,\qquad z<1\Longrightarrow q\le2-s.$$* *The bounds include $0\le x,y,w,z\le1$, or $0\le q\le2$ in the tied case, supplied by the coordinate capacities.
  - Explanation: Planar projection tests transfer positive coordinate rates; tied clocks require a joint middle rate and additional conditional tests.
- **claim-affine-block-core** (construction, [source](#stmt-lem-affine-block-core)): Fix an integer $k\ge1$. Let $p^0$ be a probability law on a finite pair space $\mathcal P\times\Theta$. Write $\mu^0=p^0_P$ and $\lambda^0=p^0_\theta$. Let $Q_j=Q_j(P,\theta)$, $1\le j\le k$, be finite coordinate observations, and put $\xi_j^\theta=p^0_{Q_j\mid\theta}$ on positive label fibers, choosing an arbitrary probability law on a zero-mass label fiber. Define the two nonnegative natural-log quantities $$\begin{aligned} D_{\mathrm{pair}} &=\mathop{\mathrm{KL}}(p^0_{P,\theta}\Vert\mu^0\otimes\lambda^0),\\ D_{\mathrm{coord}} &=\mathop{\mathrm{KL}}\left(p^0_{\theta,Q_1,\ldots,Q_k} \middle\Vert \lambda^0(\theta)\prod_{j=1}^k\xi_j^\theta(Q_j)\right)\\ &=\sum_{j=1}^k\mathsf H_{\mathrm{nat}}^{p^0}(Q_j\mid\theta) -\mathsf H_{\mathrm{nat}}^{p^0}(Q_1,\ldots,Q_k\mid\theta). \end{aligned}$$ The second quantity is averaged over the labels; no individual label is assumed to have small conditional multiinformation.* *Let $\mathcal F$ be a finite list of observations on the pair space which contains $P$, $\theta$, and every $(\theta,Q_j)$. It may also contain any finite list of prefix and joint observations. Write $N=\|\mathcal F\|$, counting occurrences rather than values. Let $\mathcal H$ be an event of $p^0$-mass at least $1-\zeta$, where $\zeta\ge0$. For $v>0$, choose $$0<\underline M \le1-\zeta-\frac{D_{\mathrm{pair}}+D_{\mathrm{coord}}+2/e}{v}, \qquad \delta=\frac{\underline M}{2N}.$$ Then there is a restriction $r\le\boldsymbol1_{\mathcal H}p^0$, of mass $M\ge\underline M/2$, such that, for every listed observation $F$ and every value with $r_F(f)>0$, $$\delta p^0_F(f)\le r_F(f)\le p^0_F(f). \label{eq:block-core-floors}$$ For the normalized law $\pi=r/M$, write $\mu=\pi_P$ and $\lambda=\pi_\theta$. Its pair law and its coordinate law on every positive label fiber satisfy $$\begin{aligned} \pi(P,\theta) &\le e^v M\delta^{-2}\mu(P)\lambda(\theta), \label{eq:block-core-pair}\\ \pi(Q_1,\ldots,Q_k\mid\theta) &\le e^v\delta^{-k} \prod_{j=1}^k\pi(Q_j\mid\theta). \label{eq:block-core-coordinate} \end{aligned}$$ All factors on the right of these two inequalities are marginals of this same law $\pi$.* *If $A,B$ are listed observations and $A$ is determined by $B$, then for every retained child value $b$, with parent $a=A(b)$, $$\delta p^0(B=b\mid A=a) \le \pi(B=b\mid A=a) \le\delta^{-1}p^0(B=b\mid A=a). \label{eq:block-core-prefix-ratio}$$ The upper inequality can be summed over any set of child values. The lower inequality is asserted only for retained children. In particular, fix $0<\rho<1$. If on $\mathcal H$ the original conditional surprises for this pair lie in $[d_-,d_+]$ in units $L=\log(1/\rho)$, then every retained parent has at most $\rho^{-d_+}$ retained children, and its retained conditional child masses obey $$\delta\rho^{d_+} \le\pi(B=b\mid A=a)\le\delta^{-1}\rho^{d_-}.$$ When a parent is nested only up to bounded ambiguity, include it in the child symbol before applying this assertion.
  - Explanation: Likelihood trimming and repeated marginal floors construct one finite core with actual pair and conditional coordinate products.
- **claim-directional-bootstrap** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-prop-directional-bootstrap)): Let $0<s\le1$. Let a sequence of pair laws of bounded planar parameters $(A,B)$ be dominated, with subpower loss at precision $\rho$, by the product of two populations having conditional child bounds of rate $s$. Assume that for each fixed $t>0$, both comparison marginals satisfy $$\label{eq:rate-no-strip} \sup_{\ell}\mu\{\mathop{\mathrm{dist}}(\cdot,\ell)\le\rho^t\} \le\rho^{\kappa_t+o(1)}\quad\text{for some }\kappa_t>0,$$ and likewise for the other marginal. Suppose the direction-prefix probabilities conditional on either pin are homogenized on the same pair law. For each finite test, assume a common event of subpower pair mass on which the required original direction bins are uniform and the pair support lies over the simultaneous tested good-parent fibers for the child bounds. Then, on uniform trims, the direction of $B-A$ conditional on either pin has prefix ball dimension at least $s$. The assertion is hereditary under subpower restrictions which retain the stated child bounds and product comparisons.
  - Explanation: Reciprocal projection tests raise conditional direction dimension to the parameter child rate under product domination and absence of strip concentration.
- **claim-contact-rate-tuples** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-lem-closure-contact-tuples)): At almost every $u_0\in(0,1)$, set $$b_0=b(u_0),\qquad p=-b'(u_0),\qquad s=S'(u_0).$$ The following assertions hold on each side of the contact curve that lies inward from the aperture boundary. Minus denotes smaller $i$ and plus denotes larger $i$.* 1. *Rescale area measure on a fixed bounded region of positive area in a tangent half-plane and form the joint distribution of the generic plane rates. Tuples in a subsequential limiting support obey the capacity bounds and all the implications of Proposition <a href="#prop:rate-transfer" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="prop:rate-transfer">29</a>, with the fixed value $s$. Every data rate with clock $c_j\ne p$, and also $D$, has a fixed value on each such support, equal to its one-sided strong trace. Here $c_j\in\{0,1,m,1+m\}$, with the two middle clocks grouped when $m=1$.* 2. *Every tuple on either side satisfies $$F(p)+D=2s-\beta-\gamma m. \label{eq:closure-contact-identity}$$* 3. *There is a minus tuple with $B\le0$ whenever that side is admissible, and there is a plus tuple with $B\ge0$ whenever that side is admissible.* 4. *If both sides are admissible and $p<1+m$, then $$D^- -D^+\ge (1+m-p)(z^+-z^-). \label{eq:closure-jump}$$* *If $b_0=0$, then $p=0$ and the plus side is admissible. If $b_0+(1+m)u_0=L$, then $p=1+m$ and the minus side is admissible.
  - Explanation: Inward limiting rate tuples obey transferred constraints, the contact identity, horizontal sign selection, and the transverse jump bound.
- **claim-positive-tangent-rate** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-closure-positive-x)): At the contact points of Lemma <a href="#lem:closure-contact-tuples" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:closure-contact-tuples">32</a>, $x^-\ge\gamma$ if $p>0$. If $p=0$, an admissible plus tuple can be chosen with $x\ge\gamma>0$.
  - Explanation: Aperture refinement forces a positive tangent rate at contact, including a suitable tuple when that rate is characteristic.
- **claim-contact-sign-algebra** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-closure-sign-algebra)): Let $m>0$, $0<s\le1$, and let a rate tuple obey the capacity bounds and the implications of Proposition <a href="#prop:rate-transfer" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="prop:rate-transfer">29</a>. Put $p_*=(1+m)/2$. Then $$\begin{aligned} x>0,\ z<1&\quad\Longrightarrow\quad F(p_*)\ge1+s, \label{eq:closure-midpoint}\\ x>0,\ z=1&\quad\Longrightarrow\quad F(0)\ge1+s, \label{eq:closure-left-end}\\ x=0,\ z<1&\quad\Longrightarrow\quad F(1+m)\ge1+s. \label{eq:closure-right-end} \end{aligned}$$ Moreover, if $x>0$, $z<1$, and $0\le p\le p_*$, replacing $z$ by $1$ in $F(p)$ gives a number at least $1+s$.
  - Explanation: Capacity and rate-transfer constraints force algebraic lower bounds at the midpoint, endpoints, and the specified replaced-coordinate expression.
- **claim-packet-growth** (bound, [source](#stmt-thm-packet-growth)): For the phase class <a href="#eq:packet-phase" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:packet-phase">[eq:packet-phase]</a>–<a href="#eq:packet-definiteness" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:packet-definiteness">[eq:packet-definiteness]</a>, $\beta_{\mathrm q}\le\gamma/2$. Equivalently, for fixed admissible depth parameters and uniform bounds on the data, and for every $\nu>0$, there is $\epsilon_0>0$ such that $$P_t\le K_0+\left(\frac\gamma2+\nu\right)t \qquad(0<\epsilon<\epsilon_0). \label{eq:packet-growth-finite}$$ The same statement holds for convergent bounded parameters with positive limiting duration.
  - Explanation: The packet score growth is bounded by half the eccentricity parameter, with a finite small-precision formulation for fixed data classes.
- **claim-uniform-packet-bessel** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-packet-bessel)): At a fixed time anchor, packets with natural spacings $\rho$ in velocity and $\sigma=(\lambda\rho)^{-1}$ in position satisfy $$\sum_O m_O(f)\le C\\|f\\|_2^2,\qquad \left\\|\sum_T c_T g_T\right\\|_2^2\le C\sum_T\|c_T\|^2, \label{eq:packet-bessel}$$ where $g_T$ are the normalized synthesis packets with the opposite phase sign. These inequalities hold for subsets and for canonical supremum masses. Their constants depend only on ellipticity, finitely many phase and amplitude derivative bounds, support sizes, and lattice multiplicity, and not on the number of sites or on the position cutoff.* *More precisely, packets at this same time and scale obey, for every integer $M\ge1$, $$\|\langle g_{V,X},g_{V',X'}\rangle\| \le C_M\mathbf 1_{\{\|V-V'\|\le C\rho\}} \left(1+\frac{\|X-X'\|}{\sigma}\right)^{-M}. \label{eq:packet-gram}$$ At a local root, where both natural spacings equal $s$, let $F$ be any allowed phase-space cap and let $F^R$ denote its enlargement by distance $Rs$ in each velocity and position coordinate, $R\ge2$. For $h=\sum_Tc_Tg_T$ and every integer $M>2$, canonical analysis gives $$\sum_{O\in F}m_O(h) \le C\sum_{T\in F^R}\|c_T\|^2 +C_M R^{4-2M}\sum_T\|c_T\|^2. \label{eq:packet-cap-bessel}$$ Here a fixed enlargement of the support sizes is included in $F^R$. Every axis of $F$ is at least $s$; consequently $F^R$ is covered by at most $CR^4$ caps of the same widths.
  - Explanation: Uniform Gram decay yields analysis, synthesis, and cap-localized Bessel bounds, including independent choices of amplitudes at sites.
- **claim-finite-packet-decomposition** (construction, [source](#stmt-lem-packet-decomposition)): Fix the data bounds, admissible depths, $r<t$, and $b_*\le b$. Put $\Delta=u_r-b_*$; then $\Delta\ge(t-r)/2>0$. For each localization $J_0$, there is a finite family of atoms $$g_T(v)=\rho_r^{-1}\eta_T((v-V_T)/\rho_r) e^{-i\lambda\Phi(C_r,X_T,v)}, \qquad h_J=\sum_Tc_Tg_T, \label{eq:packet-earlier-atoms}$$ with $V_T$ within a fixed enlargement of its velocity cell and $\|X_T-X_J\|\le C\epsilon^{r+b_*}$. The amplitudes have uniform derivative bounds, the sites have bounded multiplicity, and $\sum_T\|c_T\|^2\le C\\|f\\|_2^2$. Each coefficient is an analysis test at time $r$. If $r=0$, then $$\|c_T\|^2\le C_{\rm can}m_T^{\rm can}(f) \label{eq:packet-coeff-canonical}$$ with a fixed constant.* *More quantitatively, choose $0<\eta<\Delta/4$ and any required power $A>0$. There are an integer integration order $M$, a coefficient cutoff exponent $B$, constants $C_A$, and $\epsilon_0>0$, depending only on these choices and the fixed data, such that, for $0<\epsilon<\epsilon_0$:* 1. *Replacing $f$ by $h_J$ in every endpoint pairing belonging to $J_0$ changes it by at most $C_A\epsilon^A\\|f\\|_2$. Coefficients with $\|c_T\|^2<\epsilon^B\\|f\\|_2^2$ may be omitted with the same error.* 2. *An individual endpoint test interacts, up to such an error, only with overlapping velocity supports and atoms satisfying $$\|V-V_T\|\le C\rho_t,\qquad \|X-X_T-(C_t-C_r)V_T\|\le C\epsilon^{-\eta}\sigma_r. \label{eq:packet-transport}$$ This assertion also holds for any subset of the retained coefficients.* 3. *If one subsequently sums squared errors over at most $C\epsilon^{-Q}$ tests, the orders can be chosen to give total squared error at most $C_A\epsilon^{2A}\\|f\\|_2^2$.* *For example it suffices to choose $$M>4+\frac{A+Q+4}{\min(\eta,\Delta/2)},\qquad B>2A+3Q+10. \label{eq:packet-tail-orders}$$ Only finitely many derivatives, up to an order determined by $M$, are used. All constants are fixed before $\epsilon$ tends to zero. The enlargement parameter $\eta$ may tend to zero afterwards. After the finite family and its coefficient cutoff $B$ have been chosen, the integration order for the transport estimate in part 2 can be increased independently, without changing that family or $B$.
  - Explanation: A finite Fourier decomposition provides earlier packet atoms, coefficient tests, and controlled transport and truncation errors.
- **claim-greedy-packet-cap-classes** (construction, [source](#stmt-lem-cap-class)): In a geometric localizer, bin nonnegligible coefficients so that $$\|\log_{1/\epsilon}\!\left(\|c_T\|^2\right)-\log_{1/\epsilon}\!\left(m\right)\|\le\xi \label{eq:packet-mass-bin}$$ on each bin. Each bin admits a partition into classes, with a count parameter $g$ and fixed assigned-cap widths, having the following properties. If $N_{\rm all}$ is the full class size, then for every allowed local root cap $F$, $$\log_{1/\epsilon}\!\left(\#\{T\hbox{ in the class}:T\in F\}\right)+w(F) \le g+e_{\rm pkt}. \label{eq:packet-cap-count}$$ An empty count imposes no restriction. There is an assigned cap $E=E(T)$ whose nonempty fibers in the full class satisfy $$\log_{1/\epsilon}\!\left(\#\{T:E(T)=E\}\right) \ge g-w(E)-e_{\rm pkt}. \label{eq:packet-assigned-fiber}$$ There are only a number of classes polynomial in $1+\ell$, with constants depending on the fixed exponents and $\xi$. Any further tagged subdivision preserves <a href="#eq:packet-cap-count" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:packet-cap-count">[eq:packet-cap-count]</a>; its retained size is denoted by $N\le N_{\rm all}$. The lower bound <a href="#eq:packet-assigned-fiber" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:packet-assigned-fiber">[eq:packet-assigned-fiber]</a> always refers to the full class.
  - Explanation: Greedy cap selection partitions coefficient bins into classes with cap occupancy upper bounds and whole assigned-fiber lower bounds.
- **claim-local-root-comparison** (bound, [source](#stmt-prop-local-root-comparison)): Fix a winning retained class as above, and use translated coordinates <a href="#eq:packet-rescale-coordinates" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:packet-rescale-coordinates">[eq:packet-rescale-coordinates]</a>. Let $K_0^{\rm loc}$ be the canonical root supremum of its input, including the norm option. Set $$A_J=\log_{1/\epsilon}\!\left(N\right)+\frac32\log_{1/\epsilon}\!\left(m\right)+\frac12g. \label{eq:packet-local-root-value}$$ Then, with the error convention <a href="#eq:packet-finite-error" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:packet-finite-error">[eq:packet-finite-error]</a>, $$K_0^{\rm loc}\le A_J+e_{\rm pkt}. \label{eq:packet-local-root-upper}$$ For any chosen marginal law on the tagged localizers there is an earlier test, using the original input at time $r$, with score $$P_r^{\rm all}\ge\mathsf H(J)+b_*+ \mathbb E\left[\log_{1/\epsilon}\!\left(N_{\rm all}\right)+\frac32\log_{1/\epsilon}\!\left(m\right)+\frac12g\right] -e_{\rm pkt}. \label{eq:packet-earlier-whole-score}$$ At $r=0$, the right hand side is a lower bound for $K_0$ up to the displayed error. The earlier test uses the uniform law on each *whole* class before the final retained subdivision.
  - Explanation: The retained superposition has a controlled local root score, while the earlier lower test uses the whole assigned class.
- **claim-preliminary-packet-growth** (bound, [source](#stmt-prop-packet-trivial-growth)): The supremum $\beta_{\mathrm q}$ is finite and $\beta_{\mathrm q}\le1$. This conclusion uses no identification of the original coherent mass with a positive particle law.
  - Explanation: Coarsened coherent masses and an auxiliary contributor law give a finite preliminary growth ceiling.
- **claim-finite-packet-composition** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-prop-finite-packet-composition)): Fix $0\le r<t$, a shape $0\le b\le a\le\min(L-t,u_t)$, and $0\le b_*\le b$. Choose $0<\eta<(u_r-b_*)/4$, and make the decomposition and cap-class construction of Section <a href="#sec:packet-structure" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:packet-structure">9</a>, with the mass floor <a href="#eq:composition-mass-floor" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:composition-mass-floor">[eq:composition-mass-floor]</a>. Within the localizer $J$, including its auxiliary tags, let $N_{\rm all}(J)$ be the size of the whole cap class, $N(J)>0$ its retained size, $m(J)$ its coefficient mass bin, and $g(J)$ its cap maximum bin. Set $$\begin{aligned} A_J&=\log_{1/\epsilon}\!\left(N(J)\right)+\tfrac32\log_{1/\epsilon}\!\left(m(J)\right)+\tfrac12g(J), \label{eq:composition-A}\\ K_r^*&=\mathsf H(J)+b_*+ \mathbb E\left[\log_{1/\epsilon}\!\left(N_{\rm all}(J)\right) +\tfrac32\log_{1/\epsilon}\!\left(m(J)\right)+\tfrac12g(J)\right]. \label{eq:composition-Kstar} \end{aligned}$$ Let $K_J$ denote the canonical local root score, including its norm option, for the retained local superposition. Let $P_J$ be its score at duration $t-r$, with the conditional output law and the winning superposition masses. All expectations here use the current marginal of $J$ after the indicated preliminary split.* *With $\mathcal R$ as in <a href="#eq:composition-error-budget" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:composition-error-budget">[eq:composition-error-budget]</a>, enlarged by a fixed constant if necessary, the following four quantities are nonnegative: $$\begin{aligned} d_0&=K_0+\beta_{\mathrm q}r-K_r^*+2\mathcal R,\nonumber\\ d_1(J)&=\log_{1/\epsilon}\!\left(N_{\rm all}(J)/N(J)\right),\nonumber\\ d_2(J)&=A_J-K_J+\mathcal R,\nonumber\\ d_3(J)&=K_J+\beta_{\mathrm q}(t-r)-P_J+\mathcal R. \label{eq:four-packet-deficits} \end{aligned}$$ Up to the displayed error allowances, these are the deficits in growth before the cut, class retention, the local root comparison, and growth after the cut. The next inequality shows that saturation at the endpoint forces these four comparisons to be nearly sharp on average; the subsequent selection estimate specifies the branches on which this remains true. Writing $\Delta_t=K_0+\beta_{\mathrm q}t-P_t$, one has the finite bound $$\label{eq:finite-packet-deficits} d_0+\mathbb E(d_1+d_2+d_3)\le\Delta_t+5\mathcal R.$$ There is also an earlier test on the *retained uniform classes*, with that same current marginal of $J$ and the assigned cap labels, whose score satisfies $$\label{eq:retained-back-score} P_r^{\rm ret}\ge K_r^* -\tfrac32\mathbb Ed_1-\mathcal R.$$ At $r=0$ this is an actual test for the original canonical $K_0$; the norm option is not used in this lower bound.* *More quantitatively, put $R_t=\Delta_t+5\mathcal R$. For an event $B$ measurable in $J$ with probability $p>0$ and any $\theta>0$, $$\label{eq:packet-typical-selection} \mathbb P\bigl(B\cap\{d_1+d_2+d_3>\theta\}\bigr) \le R_t/\theta.$$ In particular, taking $\theta=2R_t/p$ leaves at least $p/2$ of the current probability in $B$, and bounds each of the three local deficits by $2R_t/p$. If $R_t=0$, all three vanish almost surely.
  - Explanation: Composition separates growth, retention, and local root deficits, controls their total mean, and provides a retained earlier test.
- **claim-boundary-slack-exclusion** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-lem-packet-boundary-slack)): Assume Theorem <a href="#thm:classical-growth" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:classical-growth">15</a> and $\beta_{\mathrm q}>\gamma/2$. A saturating packet law at any fixed positive duration has $$\label{eq:active-packet-boundary} a=u_t+o(1)$$ on its typical fixed-shape branches. More precisely, if $r=t-2h>0$ and $a+2h\le u_r-2\eta$, the construction above with $b_*=b$ gives $$\label{eq:off-boundary-finite-growth} P_t\le K_0+\beta_{\mathrm q}r+\gamma h +C\mathcal R+\tfrac12\omega^{\rm cl}_{\mathcal B}(\epsilon).$$ Here $\omega^{\rm cl}_{\mathcal B}\to0$ is the fixed-class error in the classical growth theorem, and the constant is fixed for this cut.
  - Explanation: The classical transport estimate rules out a fixed uncertainty slack in a saturating packet system with excessive growth.
- **claim-boundary-backward-alternatives** (classification, [source](#stmt-prop-boundary-alternatives)): Assume $\beta_{\mathrm q}>\gamma/2$. For every fixed integer $q\ge1$ and every fixed $M>0$, a saturation array approaching $\beta_{\mathrm q}$ admits $q$ successive backward cuts at times $$t_j=t_0-2jh>0\quad(0\le j\le q),\qquad u_{t_j}>h,$$ with $h>0$ fixed in the inner limits, satisfying one of the following alternatives.* 1. *A forced array exists. One can use the same such array, choose a fixed $\nu>0$ from <a href="#eq:forced-root-gap" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:forced-root-gap">[eq:forced-root-gap]</a>, and take all the times early enough that the saturated tests satisfy $$a_j=u_{t_j}+o(1),\qquad a_j-b_j\ge\nu/2+o(1),\qquad a_j-b_j\ge M h/\gamma+o(1).$$ Every cut uses $b_*=b_j$ at its later endpoint.* 2. *No forced saturation array exists. At all the indicated times one can use exact isotropic boundary tests $a_j=b_j=u_{t_j}$, and every cut uses $b_*=0$.* *These assertions remain valid when a prescribed finite number of subdivisions with vanishing tag cost are made at each step, before the earlier test is constructed. In particular the earlier law is uniform on the retained classes produced by those subdivisions. For any prescribed positive accuracy, all the assertions about saturation hold at sufficiently small finite precision with that accuracy; the required precision can depend on the outer bounds, $q,h,\nu,M$, the subdivision costs, and the selected branch.
  - Explanation: A fixed finite backward chain uses either elongated tests forced by a root gap or exact isotropic boundary tests.
- **claim-credit-retention** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-packet-credit-retention)): Suppose a finite law satisfies $\mathbb P(W=w\mid P=p)\leq\epsilon^{k-\alpha}$. Let $A$ have probability $p_A>0$, and let $\zeta>0$. Under the law conditioned on $A$, the set of fibers on which $$\mathbb P(A\mid P)<p_A\epsilon^\zeta$$ has probability at most $\epsilon^\zeta$. On every remaining fiber, $$\mathbb P(W=w\mid P,A)\leq \epsilon^{\,k-\alpha-\zeta-\log_{1/\epsilon}\!\left(1/p_A\right)}. \label{eq:credit-retention}$$ Removing the exceptional fibers does not change this conditional bound. The same assertion holds when $P$ includes other previously fixed labels.
  - Explanation: Conditioning on an event preserves a conditional probability cap on typical parent fibers with an explicit retention cost.
- **claim-normal-prediction** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-lem-orientation-prediction)): Assume the elongated geometry. On $\pi^{\rm buf}$, suppose the replacement losses for the isotropic apertures of widths $a$ and $b$ are included in $C_*\eta$. Take two copies $(O,D),(O',D')$, independent conditional on $P$, and set $$A_{\rm sep}=\{\angle(n(D),n(D'))\ge\epsilon^{4h}\}.$$ If this event has probability at least $1/4$, require the same replacement bounds on both marginals of the law conditioned on $A_{\rm sep}$. Then there is a deterministic normal $n(P)$, defined on every coarse cell used by the atom partition, such that $$\angle(n(D),n(P))\le C\epsilon^{4h}$$ on a part of $\pi^{\rm buf}$-probability at least $3/4$.
  - Explanation: Small isotropic replacement losses force coarse cells to predict aperture normals on a large retained part.
- **claim-earlier-aperture-alignment** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-orientation-alignment)): For the elongated prepared cut, let $\nu$ be a current endpoint law supported on $A_{\rm pre}$, with the frozen winner map, and let $d_i,R_t$ be its deficits and bound from Proposition <a href="#prop:finite-packet-composition" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="prop:finite-packet-composition">41</a>. Let $B$ be a $J$-measurable event of misaligned winners, with $p=\nu(B)>0$, and put $\varrho=\nu(\,\cdot\mid B)$. In local coordinates write $e=a-b$ and $(j,l)$ for the assigned-cap widths. Assume the common shape bins satisfy $$l=e+h+O(\eta),\qquad l-j\ge e_0-O(\eta),$$ as supplied by the boundary alternative, and that the prepared packet, cap, and label errors are included in $C_*\eta$. Then $$p\,[2\gamma e_0-C_*(h+\eta)] \le \mathbb E_\nu\!\left[\boldsymbol1_B(d_1+3d_2+3d_3)\right] \le 3R_t . \label{eq:alignment-misaligned-mass}$$ Thus a positive bracket bounds the current probability of misaligned winners by the current finite deficit.
  - Explanation: A positive eccentricity gap makes misaligned winners consume finite composition deficit, enabling their exclusion.
- **claim-finite-packet-repayment** (bound, [source](#stmt-prop-finite-repayment)): Fix $0<\gamma<1$ and a comparison rate $b_{\mathrm q}\in[0,1]$. For the prepared cut constructed above, let $\eta$ bound the composition budget $\mathcal R$, $\theta+\xi+(\log C)/\ell$, all logarithmic class, winner, tail, and label costs, the current mean $\mathbb E_\pi d_1$, and the finite classical growth error on the fixed class of lines, after a fixed increase of $C_*$. The selected endpoint and earlier replacement and composition deficits required in the construction are at most $\eta$ on their specified current laws, including the two conditional prediction marginals. The common shape and count bins have width at most $\eta$; in the isotropic case they also give the error in <a href="#eq:repayment-isotropic-score" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:repayment-isotropic-score">[eq:repayment-isotropic-score]</a>. When $k_f>0$, assume <a href="#eq:repayment-selected-credit" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:repayment-selected-credit">[eq:repayment-selected-credit]</a> under $\pi$ with its accumulated error $\alpha_f\le\eta$. Finally suppose $$P_t\ge B_r+2b_{\mathrm q}h-\Delta . \label{eq:repayment-saturation-input}$$ Then the prepared statistic $P,n(P),W,k$ under $\mu$ satisfies $$0\le k\le d h+C_*\eta,\qquad k\ge k_f+(4b_{\mathrm q}-2\gamma)h-2\Delta-C_*\eta, \quad d=\begin{cases}1&\text{elongated},\\2&\text{isotropic}. \end{cases} \label{eq:finite-packet-repayment}$$ Its pointwise probability bound is <a href="#eq:repayment-outgoing-credit" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:repayment-outgoing-credit">[eq:repayment-outgoing-credit]</a>. In the elongated case the continued aperture normal is within $C\epsilon^h$ of $n(P)$. The returned score satisfies <a href="#eq:repayment-earlier-scores" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:repayment-earlier-scores">[eq:repayment-earlier-scores]</a> in that case and <a href="#eq:repayment-isotropic-score" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:repayment-isotropic-score">[eq:repayment-isotropic-score]</a> in the isotropic case. All these bounds are finite at fixed $\epsilon$.
  - Explanation: A prepared cut converts near-maximal endpoint growth into increased fine-velocity credit, bounded by the layer capacity.
- **claim-strip-cell-packet-coherence** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-packet-coherence)): Use local coordinates with root time $r$, endpoint duration $2h$, and put $$\rho=\epsilon^u,\qquad s=\epsilon^{u+h},\qquad \sigma=\epsilon^{u+2h}=s^2/\rho,\qquad \lambda_{\rm loc}=s^{-2}.$$ Fixed multiplicative errors in these relations change only constants. Let $P$ be a buffered isotropic cell of width $\rho$. Let $Q$ specify $P,C_t$ and a position cell of side $s$ at $C_t$. Candidate atoms have this $P$, velocity spacing $s$, earlier position spacing $s$, and transported position within $Rs$ of that cell, where $R=\epsilon^{-\theta}$. Let $N_Q$ be their number, and suppose $$\|c_T\|^2\leq\epsilon^{-\xi}m.$$ Partition their velocities into $K\leq\epsilon^{-k-\xi}$ bins of width $s$, in a fixed normal direction for $d=1$ or in both directions for $d=2$. Let $Z$ add to $Q$ the output position at precision $\sigma$ in those $d$ directions. Let $m_Z$ be the sum of squared packet tests over all output sites mapping to $Z$, on the input truncated to these candidates. Then $$\sum_{Z\mid Q}m_Z\leq C\epsilon^{-\xi}N_Qm,\qquad m_Z\leq C\epsilon^{dh-k-2\theta-2\xi}N_Qm. \label{eq:finite-coherence}$$ The constant is uniform over all admissible choices of the site-dependent amplitudes. Without candidate truncation, the square root of the mass estimate has the additive tail error provided by Lemma <a href="#lem:packet-decomposition" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:packet-decomposition">37</a>.
  - Explanation: Candidate truncation and velocity bins give both aggregate and pointwise coherent mass bounds for strips and cells.
- **claim-oscillatory-integral-estimate** (bound, [source](#stmt-thm-oscillatory-estimate)): Fix bounded input and output regions $K_v,K_x\subset\mathbb R^2$. For the input patch $K_v$, fix a class of smooth real phases satisfying the phase assumptions of Section <a href="#sec:packet-structure" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:packet-structure">9</a>, with common domain $[0,1]\times\mathbb R^2\times U_v$, where $U_v$ is an open neighborhood of $K_v$. All enlarged patches required by the decomposition, expressed in the original $v$ coordinates, are contained in $U_v$ and obey common bounds. The translated systems are considered on the corresponding bounded rescaled patches described in that section, with the resulting uniform bounds. Throughout the phase domain, $$\partial_v\Phi(c,x,v)=\zeta(v,x-cv).$$ For each phase and each required original input patch $V$, the matrix $\partial_p\zeta$ is symmetric and satisfies either $$a_0I\le\partial_p\zeta(v,p)\le a_1I \qquad(v\in V,\ p\in\mathbb R^2),$$ or the same inequality with $-\partial_p\zeta$ in place of $\partial_p\zeta$, with common constants $a_0>0$ and $a_1$ for the class. On these original patches, every mixed $v,p$ derivative of total order $j$ of this matrix is bounded by $A^{j+1}(j!)^3$ for a common $A\ge1$. Fix these constants and all the seminorm bounds of a class of smooth amplitudes $B$ supported in $[0,1]\times K_x\times K_v$. For every $\nu>0$ there is a constant $C_\nu$, depending only on these fixed data and $\nu$, such that, for every $\lambda\ge2$, every phase and amplitude in the specified classes, and every $f\in L^3(\mathbb R^2)$ supported in $K_v$, $$\label{eq:oscillatory-estimate} \left\\|E_\lambda f\right\\|_{L^3([0,1]\times K_x)} \le C_\nu\lambda^{-1+\nu}\\|f\\|_3, \qquad E_\lambda f(c,x)=\int e^{i\lambda\Phi(c,x,v)}B(c,x,v)f(v)\,dv.$$
  - Explanation: Packet growth yields the stated oscillatory integral estimate with arbitrarily small positive power loss for a fixed uniform phase and amplitude class.
- **claim-radial-kernel-expansion** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-br-kernel)): The kernel is bounded on $\mathbb R^3$. For $R\ge1$ it has an expansion $$\label{eq:br-kernel-symbol} K_\delta(Re_3)=e^{2\pi iR}b_+(R)+e^{-2\pi iR}b_-(R), \qquad \|b_\pm^{(j)}(R)\|\le C_{\delta,j}R^{-2-\delta-j} \quad(j\ge0).$$ In particular $K_\delta\in L^1(\mathbb R^3)$ whenever $\delta>1$.
  - Explanation: The radial kernel has oscillatory endpoint symbols with derivative decay and becomes integrable in the stated order regime.
- **claim-complex-order-transfer** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-br-complex-order)): For $\Re z>0$ and $R>0$, let $T_{z,R}$ have multiplier $(1-\|\xi\|^2/R^2)_+^z$, and write $T_z=T_{z,1}$. Suppose $r>0$ and $T_r$ is bounded on $L^q$ for $1\le q<\infty$. If $a>r$ and $N$ is an integer with $N>r+1$, then $$\label{eq:br-complex-bound} \\|T_{a+i\tau}\\|_{q\to q} \le \\|T_r\\|_{q\to q} \prod_{k=0}^{N-1}\left(1+\frac{\tau^2}{(a-r+k)^2}\right)^{1/2}.$$ The same conclusion holds for $q=\infty$ if $K_r\in L^1$.
  - Explanation: A beta-integral mixture transfers real-order boundedness to complex orders with an explicit polynomial growth factor.
- **claim-full-strict-multiplier-range** (theorem, [source](#stmt-cor-full-bochner-riesz)): Let $1\le p\le\infty$ and $$\label{eq:full-br-range} \delta>\max\left\{0,\,3\left\|\frac1p-\frac12\right\|-\frac12\right\}.$$ Then the multiplier $(1-\|\xi\|^2)_+^\delta$ is bounded on $L^p(\mathbb R^3)$. The same bounds hold uniformly for every positive radius after dilation. This assertion concerns the strict inequality <a href="#eq:full-br-range" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:full-br-range">[eq:full-br-range]</a>.
  - Explanation: Analytic interpolation, real interpolation, duality, and integrable kernels establish the full strict smoothing range uniformly over positive radii.

For arbitrary $B,D$, $$\\begin{aligned}\n \\mathsf H_{\\mathrm{nat}}^{\\mathsf Q}(D\\mid B)\n &=\\mathbb E_{\\mathsf Q}[-\\log\\mathsf P(D\\mid B)]\n   -\\mathbb E_{\\mathsf Q_B}\n     \\mathop{\\mathrm{KL}}(\\mathsf Q_{D\\mid B}\\Vert\\mathsf P_{D\\mid B}),\\label{eq:conditional-kl}\\\\\n \\mathbb E_{\\mathsf Q_B}\n     \\mathop{\\mathrm{KL}}(\\mathsf Q_{D\\mid B}\\Vert\\mathsf P_{D\\mid B})\n &\\le\\log K.\\label{eq:conditional-kl-bound}\n\\end{aligned}$$ In particular, restriction to an event of $\\mathsf P$-mass $m>0$ costs at most $\\log(1/m)$ in <a href=\"#eq:conditional-kl-bound\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"eq:conditional-kl-bound\">[eq:conditional-kl-bound]</a>.         "exact_quote": "Let $\\mathsf U,\\mathsf V$ be probability laws on the same finite space with $\\mathsf U\\le A\\mathsf V$, $A\\ge1$, and let $C$ be a finite observation. For $0<\\eta<1$, $$\\mathsf U_C\\{c:\\mathsf U_C(c)<\\eta\\mathsf V_C(c)\\}\\le\\eta.\n \\label{eq:conditioning-likelihood}$$ At every other $\\mathsf U_C$-positive value, $$\\mathsf U(\\,\\cdot\\mid C=c)\n \\le \\frac A\\eta\\,\\mathsf V(\\,\\cdot\\mid C=c).$$ The estimate is independent of the number of values of $C$.*\n\n\n*In particular, let $\\mathsf P$ be a finite law, let $\\mathcal E$ have mass $m=\\mathsf P(\\mathcal E)>0$, and put $\\mathsf U=\\mathsf P(\\,\\cdot\\mid\\mathcal E)$ and $r_C(c)=\\mathsf P(\\mathcal E\\mid C=c)$. Then $$\\begin{gathered}\n \\mathsf U_C(c)=\\frac{\\mathsf P_C(c)r_C(c)}m,\\qquad\n \\mathsf U_C\\{r_C<t\\}\\le\\frac tm\\quad(t>0),\\\\\n \\mathsf U(\\,\\cdot\\mid C=c)\n \\le r_C(c)^{-1}\\mathsf P(\\,\\cdot\\mid C=c).\n \\end{gathered}\n \\label{eq:retention-fibers}$$ The last inequality is asserted on positive $\\mathsf U_C$ fibers. Thus for $0<\\eta_0<1$, outside $\\mathsf U_C$-mass $\\eta_0$, their domination constants are at most $(m\\eta_0)^{-1}$.*\n\n\n\n\n*Suppose further that $C$ is a function of a finite parent observation $X$, and write $r_X(x)=\\mathsf P(\\mathcal E\\mid X=x)$. On every positive $C=c$ fiber, for $0<\\eta_1<1$, $$\\mathsf U\\{r_X(X)<\\eta_1r_C(c)\\mid C=c\\}\\le\\eta_1.\n \\label{eq:nested-retention-fibers}$$ Removing these parent values does not change a conditional law given $X$. Let $d_-\\le d_+$ be real numbers. If a finite child $Y$ satisfies, on every $(X,Y)$ value attained in $\\mathcal E$, $$d_-\\le-\\ell^{-1}\\log\\mathsf P(Y\\mid X)\\le d_+,\n \\qquad \\ell=\\log(1/\\epsilon),$$ then there are at most $\\epsilon^{-d_+}$ retained children over each parent, and, with $\\mathsf U_c=\\mathsf U(\\,\\cdot\\mid C=c)$, $$d_- -\\frac{\\log(1/r_C(c))}{\\ell}\n \\le \\mathsf H^{\\mathsf U_c}(Y\\mid X)\\le d_+.\n \\label{eq:typical-cell-entropy}$$ More precisely, outside $\\mathsf U_c$-mass at most $\\eta_1+\\eta_2$, $$d_- -\\frac{\\log(1/(\\eta_1r_C(c)))}{\\ell}\n \\le-\\ell^{-1}\\log\\mathsf U_c(Y\\mid X)\n \\le d_+ +\\frac{\\log(1/\\eta_2)}{\\ell},\n \\qquad 0<\\eta_2<1.\n \\label{eq:typical-cell-surprise}$$ These conclusions concern the retained support and sampled conditional values. They assert no lower mass bound for every untrimmed child.",

        "anchor": "stmt-lem-entropy-splitting",
        "exact_quote": "For any finite tag $Q$, $$\\begin{aligned}\n 0\\le\\mathsf H_{\\mathrm{nat}}(D\\mid B)-\\mathsf H_{\\mathrm{nat}}(D\\mid B,Q)&\\le\\mathsf H_{\\mathrm{nat}}(Q),\\\\\n |\\mathsf I_{\\mathrm{nat}}(T;D\\mid Q)-\\mathsf I_{\\mathrm{nat}}(T;D)|&\\le\\mathsf H_{\\mathrm{nat}}(Q),\\\\\n \\mathsf I_{\\mathrm{nat}}(U;V\\mid Z,Q)&\\le\\mathsf I_{\\mathrm{nat}}(U;V\\mid Z)+\\mathsf H_{\\mathrm{nat}}(Q).\n\\end{aligned}$$ The conditional quantities on the left are averages of the quantities on the individual tag fibers. If $U,V$ are conditionally independent given $Z$ under $\\mathsf P$, and $\\mathsf R\\le K\\mathsf P$, then $$\\mathsf I_{\\mathrm{nat}}^{\\mathsf R}(U;V\\mid Z)\\le\\log K.$$ Given a joint law of $(T,C,V)$ and a kernel $\\kappa(u\\mid T,C)$, one may adjoin $U$ by this kernel while preserving that entire joint law. The new $U$ is conditionally independent of $V$ given $(T,C)$, and its joint law with $(T,C)$ is the prescribed kernel law.",

      "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-lem-homogenization",
        "exact_quote": "Fix a law $\\mathsf P$, a finite list $(X_j,Y_j)$, $1\\le j\\le q$, and numbers $A_j\\ge0$ such that $|\\mathcal Y_j|\\le\\epsilon^{-A_j}$. There is no cardinality assumption on $X_j$. For $a,\\sigma,\\theta>0$, there are disjoint events $E_z$ whose union has probability at least $1-q\\epsilon^\\sigma-\\theta$, with the following properties. The number of events is at most $$J=\\prod_{j=1}^q\\left(1+\\left\\lceil\\frac{A_j+\\sigma}{a}\\right\\rceil\\right),\n \\qquad m_z:=\\mathsf P(E_z)\\ge\\theta/J.$$ For each $z,j$ there is $d_{j,z}\\in[0,A_j+\\sigma]$ such that, on $E_z$, $$d_{j,z}\\le -\\ell^{-1}\\log\\mathsf P(Y_j\\mid X_j)\n \\le d_{j,z}+a.\n \\label{eq:homogeneous-bin}$$ If $\\mathsf R$ is any law supported on $E_z$ satisfying $\\mathsf R\\le K\\mathsf P(\\,\\cdot\\mid E_z)$, then $$d_{j,z}-\\frac{\\log(K/m_z)}\\ell\n \\le\\mathsf H_{\\mathsf R}(Y_j\\mid X_j)\\le d_{j,z}+a.\n \\label{eq:homogeneous-entropy}$$ More precisely, for every $0<\\eta<1$, outside a set of $\\mathsf R$-probability at most $2\\eta$, $$d_{j,z}-\\frac{\\log(K/(m_z\\eta))}\\ell\n \\le-\\ell^{-1}\\log\\mathsf R(Y_j\\mid X_j)\n \\le d_{j,z}+a+\\frac{\\log(1/\\eta)}\\ell.\n \\label{eq:homogeneous-surprise}$$ There are at most $\\epsilon^{-(d_{j,z}+a)}$ retained $Y_j$ values over each fixed $X_j$ value. The support-count assertion and <a href=\"#eq:homogeneous-bin\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"eq:homogeneous-bin\">[eq:homogeneous-bin]</a> are uniform on the retained support, before any further restriction is chosen.",

        "exact_quote": "Let $\\pi$ be a law and let $\\Lambda$ be a comparison probability law with $\\pi\\ll\\Lambda$. Write $L=d\\pi/d\\Lambda$ and $D=\\mathop{\\mathrm{KL}}(\\pi\\Vert\\Lambda)$.       "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-thm-finite-conditioning",
        "exact_quote": "Let $\\pi(p,b)$ be a probability law with $\\mu=\\pi_P$, $\\lambda=\\pi_B$. Let $E$ be an allowed set with $\\pi(E)\\ge1-\\zeta$ and suppose $$\\boldsymbol1_E(p,b)\\pi(p,b)\\le K\\mu(p)\\lambda(b),\\qquad K\\ge1.\n \\label{eq:pair-product}$$ Choose $0<\\alpha<1$ with $\\zeta<1-\\alpha$, retain only point fibers with $r(p):=\\pi(E\\mid P=p)\\ge\\alpha$, and normalize the pairs in these fibers and in $E$ to a law $q$. Its retained mass $M_0$ satisfies $$M_0\\ge1-\\frac{\\zeta}{1-\\alpha},\\qquad\n q(p,b)\\le M_0^{-1}\\pi(p,b),\\qquad\n q(b\\mid p)\\le c\\lambda(b),\\quad c:=K/\\alpha.\n \\label{eq:star-kernel}$$ For a fixed integer $n\\ge1$, sample $B_1,\\ldots,B_n$ independently given $P$ with kernel $q(b\\mid p)$, and let $$S(p,b_1,\\ldots,b_n)=q_P(p)\\prod_{i=1}^nq(b_i\\mid p).$$ The following are comparison probability laws on the whole star: $$\\begin{aligned}\n \\Lambda_0&=q_P\\otimes\\lambda^{\\otimes n},\n &S&\\le c^n\\Lambda_0,\\label{eq:star-independent}\\\\\n \\Lambda_i&=q_{P,B_i}\\otimes\\bigotimes_{j\\ne i}\\lambda_{B_j},\n &S&\\le c^{n-1}\\Lambda_i\\quad(1\\le i\\le n).\n \\label{eq:star-pair}\n\\end{aligned}$$ Here $q_{P,B_i}$ is a copy of the retained pair law $q$. It may be replaced by the original $\\pi$ in <a href=\"#eq:star-pair\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"eq:star-pair\">[eq:star-pair]</a> at the additional cost $M_0^{-1}$.*\n\n\n\n\n\n\n*Let $R=wS/m$, where $0\\le w\\le1$ and $m=\\mathbb E_Sw>0$. Fix an index set $J\\subset\\{1,\\ldots,n\\}$ of *fixed labels*; write $F=\\{1,\\ldots,n\\}\\setminus J$ for the *free labels*. Choose any observation $$C=(B_J,Z),\\qquad Z=f(P,B_J).$$ Thus the function defining $Z$ involves the point and the fixed labels only. For every $0<\\eta<1/(n+1)$, there is a set of $C$ values of $R_C$-mass at least $1-(n+1)\\eta$ on which, simultaneously, $$\\begin{aligned}\n R(\\,\\cdot\\mid C)&\\le\\frac{c^n}{m\\eta}\\Lambda_0(\\,\\cdot\\mid C),\n \\label{eq:conditional-independent}\\\\\n R(\\,\\cdot\\mid C)&\\le\\frac{c^{n-1}}{m\\eta}\n                 \\Lambda_i(\\,\\cdot\\mid C),\\quad1\\le i\\le n.\n \\label{eq:conditional-pair}\n\\end{aligned}$$ For a fixed value $C=(b_J,z)$, put $z_{b_J}(p)=f(p,b_J)$. Ignoring the deterministic coordinates $B_J$, these comparison laws are exactly $$\\begin{aligned}\n \\Lambda_0(\\,\\cdot\\mid b_J,z)\n &=q_P(\\,\\cdot\\mid z_{b_J}(P)=z)\n                            \\otimes\\bigotimes_{j\\in F}\\lambda_{B_j},\n \\label{eq:fixed-comparison-zero}\\\\\n \\Lambda_i(\\,\\cdot\\mid b_J,z)\n &=q_P(\\,\\cdot\\mid B_i=b_i,z_{b_J}(P)=z)\n                            \\otimes\\bigotimes_{j\\in F}\\lambda_{B_j},\n                  &&i\\in J,\\label{eq:fixed-comparison-pair}\\\\\n \\Lambda_i(\\,\\cdot\\mid b_J,z)\n &=q_{P,B_i}(\\,\\cdot\\mid z_{b_J}(P)=z)\n                       \\otimes\\bigotimes_{j\\in F\\setminus\\{i\\}}\\lambda_{B_j},\n                  &&i\\in F.\\label{eq:free-comparison-pair}\n\\end{aligned}$$ Conditionals in this display need only be defined when their conditioning event has positive comparison mass; the inequalities hold at every $R$-positive value under consideration.*\n\n\n*There is also a direct comparison using the actual point marginal. There is a set $G$ of $(P,C)$ values with $R(G)\\ge1-\\eta$ such that, for every $C$ value, as an inequality of subprobabilities, $$\\boldsymbol1_G(p,C)R(p,b_F\\mid C)\n \\le\\frac{c^{|F|}}{m\\eta}R_P(p\\mid C)\n                             \\prod_{j\\in F}\\lambda(b_j).\n \\label{eq:actual-point-free}$$ For $0<\\tau<1$, outside $C$ values of $R_C$-mass at most $\\eta/\\tau$, the subprobability on the left has mass at least $1-\\tau$. In any of these conditionals, all applicable product comparisons, including product comparisons for coordinate tuples at several fixed labels, may be converted *simultaneously* to comparisons using their actual retained marginals by Lemma <a href=\"#lem:marginal-core\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"lem:marginal-core\">7</a>. If the subprobability after all prior trims, including intersection with $G$ when used, has conditional mass $u$ and the resulting list has $N_{\\mathrm{fac}}$ factor occurrences, its core has conditional mass at least $u/2$ and each $k$-factor comparison constant $A$ becomes at most $A(2N_{\\mathrm{fac}}/u)^k$. All exceptional-mass and domination estimates above are independent of the number of possible values of $C$, $P$, and the labels.",
