Ignoring the deterministic coordinates $B_J$, these comparison laws are exactly $$\\begin{aligned}\n \\Lambda_0(\\,\\cdot\\mid b_J,z)\n &=q_P(\\,\\cdot\\mid z_{b_J}(P)=z)\n                            \\otimes\\bigotimes_{j\\in F}\\lambda_{B_j},\n \\label{eq:fixed-comparison-zero}\\\\\n \\Lambda_i(\\,\\cdot\\mid b_J,z)\n &=q_P(\\,\\cdot\\mid B_i=b_i,z_{b_J}(P)=z)\n                            \\otimes\\bigotimes_{j\\in F}\\lambda_{B_j},\n                  &&i\\in J,\\label{eq:fixed-comparison-pair}\\\\\n \\Lambda_i(\\,\\cdot\\mid b_J,z)\n &=q_{P,B_i}(\\,\\cdot\\mid z_{b_J}(P)=z)\n                       \\otimes\\bigotimes_{j\\in F\\setminus\\{i\\}}\\lambda_{B_j},\n                  &&i\\in F.\\label{eq:free-comparison-pair}\n\\end{aligned}$$ Conditionals in this display need only be defined when their conditioning event has positive comparison mass; the inequalities hold at every $R$-positive value under consideration.*\n\n\n*There is also a direct comparison using the actual point marginal. There is a set $G$ of $(P,C)$ values with $R(G)\\ge1-\\eta$ such that, for every $C$ value, as an inequality of subprobabilities, $$\\boldsymbol1_G(p,C)R(p,b_F\\mid C)\n \\le\\frac{c^{|F|}}{m\\eta}R_P(p\\mid C)\n                             \\prod_{j\\in F}\\lambda(b_j).\n \\label{eq:actual-point-free}$$ For $0<\\tau<1$, outside $C$ values of $R_C$-mass at most $\\eta/\\tau$, the subprobability on the left has mass at least $1-\\tau$. In any of these conditionals, all applicable product comparisons, including product comparisons for coordinate tuples at several fixed labels, may be converted *simultaneously* to comparisons using their actual retained marginals by Lemma <a href=\"#lem:marginal-core\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"lem:marginal-core\">7</a>. If the subprobability after all prior trims, including intersection with $G$ when used, has conditional mass $u$ and the resulting list has $N_{\\mathrm{fac}}$ factor occurrences, its core has conditional mass at least $u/2$ and each $k$-factor comparison constant $A$ becomes at most $A(2N_{\\mathrm{fac}}/u)^k$.         "anchor": "stmt-lem-profile-diagonal",
        "exact_quote": "The following three statements hold.*\n\n1.  *Suppose for each $\\epsilon\\to0$ there is a countable list $(X_j,Y_j)_{j\\ge1}$, with $|\\mathcal Y_j|\\le\\epsilon^{-A_j}$ for each fixed $j$. One can partition all but $o(1)$ of the law into $\\epsilon^{-o(1)}$ parts, each of mass at least $\\epsilon^{o(1)}$, such that the following holds. From any choice of one retained part at each scale, a subsequence can be extracted on which every listed observation is homogeneous. The same exponents are inherited by every sequence of laws supported on those parts whose density relative to their normalized laws is at most $\\epsilon^{-o(1)}$. The assertion is simultaneous for joint observations and observations conditional on an exact particle index, when these are included in the list.*\n\n2.  *Let $v$ range over a compact rectangle of depth parameters. Suppose observations $Y_v$, conditional on any $X$, obey, uniformly for fixed $u,v$, the two ambiguity bounds $$\\log N(Y_v\\mid Y_u,X),\\ \\log N(Y_u\\mid Y_v,X)\n           \\le C\\ell\\|u-v\\|_1+o(\\ell),$$ and have bounded normalized alphabet sizes at one reference depth. Their normalized entropy profiles have subsequences converging on all depths to a $C$-Lipschitz function, after extraction on a countable dense set. Homogeneous surprise exponents on that dense set extend to the same function at every fixed depth, provided the ambiguity bounds also hold on the retained support.*\n\n3.  *Suppose a finite construction at each fixed $h>0$ has finitely many normalized errors tending to zero as $\\epsilon\\to0$. Given any sequence of permissible $h_k\\downarrow0$, and any countable sequence of such requirements, a diagonal can be chosen so that the first $k$ requirements have errors at most $h_k/k$ and $h_k\\log(1/\\epsilon_k)\\to\\infty$. Thus errors may be made $o(h)$ before passing to the scale $\\epsilon^h$. This assertion supplies no rate uniform in $h$ or in the limiting profile.",

      },

        "exact_quote": "Fix $0<s\\le1$, $0<d\\le2$, and $\\alpha>0$. There are $\\eta_0=\\eta_0(\\alpha,s,d)>0$ and $\\rho_0=\\rho_0(\\alpha,s,d)>0$ with the following property.         "exact_quote": "Fix $0<d\\le2$, $0<s\\le1$, and $\\alpha>0$, and fixed bounded point and slope domains.       "conclusion": {

        "anchor": "stmt-lem-isotropic-intercepts",
        "exact_quote": "Suppose an incidence population uses at most $N$ point cells. For every retained exact particle and slope bin incident to it, suppose there are at least $m$ distinct retained time children in the same base cell and slope bin. Suppose further that these children lie on one line of true slope within $O(\\rho)$ of the bin representative. Then, for each slope bin, all its retained incidences use at most $CN/m$ intercept cells of side $\\rho$.",

        "anchor": "stmt-lem-isotropic-grid-projections",
        "exact_quote": "Let $E$ be a set of occupied $\\rho$-cells in a fixed bounded region.*\n\n\n1.  *In $\\mathbb R^3$, let $v_1,v_2,v_3\\in\\mathbb R^2$ be bounded slopes and put $D=\\abs{\\det((1,v_1),(1,v_2),(1,v_3))}>0$. If $\\pi_{v_i}(E)$ uses at most $N_i$ cells, with bounded enlargements permitted, then $$\\abs E^2\\leq C D^{-6}N_1N_2N_3.\n     \\label{eq:isotropic-lw}$$*\n\n\n2.  *In $\\mathbb R^2$, for two bounded scalar slopes $v_1,v_2$ with $\\abs{v_1-v_2}\\geq\\rho^a$, if their intercepts use at most $N_1,N_2$ cells, then $$\\abs E\\leq C\\rho^{-2a}N_1N_2.\n     \\label{eq:isotropic-two-projections}$$",

        "anchor": "stmt-thm-characteristic-trace",
        "exact_quote": "Suppose $f$ is locally Lipschitz on $\\mathcal D$, and, in its interior, $$0\\le f_j\\le d_j,\\qquad 0\\le f_v\\le d_v,\n \\qquad f_{jk}\\le0\\ (j\\ne k),\\qquad f_{jv}\\le0$$ in the distributional sense. The derivative bounds may instead be local bounds on each compact neighborhood under consideration; in that case all conclusions concerning boundedness are local. Then there are, up to null sets, uniquely determined locally bounded fields $a_1,\\ldots,a_n,D$ on $\\mathbb R\\times I$, with $0\\le a_j\\le d_j$ and $0\\le D\\le d_v$, having the following properties.*\n\n\n1.  **Strong traces.* For almost every interior offset $\\eta\\in\\mathcal K^\\circ$, the restrictions of the ambient gradients to $\\Pi(\\cdot)+\\eta$ are defined almost everywhere. As $\\eta\\to0$ through such offsets, they converge strongly in $L^1_{\\rm loc}(di\\,du)$ to $(a_1,\\ldots,a_n,D)$. For $Q\\Subset Q'\\Subset\\mathbb R\\times I$ this convergence has the bound $$\\label{eq:trace-quantitative-slices}\n     \\|f_\\alpha(\\Pi(\\cdot)+\\eta)-A_\\alpha\\|_{L^1(Q)}\n     \\le C_Q|\\eta|+\\omega_{\\alpha,Q'}(C_Q|\\eta|),\n     \\qquad A=(a_1,\\ldots,a_n,D),$$ where $\\omega_{\\alpha,Q'}(r)\\to0$ is the $L^1$ translation modulus of $A_\\alpha$ on $Q'$. The constant depends only on the local derivative bounds, the clock speeds, and the two patches.*\n\n\n\n\n\n2.  **Measure identities.* There exist locally finite nonnegative measures $\\nu_{jk}=\\nu_{kj}$, $j\\ne k$, and $\\nu_{jv}$ on the plane such that $$\\label{eq:trace-mixed-measures}\n     V_j a_j=-\\nu_{jv}-\\sum_{k\\ne j}(c_k-c_j)\\nu_{jk},\n     \\qquad \\partial_iD=-\\sum_j\\nu_{jv}.$$ For $F=f\\circ\\Pi$, the weak derivatives are $$\\label{eq:trace-plane-derivatives}\n     F_i=\\sum_j a_j,\\qquad F_u=\\sum_j c_ja_j+D.$$ In particular, $$\\label{eq:trace-distribution-inequality}\n     V_n a_n\\ge\\partial_iD$$ as measures. With $q_j=1+c_n-c_j$, the full flux identity is $$\\label{eq:trace-measure-flux}\n     -\\sum_jq_jV_ja_j\n     =\\sum_{j<k}(c_k-c_j)^2\\nu_{jk}+\\sum_jq_j\\nu_{jv}.$$*\n\n\n3.  **Affine approximation.* There is a sequence $h_\\ell\\downarrow0$ and a single null set $N\\subset\\mathbb R\\times I$ such that, for every $(i,u)\\notin N$ and every finite $R$, $$\\label{eq:trace-affine-blowup}\n     \\lim_{\\ell\\to\\infty}\\sup_{\\xi\\in\\mathcal K,\\ |\\xi|\\le R}\n     \\left|\n     \\frac{f(\\Pi(i,u)+h_\\ell\\xi)-f(\\Pi(i,u))}{h_\\ell}\n          -\\sum_j a_j(i,u)\\xi_j-D(i,u)\\xi_v\n     \\right|=0.$$ Only sufficiently large $\\ell$, for which the displayed label times belong to $I$, are used. The sequence may depend on $f$.",
        "source_id": "PM-078.1"
      },

      "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-cor-finite-characteristic-trace",
        "exact_quote": "Assume Theorem <a href=\"#thm:characteristic-trace\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"thm:characteristic-trace\">26</a>, and let $f_\\epsilon\\to f$ locally uniformly on $\\mathcal D$ along the sequence of finite systems under consideration. Fix a bounded measurable base patch $Q$ of positive measure with compact closure in $\\mathbb R\\times I$, a radius $R\\ge1$, an error $\\eta>0$, an exceptional proportion $0<\\tau<1$, and a maximum block length $h_*>0$. There exist $$0<h<h_*,\\qquad G\\subset Q,\\qquad |Q\\setminus G|\\le\\tau|Q|,$$ and a compact neighborhood $K_0\\subset\\mathcal D$ containing all $\\Pi(q)+h\\xi$ with $q\\in\\overline Q$, $\\xi\\in\\mathcal K\\cap B_R$, such that the following holds. If $$\\label{eq:trace-finite-tolerance}\n \\|f_\\epsilon-f\\|_{L^\\infty(K_0)}\\le\\eta h/4,$$ then, simultaneously for every $q\\in G$ and every $\\xi\\in\\mathcal K\\cap B_R$, $$\\label{eq:trace-finite-affine}\n |f_\\epsilon(\\Pi(q)+h\\xi)-f_\\epsilon(\\Pi(q))-hA(q)\\cdot\\xi|\n \\le\\eta h.$$ In particular, for every finite family of such displacements, every information increment between two of them differs from its affine value by at most $2\\eta h$. An alternating sum of $r$ profile values whose affine contributions cancel has absolute value at most $r\\eta h$.*\n\n*All dependencies have the order $$f,\\ Q,R,\\eta,\\tau,h_*\\quad\\longrightarrow\\quad h,G,K_0\n \\quad\\longrightarrow\\quad\\epsilon_0.$$ For every member of the converging finite sequence with $\\epsilon<\\epsilon_0$, <a href=\"#eq:trace-finite-tolerance\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"eq:trace-finite-tolerance\">[eq:trace-finite-tolerance]</a> holds. If finitely many entropy identities also incur a total normalized ambiguity error at most $B/\\log(1/\\epsilon)$, one may, after choosing $h$, require in addition $$\\log(1/\\epsilon)\\ge B/(\\eta h).$$ Each such combined identity then has at most one additional $\\eta h$ of error. More generally one may prescribe any sequences $\\eta_\\ell,\\tau_\\ell\\downarrow0$ and $h_{*,\\ell}\\downarrow0$ and select successively $h_\\ell<h_{*,\\ell}$, then the inner approximation thresholds. If $\\sum_\\ell\\tau_\\ell<\\infty$, almost every point of $Q$ belongs to all but finitely many of the resulting $G_\\ell$.",

      "exact_statement": "Assume Theorem <a href=\"#thm:characteristic-trace\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"thm:characteristic-trace\">26</a>, and let $f_\\epsilon\\to f$ locally uniformly on $\\mathcal D$ along the sequence of finite systems under consideration. Fix a bounded measurable base patch $Q$ of positive measure with compact closure in $\\mathbb R\\times I$, a radius $R\\ge1$, an error $\\eta>0$, an exceptional proportion $0<\\tau<1$, and a maximum block length $h_*>0$. There exist $$0<h<h_*,\\qquad G\\subset Q,\\qquad |Q\\setminus G|\\le\\tau|Q|,$$ and a compact neighborhood $K_0\\subset\\mathcal D$ containing all $\\Pi(q)+h\\xi$ with $q\\in\\overline Q$, $\\xi\\in\\mathcal K\\cap B_R$, such that the following holds. If $$\\label{eq:trace-finite-tolerance}\n \\|f_\\epsilon-f\\|_{L^\\infty(K_0)}\\le\\eta h/4,$$ then, simultaneously for every $q\\in G$ and every $\\xi\\in\\mathcal K\\cap B_R$, $$\\label{eq:trace-finite-affine}\n |f_\\epsilon(\\Pi(q)+h\\xi)-f_\\epsilon(\\Pi(q))-hA(q)\\cdot\\xi|\n \\le\\eta h.$$ In particular, for every finite family of such displacements, every information increment between two of them differs from its affine value by at most $2\\eta h$. An alternating sum of $r$ profile values whose affine contributions cancel has absolute value at most $r\\eta h$.*\n\n*All dependencies have the order $$f,\\ Q,R,\\eta,\\tau,h_*\\quad\\longrightarrow\\quad h,G,K_0\n \\quad\\longrightarrow\\quad\\epsilon_0.$$ For every member of the converging finite sequence with $\\epsilon<\\epsilon_0$, <a href=\"#eq:trace-finite-tolerance\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"eq:trace-finite-tolerance\">[eq:trace-finite-tolerance]</a> holds. If finitely many entropy identities also incur a total normalized ambiguity error at most $B/\\log(1/\\epsilon)$, one may, after choosing $h$, require in addition $$\\log(1/\\epsilon)\\ge B/(\\eta h).$$ Each such combined identity then has at most one additional $\\eta h$ of error. More generally one may prescribe any sequences $\\eta_\\ell,\\tau_\\ell\\downarrow0$ and $h_{*,\\ell}\\downarrow0$ and select successively $h_\\ell<h_{*,\\ell}$, then the inner approximation thresholds. If $\\sum_\\ell\\tau_\\ell<\\infty$, almost every point of $Q$ belongs to all but finitely many of the resulting $G_\\ell$.",

        "anchor": "stmt-lem-curve-traces",
        "exact_quote": "Let $b$ be Lipschitz on an interval $J$, and let $\\Gamma=\\{(b(u),u):u\\in J\\}$ lie in an open plane region. Suppose bounded fields $a_j,D$ in this region satisfy $V_ja_j\\in\\mathcal M_{\\rm loc}$ and $\\partial_iD\\in\\mathcal M_{\\rm loc}$, where $\\mathcal M_{\\rm loc}$ denotes locally finite signed measures. Put $p(u)=-b'(u)$ at points where this derivative exists. For almost every $u\\in J$ the field $D$ has two strong traces $D^-,D^+$ and every $a_j$ with $c_j\\ne p(u)$ has two strong traces $a_j^-,a_j^+$. Specifically, at $q_0=(b(u_0),u_0)$ the mean of $|a_j-a_j^\\pm(u_0)|$ tends to zero on the corresponding tangent half-ball $$B_\\rho(q_0)\\cap\n \\{\\ \\pm(i-b(u_0)+p(u_0)(u-u_0))>0\\ \\},\n \\qquad\\rho\\downarrow0,$$ and likewise for $D$.         "exact_quote": "For almost every point $(i,u)$ of the characteristic plane with $i>0$ and $0<u<1$, put $s=S'(u)$.         "anchor": "stmt-lem-affine-block-core",
        "exact_quote": "Fix an integer $k\\ge1$. Let $p^0$ be a probability law on a finite pair space $\\mathcal P\\times\\Theta$. Write $\\mu^0=p^0_P$ and $\\lambda^0=p^0_\\theta$. Let $Q_j=Q_j(P,\\theta)$, $1\\le j\\le k$, be finite coordinate observations, and put $\\xi_j^\\theta=p^0_{Q_j\\mid\\theta}$ on positive label fibers, choosing an arbitrary probability law on a zero-mass label fiber. Define the two nonnegative natural-log quantities $$\\begin{aligned}\n D_{\\mathrm{pair}}\n &=\\mathop{\\mathrm{KL}}(p^0_{P,\\theta}\\Vert\\mu^0\\otimes\\lambda^0),\\\\\n D_{\\mathrm{coord}}\n &=\\mathop{\\mathrm{KL}}\\left(p^0_{\\theta,Q_1,\\ldots,Q_k}\n       \\middle\\Vert\n       \\lambda^0(\\theta)\\prod_{j=1}^k\\xi_j^\\theta(Q_j)\\right)\\\\\n &=\\sum_{j=1}^k\\mathsf H_{\\mathrm{nat}}^{p^0}(Q_j\\mid\\theta)\n       -\\mathsf H_{\\mathrm{nat}}^{p^0}(Q_1,\\ldots,Q_k\\mid\\theta).\n\\end{aligned}$$ The second quantity is averaged over the labels; no individual label is assumed to have small conditional multiinformation.*\n\n\n\n\n*Let $\\mathcal F$ be a finite list of observations on the pair space which contains $P$, $\\theta$, and every $(\\theta,Q_j)$. It may also contain any finite list of prefix and joint observations. Write $N=|\\mathcal F|$, counting occurrences rather than values. Let $\\mathcal H$ be an event of $p^0$-mass at least $1-\\zeta$, where $\\zeta\\ge0$. For $v>0$, choose $$0<\\underline M\n \\le1-\\zeta-\\frac{D_{\\mathrm{pair}}+D_{\\mathrm{coord}}+2/e}{v},\n \\qquad\n \\delta=\\frac{\\underline M}{2N}.$$ Then there is a restriction $r\\le\\boldsymbol1_{\\mathcal H}p^0$, of mass $M\\ge\\underline M/2$, such that, for every listed observation $F$ and every value with $r_F(f)>0$, $$\\delta p^0_F(f)\\le r_F(f)\\le p^0_F(f).\n \\label{eq:block-core-floors}$$ For the normalized law $\\pi=r/M$, write $\\mu=\\pi_P$ and $\\lambda=\\pi_\\theta$. Its pair law and its coordinate law on every positive label fiber satisfy $$\\begin{aligned}\n \\pi(P,\\theta)\n &\\le e^v M\\delta^{-2}\\mu(P)\\lambda(\\theta),\n \\label{eq:block-core-pair}\\\\\n \\pi(Q_1,\\ldots,Q_k\\mid\\theta)\n &\\le e^v\\delta^{-k}\n          \\prod_{j=1}^k\\pi(Q_j\\mid\\theta).\n \\label{eq:block-core-coordinate}\n\\end{aligned}$$ All factors on the right of these two inequalities are marginals of this same law $\\pi$.*\n\n\n*If $A,B$ are listed observations and $A$ is determined by $B$, then for every retained child value $b$, with parent $a=A(b)$, $$\\delta p^0(B=b\\mid A=a)\n \\le \\pi(B=b\\mid A=a)\n \\le\\delta^{-1}p^0(B=b\\mid A=a).\n \\label{eq:block-core-prefix-ratio}$$ The upper inequality can be summed over any set of child values. The lower inequality is asserted only for retained children. In particular, fix $0<\\rho<1$. If on $\\mathcal H$ the original conditional surprises for this pair lie in $[d_-,d_+]$ in units $L=\\log(1/\\rho)$, then every retained parent has at most $\\rho^{-d_+}$ retained children, and its retained conditional child masses obey $$\\delta\\rho^{d_+}\n \\le\\pi(B=b\\mid A=a)\\le\\delta^{-1}\\rho^{d_-}.$$ When a parent is nested only up to bounded ambiguity, include it in the child symbol before applying this assertion.",
        "source_id": "PM-078.1"
      },

        "exact_quote": "Let $0<s\\le1$.       "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-lem-packet-bessel",
        "exact_quote": "At a fixed time anchor, packets with natural spacings $\\rho$ in velocity and $\\sigma=(\\lambda\\rho)^{-1}$ in position satisfy $$\\sum_O m_O(f)\\le C\\|f\\|_2^2,\\qquad\n \\left\\|\\sum_T c_T g_T\\right\\|_2^2\\le C\\sum_T|c_T|^2,\n \\label{eq:packet-bessel}$$ where $g_T$ are the normalized synthesis packets with the opposite phase sign. These inequalities hold for subsets and for canonical supremum masses. Their constants depend only on ellipticity, finitely many phase and amplitude derivative bounds, support sizes, and lattice multiplicity, and not on the number of sites or on the position cutoff.*\n\n\n\n*More precisely, packets at this same time and scale obey, for every integer $M\\ge1$, $$|\\langle g_{V,X},g_{V',X'}\\rangle|\n \\le C_M\\mathbf 1_{\\{|V-V'|\\le C\\rho\\}}\n       \\left(1+\\frac{|X-X'|}{\\sigma}\\right)^{-M}.\n \\label{eq:packet-gram}$$ At a local root, where both natural spacings equal $s$, let $F$ be any allowed phase-space cap and let $F^R$ denote its enlargement by distance $Rs$ in each velocity and position coordinate, $R\\ge2$. For $h=\\sum_Tc_Tg_T$ and every integer $M>2$, canonical analysis gives $$\\sum_{O\\in F}m_O(h)\n \\le C\\sum_{T\\in F^R}|c_T|^2\n       +C_M R^{4-2M}\\sum_T|c_T|^2.\n \\label{eq:packet-cap-bessel}$$ Here a fixed enlargement of the support sizes is included in $F^R$. Every axis of $F$ is at least $s$; consequently $F^R$ is covered by at most $CR^4$ caps of the same widths.",
        "source_id": "PM-078.1"
      },
      "evidence": [
        {
          "anchor": "stmt-lem-packet-bessel",
          "exact_quote": "At a fixed time anchor, packets with natural spacings $\\rho$ in velocity and $\\sigma=(\\lambda\\rho)^{-1}$ in position satisfy $$\\sum_O m_O(f)\\le C\\|f\\|_2^2,\\qquad\n \\left\\|\\sum_T c_T g_T\\right\\|_2^2\\le C\\sum_T|c_T|^2,\n \\label{eq:packet-bessel}$$ where $g_T$ are the normalized synthesis packets with the opposite phase sign. These inequalities hold for subsets and for canonical supremum masses. Their constants depend only on ellipticity, finitely many phase and amplitude derivative bounds, support sizes, and lattice multiplicity, and not on the number of sites or on the position cutoff.*\n\n\n\n*More precisely, packets at this same time and scale obey, for every integer $M\\ge1$, $$|\\langle g_{V,X},g_{V',X'}\\rangle|\n \\le C_M\\mathbf 1_{\\{|V-V'|\\le C\\rho\\}}\n       \\left(1+\\frac{|X-X'|}{\\sigma}\\right)^{-M}.\n \\label{eq:packet-gram}$$ At a local root, where both natural spacings equal $s$, let $F$ be any allowed phase-space cap and let $F^R$ denote its enlargement by distance $Rs$ in each velocity and position coordinate, $R\\ge2$. For $h=\\sum_Tc_Tg_T$ and every integer $M>2$, canonical analysis gives $$\\sum_{O\\in F}m_O(h)\n \\le C\\sum_{T\\in F^R}|c_T|^2\n       +C_M R^{4-2M}\\sum_T|c_T|^2.\n \\label{eq:packet-cap-bessel}$$ Here a fixed enlargement of the support sizes is included in $F^R$.         "exact_quote": "Fix the data bounds, admissible depths, $r<t$, and $b_*\\le b$. Put $\\Delta=u_r-b_*$; then $\\Delta\\ge(t-r)/2>0$. For each localization $J_0$, there is a finite family of atoms $$g_T(v)=\\rho_r^{-1}\\eta_T((v-V_T)/\\rho_r)\n                     e^{-i\\lambda\\Phi(C_r,X_T,v)},\n \\qquad h_J=\\sum_Tc_Tg_T,\n \\label{eq:packet-earlier-atoms}$$ with $V_T$ within a fixed enlargement of its velocity cell and $|X_T-X_J|\\le C\\epsilon^{r+b_*}$. The amplitudes have uniform derivative bounds, the sites have bounded multiplicity, and $\\sum_T|c_T|^2\\le C\\|f\\|_2^2$. Each coefficient is an analysis test at time $r$. If $r=0$, then $$|c_T|^2\\le C_{\\rm can}m_T^{\\rm can}(f)\n \\label{eq:packet-coeff-canonical}$$ with a fixed constant.*\n\n*More quantitatively, choose $0<\\eta<\\Delta/4$ and any required power $A>0$. There are an integer integration order $M$, a coefficient cutoff exponent $B$, constants $C_A$, and $\\epsilon_0>0$, depending only on these choices and the fixed data, such that, for $0<\\epsilon<\\epsilon_0$:*\n\n1.  *Replacing $f$ by $h_J$ in every endpoint pairing belonging to $J_0$ changes it by at most $C_A\\epsilon^A\\|f\\|_2$. Coefficients with $|c_T|^2<\\epsilon^B\\|f\\|_2^2$ may be omitted with the same error.*\n\n\n2.  *An individual endpoint test interacts, up to such an error, only with overlapping velocity supports and atoms satisfying $$|V-V_T|\\le C\\rho_t,\\qquad\n     |X-X_T-(C_t-C_r)V_T|\\le C\\epsilon^{-\\eta}\\sigma_r.\n     \\label{eq:packet-transport}$$ This assertion also holds for any subset of the retained coefficients.*\n\n3.  *If one subsequently sums squared errors over at most $C\\epsilon^{-Q}$ tests, the orders can be chosen to give total squared error at most $C_A\\epsilon^{2A}\\|f\\|_2^2$.*\n\n\n*For example it suffices to choose $$M>4+\\frac{A+Q+4}{\\min(\\eta,\\Delta/2)},\\qquad\n B>2A+3Q+10.\n \\label{eq:packet-tail-orders}$$ Only finitely many derivatives, up to an order determined by $M$, are used. All constants are fixed before $\\epsilon$ tends to zero. The enlargement parameter $\\eta$ may tend to zero afterwards. After the finite family and its coefficient cutoff $B$ have been chosen, the integration order for the transport estimate in part 2 can be increased independently, without changing that family or $B$.",

        "exact_quote": "In a geometric localizer, bin nonnegligible coefficients so that $$|\\log_{1/\\epsilon}\\!\\left(|c_T|^2\\right)-\\log_{1/\\epsilon}\\!\\left(m\\right)|\\le\\xi\n \\label{eq:packet-mass-bin}$$ on each bin. Each bin admits a partition into classes, with a count parameter $g$ and fixed assigned-cap widths, having the following properties. If $N_{\\rm all}$ is the full class size, then for every allowed local root cap $F$, $$\\log_{1/\\epsilon}\\!\\left(\\#\\{T\\hbox{ in the class}:T\\in F\\}\\right)+w(F)\n \\le g+e_{\\rm pkt}.\n \\label{eq:packet-cap-count}$$ An empty count imposes no restriction. There is an assigned cap $E=E(T)$ whose nonempty fibers in the full class satisfy $$\\log_{1/\\epsilon}\\!\\left(\\#\\{T:E(T)=E\\}\\right)\n \\ge g-w(E)-e_{\\rm pkt}.\n \\label{eq:packet-assigned-fiber}$$ There are only a number of classes polynomial in $1+\\ell$, with constants depending on the fixed exponents and $\\xi$.         "anchor": "stmt-prop-finite-packet-composition",
        "exact_quote": "Fix $0\\le r<t$, a shape $0\\le b\\le a\\le\\min(L-t,u_t)$, and $0\\le b_*\\le b$. Choose $0<\\eta<(u_r-b_*)/4$, and make the decomposition and cap-class construction of Section <a href=\"#sec:packet-structure\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"sec:packet-structure\">9</a>, with the mass floor <a href=\"#eq:composition-mass-floor\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"eq:composition-mass-floor\">[eq:composition-mass-floor]</a>. Within the localizer $J$, including its auxiliary tags, let $N_{\\rm all}(J)$ be the size of the whole cap class, $N(J)>0$ its retained size, $m(J)$ its coefficient mass bin, and $g(J)$ its cap maximum bin. Set $$\\begin{aligned}\n A_J&=\\log_{1/\\epsilon}\\!\\left(N(J)\\right)+\\tfrac32\\log_{1/\\epsilon}\\!\\left(m(J)\\right)+\\tfrac12g(J),\n       \\label{eq:composition-A}\\\\\n K_r^*&=\\mathsf H(J)+b_*+\n       \\mathbb E\\left[\\log_{1/\\epsilon}\\!\\left(N_{\\rm all}(J)\\right)\n                    +\\tfrac32\\log_{1/\\epsilon}\\!\\left(m(J)\\right)+\\tfrac12g(J)\\right].\n       \\label{eq:composition-Kstar}\n\\end{aligned}$$ Let $K_J$ denote the canonical local root score, including its norm option, for the retained local superposition. Let $P_J$ be its score at duration $t-r$, with the conditional output law and the winning superposition masses. All expectations here use the current marginal of $J$ after the indicated preliminary split.*\n\n\n\n\n*With $\\mathcal R$ as in <a href=\"#eq:composition-error-budget\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"eq:composition-error-budget\">[eq:composition-error-budget]</a>, enlarged by a fixed constant if necessary, the following four quantities are nonnegative: $$\\begin{aligned}\n d_0&=K_0+\\beta_{\\mathrm q}r-K_r^*+2\\mathcal R,\\nonumber\\\\\n d_1(J)&=\\log_{1/\\epsilon}\\!\\left(N_{\\rm all}(J)/N(J)\\right),\\nonumber\\\\\n d_2(J)&=A_J-K_J+\\mathcal R,\\nonumber\\\\\n d_3(J)&=K_J+\\beta_{\\mathrm q}(t-r)-P_J+\\mathcal R.\n       \\label{eq:four-packet-deficits}\n\\end{aligned}$$ Up to the displayed error allowances, these are the deficits in growth before the cut, class retention, the local root comparison, and growth after the cut. The next inequality shows that saturation at the endpoint forces these four comparisons to be nearly sharp on average; the subsequent selection estimate specifies the branches on which this remains true. Writing $\\Delta_t=K_0+\\beta_{\\mathrm q}t-P_t$, one has the finite bound $$\\label{eq:finite-packet-deficits}\n d_0+\\mathbb E(d_1+d_2+d_3)\\le\\Delta_t+5\\mathcal R.$$ There is also an earlier test on the *retained uniform classes*, with that same current marginal of $J$ and the assigned cap labels, whose score satisfies $$\\label{eq:retained-back-score}\n P_r^{\\rm ret}\\ge K_r^*\n              -\\tfrac32\\mathbb Ed_1-\\mathcal R.$$ At $r=0$ this is an actual test for the original canonical $K_0$; the norm option is not used in this lower bound.*\n\n\n*More quantitatively, put $R_t=\\Delta_t+5\\mathcal R$. For an event $B$ measurable in $J$ with probability $p>0$ and any $\\theta>0$, $$\\label{eq:packet-typical-selection}\n \\mathbb P\\bigl(B\\cap\\{d_1+d_2+d_3>\\theta\\}\\bigr)\n       \\le R_t/\\theta.$$ In particular, taking $\\theta=2R_t/p$ leaves at least $p/2$ of the current probability in $B$, and bounds each of the three local deficits by $2R_t/p$. If $R_t=0$, all three vanish almost surely.",

      },

        "anchor": "stmt-lem-packet-boundary-slack",
        "exact_quote": "Assume Theorem <a href=\"#thm:classical-growth\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"thm:classical-growth\">15</a> and $\\beta_{\\mathrm q}>\\gamma/2$. More precisely, if $r=t-2h>0$ and $a+2h\\le u_r-2\\eta$, the construction above with $b_*=b$ gives $$\\label{eq:off-boundary-finite-growth}\n P_t\\le K_0+\\beta_{\\mathrm q}r+\\gamma h\n              +C\\mathcal R+\\tfrac12\\omega^{\\rm cl}_{\\mathcal B}(\\epsilon).$$ Here $\\omega^{\\rm cl}_{\\mathcal B}\\to0$ is the fixed-class error in the classical growth theorem, and the constant is fixed for this cut.",

        "anchor": "stmt-prop-boundary-alternatives",
        "exact_quote": "Assume $\\beta_{\\mathrm q}>\\gamma/2$. For every fixed integer $q\\ge1$ and every fixed $M>0$, a saturation array approaching $\\beta_{\\mathrm q}$ admits $q$ successive backward cuts at times $$t_j=t_0-2jh>0\\quad(0\\le j\\le q),\\qquad u_{t_j}>h,$$ with $h>0$ fixed in the inner limits, satisfying one of the following alternatives.*\n\n1.  *A forced array exists. One can use the same such array, choose a fixed $\\nu>0$ from <a href=\"#eq:forced-root-gap\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"eq:forced-root-gap\">[eq:forced-root-gap]</a>, and take all the times early enough that the saturated tests satisfy $$a_j=u_{t_j}+o(1),\\qquad\n     a_j-b_j\\ge\\nu/2+o(1),\\qquad\n     a_j-b_j\\ge M h/\\gamma+o(1).$$ Every cut uses $b_*=b_j$ at its later endpoint.*\n\n2.  *No forced saturation array exists. At all the indicated times one can use exact isotropic boundary tests $a_j=b_j=u_{t_j}$, and every cut uses $b_*=0$.*\n\n*These assertions remain valid when a prescribed finite number of subdivisions with vanishing tag cost are made at each step, before the earlier test is constructed. In particular the earlier law is uniform on the retained classes produced by those subdivisions. For any prescribed positive accuracy, all the assertions about saturation hold at sufficiently small finite precision with that accuracy; the required precision can depend on the outer bounds, $q,h,\\nu,M$, the subdivision costs, and the selected branch.",

        "exact_quote": "Suppose a finite law satisfies $\\mathbb P(W=w\\mid P=p)\\leq\\epsilon^{k-\\alpha}$. Let $A$ have probability $p_A>0$, and let $\\zeta>0$. On every remaining fiber, $$\\mathbb P(W=w\\mid P,A)\\leq\n   \\epsilon^{\\,k-\\alpha-\\zeta-\\log_{1/\\epsilon}\\!\\left(1/p_A\\right)}.\n \\label{eq:credit-retention}$$ Removing the exceptional fibers does not change this conditional bound.         "anchor": "stmt-lem-orientation-prediction",
        "exact_quote": "Assume the elongated geometry. On $\\pi^{\\rm buf}$, suppose the replacement losses for the isotropic apertures of widths $a$ and $b$ are included in $C_*\\eta$.         "anchor": "stmt-lem-packet-coherence",
        "exact_quote": "Use local coordinates with root time $r$, endpoint duration $2h$, and put $$\\rho=\\epsilon^u,\\qquad s=\\epsilon^{u+h},\\qquad\n \\sigma=\\epsilon^{u+2h}=s^2/\\rho,\\qquad\n \\lambda_{\\rm loc}=s^{-2}.$$ Fixed multiplicative errors in these relations change only constants. Let $P$ be a buffered isotropic cell of width $\\rho$. Let $Q$ specify $P,C_t$ and a position cell of side $s$ at $C_t$. Candidate atoms have this $P$, velocity spacing $s$, earlier position spacing $s$, and transported position within $Rs$ of that cell, where $R=\\epsilon^{-\\theta}$. Let $N_Q$ be their number, and suppose $$|c_T|^2\\leq\\epsilon^{-\\xi}m.$$ Partition their velocities into $K\\leq\\epsilon^{-k-\\xi}$ bins of width $s$, in a fixed normal direction for $d=1$ or in both directions for $d=2$. Let $Z$ add to $Q$ the output position at precision $\\sigma$ in those $d$ directions. Let $m_Z$ be the sum of squared packet tests over all output sites mapping to $Z$, on the input truncated to these candidates. Then $$\\sum_{Z\\mid Q}m_Z\\leq C\\epsilon^{-\\xi}N_Qm,\\qquad\n m_Z\\leq C\\epsilon^{dh-k-2\\theta-2\\xi}N_Qm.\n \\label{eq:finite-coherence}$$ The constant is uniform over all admissible choices of the site-dependent amplitudes. Without candidate truncation, the square root of the mass estimate has the additive tail error provided by Lemma <a href=\"#lem:packet-decomposition\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"lem:packet-decomposition\">37</a>.",

      "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-thm-oscillatory-estimate",
        "exact_quote": "Fix bounded input and output regions $K_v,K_x\\subset\\mathbb R^2$. For the input patch $K_v$, fix a class of smooth real phases satisfying the phase assumptions of Section <a href=\"#sec:packet-structure\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"sec:packet-structure\">9</a>, with common domain $[0,1]\\times\\mathbb R^2\\times U_v$, where $U_v$ is an open neighborhood of $K_v$. All enlarged patches required by the decomposition, expressed in the original $v$ coordinates, are contained in $U_v$ and obey common bounds. The translated systems are considered on the corresponding bounded rescaled patches described in that section, with the resulting uniform bounds. Throughout the phase domain, $$\\partial_v\\Phi(c,x,v)=\\zeta(v,x-cv).$$ For each phase and each required original input patch $V$, the matrix $\\partial_p\\zeta$ is symmetric and satisfies either $$a_0I\\le\\partial_p\\zeta(v,p)\\le a_1I\n \\qquad(v\\in V,\\ p\\in\\mathbb R^2),$$ or the same inequality with $-\\partial_p\\zeta$ in place of $\\partial_p\\zeta$, with common constants $a_0>0$ and $a_1$ for the class. On these original patches, every mixed $v,p$ derivative of total order $j$ of this matrix is bounded by $A^{j+1}(j!)^3$ for a common $A\\ge1$. Fix these constants and all the seminorm bounds of a class of smooth amplitudes $B$ supported in $[0,1]\\times K_x\\times K_v$. For every $\\nu>0$ there is a constant $C_\\nu$, depending only on these fixed data and $\\nu$, such that, for every $\\lambda\\ge2$, every phase and amplitude in the specified classes, and every $f\\in L^3(\\mathbb R^2)$ supported in $K_v$, $$\\label{eq:oscillatory-estimate}\n \\left\\|E_\\lambda f\\right\\|_{L^3([0,1]\\times K_x)}\n \\le C_\\nu\\lambda^{-1+\\nu}\\|f\\|_3,\n \\qquad\n E_\\lambda f(c,x)=\\int e^{i\\lambda\\Phi(c,x,v)}B(c,x,v)f(v)\\,dv.$$",
        "source_id": "PM-078.1"
      },

<a id="pm-s2"></a>
## 2. Definitions, validity and bounds

- **Bochner–Riesz multiplier** ([source](#sec:introduction)): For $\delta>0$, define $$T_\delta f(x) =\int_{\mathbb R^3}(1-\abs{\xi}^2)_+^\delta \widehat f(\xi)e^{2\pi i x\cdot\xi}\,d\xi . \label{eq:main-multiplier}$$
- **Normalized entropy and mutual information** ([source](#sec:entropy)): Put $\ell=\log(1/\epsilon)$ and write $\mathsf H_{\mathrm{nat}},\mathsf I_{\mathrm{nat}}$ for natural-log entropy and mutual information, with $\mathsf H=\mathsf H_{\mathrm{nat}}/\ell$ and $\mathsf I=\mathsf I_{\mathrm{nat}}/\ell$.
- **Homogeneous conditional observation** ([source](#pm-h-12)): A conditional observation is *homogeneous with exponent $d$* if its realized conditional surprise, divided by $\ell$, converges to $d$ in probability and its normalized conditional entropy also converges to $d$.
- **Dyadic nonconcentrated square family** ([source](#sec:projection)): A finite family of dyadic $\rho$-squares $\mathcal P$ is a $(\rho,d,C)$-set if $$\#\{p\in\mathcal P:p\cap B(z,r)\ne\varnothing\} \le C r^d\#\mathcal P,\qquad \rho\le r\le1,$$ up to a fixed enlargement of the ball.
- **Slope tag** ([source](#sec:projection)): A tag is a slope together with any auxiliary labels; distinct tags may have the same slope.
- **Aperture weight** ([source](#sec:classical-extremality)): Fix $0<\gamma<1$, and put $$w(b,a)=(1+\gamma)b+(1-\gamma)a =a+b-\gamma(a-b),\qquad 0\le b\le a.$$
- **Standard aperture observation** ([source](#stmt-def-classical-aperture)): At duration $t$ and horizon $L$, a standard observation $G$ records $$(t,b,a,C_t,R_{a-b},[V]_{b,a;R}, [X(C_t)]_{b+t,a+t;R}), \qquad 0\le b\le a,\quad a+t\le L.$$
- **Classical root supremum** ([source](#pm-h-15)): Define the root supremum by $$\tau_L(T)=\sup_{D\text{ at duration }0} \{\mathbb Ew(D)-\mathsf I(T;D)\}.$$
- **Classical score and universal growth rate** ([source](#eq:classical-score)): Write $S_t=\mathsf H(C_t\mid T)$ and $$\mathcal F_t(G)=\mathbb Ew(G)-\mathsf I(T;G)+2S_t, \qquad \beta=\sup\limsup_{\epsilon\to0} \frac{\mathcal F_t(G)-\tau_L(T)}{t}. \label{eq:classical-score}$$
- **Saturated observation** ([source](#pm-h-16)): Call an observation saturated if, along the sequence under discussion, $\mathcal F_t(G)-\tau_L(T)\to\beta t$.
- **Matched-plane information potential** ([source](#eq:matched-plane-profile)): The information of a matched aperture is therefore the restriction $$\label{eq:matched-plane-profile} \Phi(i,u)=f\bigl(\Pi_m(i,u)\bigr).$$
- **Grouped middle datum** ([source](#pm-h-28)): When $m=1$, impose $L_Y=L_W=L_U$ at this point and regard $U=(Y,W)$ as one datum of capacity two, with $\mathbf L=(L_X,L_U,L_Z)$. The profile and all the trace statements below are then defined on this grouped domain, and the middle datum has one joint trace rate.
- **Packet mass** ([source](#eq:packet-mass)): Its mass is $$m_O(f)=\left\|\rho_t^{-1}\int f(v) \psi_O\left(\frac{v-V}{\rho_t}\right) e^{i\lambda\Phi(C_t,X,v)}\,dv\right\|^2. \label{eq:packet-mass}$$
- **Packet score** ([source](#eq:packet-score)): For any probability law on observations and aperture labels, supported where $m_O>0$, define $$P_t=\mathsf H(O)+\frac12\mathsf H(O\mid D) +\frac32\mathbb E\log_{1/\epsilon}\!\left(m_O\right) +\frac12\mathbb Ew(D). \label{eq:packet-score}$$
- **Packet growth supremum** ([source](#pm-h-45)): Define $\beta_{\mathrm q}$ to be the supremum of $$\limsup_{\epsilon\to0}\frac{P_t-K_0}{t} \label{eq:packet-growth-supremum}$$ over all the preceding systems, allowing convergent bounded depth parameters with positive limiting duration.
- **Successive saturation array** ([source](#stmt-def-packet-saturation-array)): After normalizing duration to one, a saturation array consists of rows indexed by $j$, with small parameters $\epsilon_{j,n}\downarrow0$ within each row.
- **Incoming fine-velocity credit** ([source](#eq:incoming-packet-credit)): An incoming credit $k_f\geq0$, with error $\alpha_f$, means that on the normalized law being used, $$\sup_w\mathbb P(W_f=w\mid P_f=p)\leq \epsilon^{\,k_f-\alpha_f} \quad\text{for every \(p\) of positive probability}. \label{eq:incoming-packet-credit}$$
- **Complex-order multiplier** ([source](#stmt-lem-br-complex-order)): For $\Re z>0$ and $R>0$, let $T_{z,R}$ have multiplier $(1-\|\xi\|^2/R^2)_+^z$, and write $T_z=T_{z,1}$.

          "exact_quote": "Fix an integer $k\\ge1$. Let $p^0$ be a probability law on a finite pair space $\\mathcal P\\times\\Theta$. Write $\\mu^0=p^0_P$ and $\\lambda^0=p^0_\\theta$. Let $Q_j=Q_j(P,\\theta)$, $1\\le j\\le k$, be finite coordinate observations, and put $\\xi_j^\\theta=p^0_{Q_j\\mid\\theta}$ on positive label fibers, choosing an arbitrary probability law on a zero-mass label fiber. Define the two nonnegative natural-log quantities $$\\begin{aligned}\n D_{\\mathrm{pair}}\n &=\\mathop{\\mathrm{KL}}(p^0_{P,\\theta}\\Vert\\mu^0\\otimes\\lambda^0),\\\\\n D_{\\mathrm{coord}}\n &=\\mathop{\\mathrm{KL}}\\left(p^0_{\\theta,Q_1,\\ldots,Q_k}\n       \\middle\\Vert\n       \\lambda^0(\\theta)\\prod_{j=1}^k\\xi_j^\\theta(Q_j)\\right)\\\\\n &=\\sum_{j=1}^k\\mathsf H_{\\mathrm{nat}}^{p^0}(Q_j\\mid\\theta)\n       -\\mathsf H_{\\mathrm{nat}}^{p^0}(Q_1,\\ldots,Q_k\\mid\\theta).\n\\end{aligned}$$ The second quantity is averaged over the labels; no individual label is assumed to have small conditional multiinformation.*\n\n\n\n\n*Let $\\mathcal F$ be a finite list of observations on the pair space which contains $P$, $\\theta$, and every $(\\theta,Q_j)$. It may also contain any finite list of prefix and joint observations. Write $N=|\\mathcal F|$, counting occurrences rather than values. Let $\\mathcal H$ be an event of $p^0$-mass at least $1-\\zeta$, where $\\zeta\\ge0$. For $v>0$, choose $$0<\\underline M\n \\le1-\\zeta-\\frac{D_{\\mathrm{pair}}+D_{\\mathrm{coord}}+2/e}{v},\n \\qquad\n \\delta=\\frac{\\underline M}{2N}.$$ Then there is a restriction $r\\le\\boldsymbol1_{\\mathcal H}p^0$, of mass $M\\ge\\underline M/2$, such that, for every listed observation $F$ and every value with $r_F(f)>0$, $$\\delta p^0_F(f)\\le r_F(f)\\le p^0_F(f).\n \\label{eq:block-core-floors}$$ For the normalized law $\\pi=r/M$, write $\\mu=\\pi_P$ and $\\lambda=\\pi_\\theta$. Its pair law and its coordinate law on every positive label fiber satisfy $$\\begin{aligned}\n \\pi(P,\\theta)\n &\\le e^v M\\delta^{-2}\\mu(P)\\lambda(\\theta),\n \\label{eq:block-core-pair}\\\\\n \\pi(Q_1,\\ldots,Q_k\\mid\\theta)\n &\\le e^v\\delta^{-k}\n          \\prod_{j=1}^k\\pi(Q_j\\mid\\theta).\n \\label{eq:block-core-coordinate}\n\\end{aligned}$$ All factors on the right of these two inequalities are marginals of this same law $\\pi$.*\n\n\n*If $A,B$ are listed observations and $A$ is determined by $B$, then for every retained child value $b$, with parent $a=A(b)$, $$\\delta p^0(B=b\\mid A=a)\n \\le \\pi(B=b\\mid A=a)\n \\le\\delta^{-1}p^0(B=b\\mid A=a).\n \\label{eq:block-core-prefix-ratio}$$ The upper inequality can be summed over any set of child values. The lower inequality is asserted only for retained children. In particular, fix $0<\\rho<1$.           "exact_quote": "Fix $0\\le r<t$, a shape $0\\le b\\le a\\le\\min(L-t,u_t)$, and $0\\le b_*\\le b$. Within the localizer $J$, including its auxiliary tags, let $N_{\\rm all}(J)$ be the size of the whole cap class, $N(J)>0$ its retained size, $m(J)$ its coefficient mass bin, and $g(J)$ its cap maximum bin. Set $$\\begin{aligned}\n A_J&=\\log_{1/\\epsilon}\\!\\left(N(J)\\right)+\\tfrac32\\log_{1/\\epsilon}\\!\\left(m(J)\\right)+\\tfrac12g(J),\n       \\label{eq:composition-A}\\\\\n K_r^*&=\\mathsf H(J)+b_*+\n       \\mathbb E\\left[\\log_{1/\\epsilon}\\!\\left(N_{\\rm all}(J)\\right)\n                    +\\tfrac32\\log_{1/\\epsilon}\\!\\left(m(J)\\right)+\\tfrac12g(J)\\right].\n       \\label{eq:composition-Kstar}\n\\end{aligned}$$ Let $K_J$ denote the canonical local root score, including its norm option, for the retained local superposition. Let $P_J$ be its score at duration $t-r$, with the conditional output law and the winning superposition masses. The next inequality shows that saturation at the endpoint forces these four comparisons to be nearly sharp on average; the subsequent selection estimate specifies the branches on which this remains true. Writing $\\Delta_t=K_0+\\beta_{\\mathrm q}t-P_t$, one has the finite bound $$\\label{eq:finite-packet-deficits}\n d_0+\\mathbb E(d_1+d_2+d_3)\\le\\Delta_t+5\\mathcal R.$$ There is also an earlier test on the *retained uniform classes*, with that same current marginal of $J$ and the assigned cap labels, whose score satisfies $$\\label{eq:retained-back-score}\n P_r^{\\rm ret}\\ge K_r^*\n              -\\tfrac32\\mathbb Ed_1-\\mathcal R.$$ At $r=0$ this is an actual test for the original canonical $K_0$; the norm option is not used in this lower bound.*\n\n\n*More quantitatively, put $R_t=\\Delta_t+5\\mathcal R$. For an event $B$ measurable in $J$ with probability $p>0$ and any $\\theta>0$, $$\\label{eq:packet-typical-selection}\n \\mathbb P\\bigl(B\\cap\\{d_1+d_2+d_3>\\theta\\}\\bigr)\n       \\le R_t/\\theta.$$ In particular, taking $\\theta=2R_t/p$ leaves at least $p/2$ of the current probability in $B$, and bounds each of the three local deficits by $2R_t/p$. ## 3. Proof roadmap

- **step-entropy-restriction** [claim](#stmt-lem-entropy-restriction) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-entropy-restriction): Chain rules, log-sum, and conditional relative entropy. -> Determination, ambiguity, mass, and restriction estimates.
- **step-typical-conditioning** [claim](#stmt-lem-typical-conditioning) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-typical-conditioning): Likelihood summation and conditional normalization. -> Typical-fiber domination and retained child estimates.
- **step-splitting-resampling** [claim](#stmt-lem-entropy-splitting) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-entropy-splitting): Information chain rules and explicit kernel extension. -> Controlled splitting and preserved original joint law.
- **step-homogeneous-bins** [claim](#stmt-lem-homogenization) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-homogenization): Tail removal, surprise binning, and conditional relative entropy. -> Uniform retained bins and support counts.
- **step-likelihood-core** [claim](#stmt-lem-zero-information) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-zero-information): Positive likelihood-tail estimate and relative entropy decomposition. -> Trimmed domination and converse information bound.
- **step-actual-marginals** [claim](#stmt-lem-marginal-core) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-marginal-core): Repeated marginal deletion with an occurrence-wise mass charge. -> One core with simultaneous actual marginal products.
- **step-finite-stars** [claim](#stmt-thm-finite-conditioning) / [proof](#proof-stmt-thm-finite-conditioning): Conditional independent sampling, typical likelihoods, and simultaneous coring. -> Explicit conditioned comparison populations.
- **step-point-slices** [claim](#stmt-cor-point-slicing) / [proof](#proof-stmt-cor-point-slicing): Restrict and divide by the common point-observation marginal. -> Point-sliced domination with preserved label comparisons.
- **step-profile-diagonal** [claim](#stmt-lem-profile-diagonal) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-profile-diagonal): Slowly increasing finite lists, compact extraction, and successive precision choices. -> Countable homogeneous profiles and correctly ordered limits.
- **step-discrete-input** [claim](#stmt-thm-ren-wang) / [proof](#sec:projection): Use the cited discrete incidence theorem with output loss fixed first. -> Sharp tube-union expansion input.
- **step-weighted-projections** [claim](#stmt-thm-planar-projection) / [proof](#proof-stmt-thm-planar-projection): Sample points and whole tags, prune occupancies, then apply the discrete input. -> Weighted tagged projection bound and limiting exponent.
- **step-saturation-splitting** [claim](#stmt-lem-classical-splitting) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-classical-splitting): Combine root kernels and compare exact score chain rules. -> Typical conditional saturation.
- **step-cap-regularization** [claim](#stmt-lem-classical-cap-regularization) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-classical-cap-regularization): Greedy cap removal and binning of successive maxima. -> Cap mass bounds and stable root levels.
- **step-classical-localization** [claim](#stmt-lem-classical-localization) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-classical-localization): Anisotropic affine rescaling and singular-value control of composed rectangles. -> Local score bounds and saturated predecessors.
- **step-least-aspect** [claim](#stmt-prop-least-aspect) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-least-aspect): Independent replicas, rectangle gain, bounded-aspect reduction, and diagonal minimization. -> Least-aspect saturated sequence.
- **step-coherent-path** [claim](#stmt-prop-saturated-path) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-saturated-path): Backward predecessor composition and conditional replica comparison. -> One saturated path with coherent orientation prefixes.
- **step-tangent-reduction** [claim](#stmt-prop-isotropic-reduction) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-isotropic-reduction): Differentiate bounded-variation shapes and localize shrinking intervals in successive limits. -> Isotropic alternative or matched positive aspect.
- **step-intercept-count** [claim](#stmt-lem-isotropic-intercepts) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-isotropic-intercepts): Count point cells against witnesses for occupied intercept cells. -> Intercept support bound.
- **step-grid-projections** [claim](#stmt-lem-isotropic-grid-projections) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-isotropic-grid-projections): Invertible linear changes of coordinates and discrete Loomis–Whitney. -> Point-cell cardinality bounds.
- **step-isotropic-exclusion** [claim](#stmt-prop-isotropic-exclusion) / [proof](#sec:isotropic): Force strip concentration, build an earlier anisotropic test, and apply terminal two-slope expansion. -> Contradiction with scalar time capacity.
- **step-plane-traces** [claim](#stmt-thm-characteristic-trace) / [proof](#proof-stmt-thm-characteristic-trace): Mixed-sign flux control, strong slice limits, weak measure limits, and affine blowup. -> Strong plane traces, measure identities, and affine approximation.
- **step-finite-trace-block** [claim](#stmt-cor-finite-characteristic-trace) / [proof](#proof-stmt-cor-finite-characteristic-trace): Select a large good patch at a profile-dependent block scale, then impose uniform finite approximation. -> Simultaneous finite affine errors.
- **step-curve-traces** [claim](#stmt-lem-curve-traces) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-curve-traces): Directional bounded-variation slicing and transverse graph reparameterization. -> One-sided strong traces and signed jump measures.
- **step-affine-block-core** [claim](#stmt-lem-affine-block-core) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-affine-block-core): Pull back likelihood trims to one pair space and delete values below marginal floors. -> Actual product comparisons and preserved prefix ratios.
- **step-direction-bootstrap** [claim](#stmt-prop-directional-bootstrap) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-directional-bootstrap): Two-pin separation followed by reciprocal weighted projection improvements. -> Conditional direction dimension reaches the child rate.
- **step-matched-rate-transfer** [claim](#stmt-prop-rate-transfer) / [proof](#sec:rate-transfer): Extract affine finite blocks, replicate labels, and apply distinct-clock or tied-clock projection tests. -> Coordinate rate-transfer rules.
- **step-contact-tuples** [claim](#stmt-lem-closure-contact-tuples) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-closure-contact-tuples): Rescale inward half-planes and pass generic rate laws to contact limits. -> Contact identities, horizontal signs, and jump constraint.
- **step-positive-tangent-rate** [claim](#stmt-lem-closure-positive-x) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-closure-positive-x): Refine aperture data and average entropy increments over an inward wedge. -> Positive tangent rate on the required contact side.
- **step-sign-algebra** [claim](#stmt-lem-closure-sign-algebra) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-closure-sign-algebra): Exact affine identities expressed as nonnegative sums, with grouped rates at tied clocks. -> Algebraic lower thresholds for contact closure.
- **step-classical-growth-closure** [claim](#stmt-thm-classical-growth) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-closure-sign-algebra-2): Compare contact identities and jumps with the algebraic threshold on each admissible side. -> Classical growth bound.
- **step-packet-bessel** [claim](#stmt-lem-packet-bessel) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-packet-bessel): Nonstationary integration by parts and Schur bounds for packet Gram matrices. -> Uniform Bessel and cap-tail estimates.
- **step-packet-decomposition** [claim](#stmt-lem-packet-decomposition) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-packet-decomposition): Windowed Fourier series, global gradient matching, and quantified mode tails. -> Finite earlier atoms and controlled endpoint pairing errors.
- **step-packet-cap-classes** [claim](#stmt-lem-cap-class) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-cap-class): Greedy cap removal grouped by maximum and assigned widths. -> Cap-count upper bounds and whole-fiber lower bounds.
- **step-local-root-comparison** [claim](#stmt-prop-local-root-comparison) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-local-root-comparison): Total and cap Bessel bounds with log-sum; uniform whole-class earlier tests. -> Local root upper bound and earlier whole-class score lower bound.
- **step-preliminary-packet-growth** [claim](#stmt-prop-packet-trivial-growth) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-packet-trivial-growth): Collapse coherent masses by coarse observations, then introduce uniform contributors and use entropy chains. -> Finite preliminary packet growth ceiling.
- **step-packet-composition** [claim](#stmt-prop-finite-packet-composition) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-finite-packet-composition): Retain geometric localizer entropy and cancel finite composition deficits. -> Nonnegative deficits, mean bound, and retained earlier score.
- **step-boundary-slack** [claim](#stmt-lem-packet-boundary-slack) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-packet-boundary-slack): Use earlier uncertainty slack to construct faithful positive-transport tests. -> Saturation forces the active uncertainty boundary.
- **step-backward-alternatives** [claim](#stmt-prop-boundary-alternatives) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-boundary-alternatives): Use a persistent root gap or exclude cap excess to select isotropic earlier tests. -> Fixed finite backward chain with compatible aperture geometry.
- **step-credit-retention** [claim](#stmt-lem-packet-credit-retention) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-packet-credit-retention): Discard parent fibers with inadequate relative event retention. -> Restored incoming credit on retained parent fibers.
- **step-normal-prediction** [claim](#stmt-lem-orientation-prediction) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-orientation-prediction): Compare independent conditional aperture copies and intersect separated strips. -> Deterministic coarse-cell normal predictor.
- **step-earlier-alignment** [claim](#stmt-lem-orientation-alignment) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-orientation-alignment): Compare assigned-cap and current-aperture information using biased contributors and finite deficit bounds. -> Misalignment probability controlled by current composition deficit.
- **step-packet-coherence** [claim](#stmt-lem-packet-coherence) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-packet-coherence): Bessel for aggregate masses and binwise Schur or Cauchy–Schwarz estimates for concentrated masses. -> Aggregate and pointwise strip or cell mass bounds.
- **step-finite-repayment** [claim](#stmt-prop-finite-repayment) / [proof](#pm-h-63): Estimate candidate masses before sampling; resample faithful apertures and preserve incoming information under the assembled law. -> Increased outgoing credit and returned earlier score.
- **step-packet-growth-closure** [claim](#stmt-thm-packet-growth) / [proof](#pm-h-65): Iterate repayment along a fixed finite backward chain and compare accumulated credit with capacity. -> Sharp packet growth bound.
- **step-oscillatory-estimate** [claim](#stmt-thm-oscillatory-estimate) / [proof](#proof-stmt-thm-oscillatory-estimate): Bound restricted root scores, maximize endpoint log-sum, and decompose general inputs into amplitude levels. -> Oscillatory integral norm decay with arbitrary positive loss.
- **step-kernel-expansion** [claim](#stmt-lem-br-kernel) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-br-kernel): Radial slicing and endpoint dyadic integration by parts. -> Oscillatory kernel symbols and integrable high-order kernels.
- **step-main-multiplier** [claim](#stmt-thm-bochner-riesz) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-br-kernel-2): Apply pseudoconformal distance coordinates with a global definite extension, then sum decaying physical shells. -> Bounded positive-order multiplier and unique extension.
- **step-complex-orders** [claim](#stmt-lem-br-complex-order) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-br-complex-order): Beta mixture of dilated real-order operators and finite gamma recurrence. -> Polynomial complex-order boundary growth.
- **step-full-strict-range** [claim](#stmt-cor-full-bochner-riesz) / [proof](#proof-stmt-cor-full-bochner-riesz): Analytic interpolation with Gaussian damping, fixed-operator interpolation, duality, and dilation. -> Full strict multiplier range uniformly over radii.

## 4. Engineering Triptych

### Panel 1 - epistemic contract

- **invariant-core-retention**: Simultaneous marginal pruning retains the stated mass lower bound. The executable specialization starts with a probability law on a finite matrix and uniform comparison marginals.
- **invariant-actual-marginal-comparison**: The normalized retained joint law satisfies the product comparison using its own actual marginals, with the retention and threshold factors specified in the lemma.
- **invariant-support-and-normalization**: Restriction preserves support upper bounds, and normalization changes marginal mass upper bounds by the reciprocal of retained mass.

### Panel 2 - negative knowledge

- **anti-use-main-theorem-certificate**: Treat a finite pruning experiment as a certificate for the Bochner–Riesz multiplier theorem. -> The experiment checks a finite probability construction and does not evaluate the oscillatory, trace, limiting, or interpolation arguments.
- **anti-use-untrimmed-independence**: Interpret small normalized mutual information as exact independence of the original population. -> The source obtains domination after trimming, with comparison factors and retained populations explicitly identified.
- **anti-use-original-marginals-after-deletion**: Delete deficient fibers and report the original marginals as the actual marginals of the retained law. -> Restriction changes the population, and the comparison in the conclusion uses marginals of the normalized retained population.
- **anti-use-free-label-conditioning**: Extend the finite star comparison to an observation that also depends on a free label. -> The required product factorization is unavailable for that observation.

### Panel 3 - reference implementation and oracle

Applicability: `constructive`. The finite construction is the marginal-pruning procedure in the proof of simultaneous replacement by actual marginals: "Starting with $\nu$, repeatedly remove all points with $F_{lj}=v$ whenever its current positive marginal is less than $\eta\mu_{lj}(v)$." The executable scope is a finite matrix with uniform comparison factors. It does not certify the paper's analytic conclusions.

```python
# INPUTS: JSON weights, a nonnegative integer matrix with at most nine cells, and eta as [numerator, denominator].
# PRECONDITIONS: Positive total weight; nonempty rectangular matrix; 0 < eta < 1/2.
# OUTPUTS: Surviving positive cells, retained mass, and normalized probabilities as exact rational strings.
# TIME: Each changing pass removes an occupied row or column; each pass scans the matrix.
# SPACE: Matrix storage and a set of retained positive cells.
# ARITHMETIC: Exact rational arithmetic with python-flint fmpq.
# FAILURE: Malformed inputs or failed preconditions raise an exception and produce a nonzero exit.
import json
import sys
from flint import fmpq

def main():
    data = json.load(sys.stdin)
    w = data['weights']
    assert isinstance(w, list) and w and isinstance(w[0], list) and w[0]
    nr, nc = len(w), len(w[0])
    assert nr * nc <= 9
    assert all(isinstance(row, list) and len(row) == nc for row in w)
    assert all(type(v) is int and v >= 0 for row in w for v in row)
    en, ed = data['eta']
    assert type(en) is int and type(ed) is int and ed > 0
    eta = fmpq(en, ed)
    assert 0 < eta < fmpq(1, 2)
    total = sum(sum(row) for row in w)
    assert total > 0
    active = {(i, j) for i in range(nr) for j in range(nc) if w[i][j] > 0}
    threshold_row = eta / nr
    threshold_col = eta / nc
    while True:
        previous = set(active)
        for i in range(nr):
            row_mass = sum((fmpq(w[r][c], total) for r, c in active if r == i), fmpq(0))
            if 0 < row_mass < threshold_row:
                active = {(r, c) for r, c in active if r != i}
        for j in range(nc):
            col_mass = sum((fmpq(w[r][c], total) for r, c in active if c == j), fmpq(0))
            if 0 < col_mass < threshold_col:
                active = {(r, c) for r, c in active if c != j}
        if active == previous:
            break
    assert active
    cells = sorted(active)
    retained = sum(w[i][j] for i, j in cells)
    result = {
        'support': [list(cell) for cell in cells],
        'mass': str(fmpq(retained, total)),
        'probabilities': [str(fmpq(w[i][j]) / retained) for i, j in cells]
    }
    print(json.dumps(result, sort_keys=True))

if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()
```

## 5. Domain engineering contracts

| domain | applies | strength | maturity | basis | why |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| software | False | none | not_applicable | inferred | The multiplier theorem supplies a bounded extension on a continuous function space, without a discretization or numerical error contract for software implementing spherical filtering. |
| games_simulation | False | none | not_applicable | inferred | The positive-transport model specifies straight trajectories and information observations; it supplies no collision, force, or integration scheme for a simulation. |
| tools | False | none | not_applicable | inferred | The finite profile approximation requires selecting a limiting profile before its block scale, and provides no uniform scale-selection procedure for an automatic analysis tool. |
| algorithms | True | strong | implementable | inferred | The simultaneous marginal replacement proof gives a terminating deletion procedure on an explicitly supplied finite population and observation list. Its output has a certified retained mass and product comparisons against its own marginals. |
| data_structures | False | none | not_applicable | inferred | The nested parameter tree supplies mathematical child-capacity bounds, but no storage layout, update operations, or data-structure performance contract. |

<a id="pm-s6"></a>
## 6. Applicability limits and search

- **limit-strict-positive-order** (hypothesis): The multiplier conclusion requires a fixed strictly positive smoothing order satisfying the stated strict range; it supplies no critical-order endpoint bound. Blocked use: ['Applying the strict-range theorem at equality.', 'Taking the smoothing order to zero while keeping its norm constant uniform.']
- **limit-spherical-dimensional-scope** (formal_scope): The main multiplier estimate concerns spherical smoothing in the stated three-dimensional Euclidean space. Blocked use: ['Transferring the positive-order threshold unchanged to other dimensions.', 'Using the theorem as a bound for arbitrary nonspherical frequency windows.']
- **limit-general-surface-extension** (formal_scope): The spherical multiplier result does not establish the separate extension theorem for general positively curved surfaces. Blocked use: ['Claiming the general-surface extension theorem as a consequence proved here.']
- **limit-norm-versus-pointwise-convergence** (formal_scope): Uniform fixed-radius multiplier bounds and norm convergence do not by themselves supply a maximal inequality or almost-everywhere summation theorem. Blocked use: ['Inferring pointwise almost-everywhere convergence directly from the fixed-radius multiplier theorem.']
- **limit-small-information-not-independence** (approximation): Small normalized information gives a product comparison after trimming, rather than exact independence of the original law. Blocked use: ['Replacing the original dependent population by an independent product without restriction or domination losses.']
- **limit-retained-child-scope** (formal_scope): Conditional surprise and support estimates concern retained support and sampled conditional values; they do not bound every untrimmed child from below. Blocked use: ['Applying retained child bounds to arbitrary children discarded during trimming.']
- **limit-homogenization-child-alphabets** (hypothesis): Finite homogenization requires the stated child-alphabet bounds and a fixed finite observation list before precision is selected. Blocked use: ['Applying the homogeneous-bin construction without controlling the child alphabets.', 'Replacing uniform surprise bins by convergence in probability alone when later restrictions are required.']
- **limit-core-positive-mass** (hypothesis): Simultaneous marginal replacement requires positive input mass, specified comparison probability laws, valid product inequalities, and an admissible deletion threshold. Blocked use: ['Normalizing an empty retained population.', 'Reporting product comparisons against original factors as comparisons against actual retained marginals without coring.']
- **limit-fixed-label-conditioning** (hypothesis): The fixed-label factorization permits the auxiliary observation to depend on the point and already fixed labels only. Blocked use: ['Conditioning on an observation involving a free label while retaining the same free-label product factorization.']
- **limit-star-not-cyclic-graph** (formal_scope): The finite conditioning conclusions concern a fixed finite star and provide no density lower bound for an arbitrary cyclic incidence graph. Blocked use: ['Extending the star comparison to arbitrary cyclic incidence configurations.']
- **limit-projection-population-hypotheses** (hypothesis): The weighted projection estimate needs point and slope nonconcentration across the prescribed scales, sufficient graph product mass, and uniform projection support counts. Blocked use: ['Substituting an averaged entropy lower bound for the required ball-mass bounds.', 'Applying the projection conclusion to an arbitrarily sparse incidence graph.']
- **limit-profile-dependent-diagonal** (nonconstructive): Profile extraction and shrinking-block diagonals supply no convergence rate uniform over block length or limiting profile. Blocked use: ['Choosing finite precision from an unspecified universal convergence rate.', 'Interchanging the profile, block-scale, and precision selections.']
- **limit-trace-signs-and-distinct-clocks** (hypothesis): Characteristic-plane traces require the local derivative bounds, nonpositive mixed distributional derivatives, and distinct clocks in the abstract trace theorem. Blocked use: ['Using ambient almost-everywhere differentiability alone to obtain derivatives on the selected plane.', 'Applying separate middle-coordinate traces when the middle clocks coincide.']
- **limit-characteristic-curve-component** (edge_case): The curve-trace lemma makes no assertion about a rate field whose speed equals the contact slope. Blocked use: ['Assigning a strong transverse trace to a characteristic component without an additional argument.']
- **limit-packet-global-phase-class** (hypothesis): The packet and oscillatory estimates require the specified transport-compatible phase, global uniform definiteness on the required patches, and common derivative and amplitude bounds. Blocked use: ['Applying the packet decomposition with only local definiteness where global gradient matching is needed.', 'Treating arbitrary smooth oscillatory phases as members of the stated phase class.']
- **limit-earlier-position-uncertainty** (approximation): The earlier packet transport tolerance can exceed the fine endpoint position spacing, so the decomposition alone does not identify coherent masses with a positive straight-trajectory law. Blocked use: ['Assigning an earlier packet a fine output position solely from its transported center.', 'Introducing a positive contributor law before establishing the analytic mass bounds.']
- **limit-tail-floor-and-parameter-order** (hypothesis): Packet tail removal and winner replacement require the stated output mass floor and the prescribed order of choosing finite parameters and precision. Blocked use: ['Discarding an absolute tail without comparing it with the retained output mass.', 'Assuming the packet error converges uniformly while the enlargement parameter shrinks.']
- **limit-whole-versus-retained-classes** (formal_scope): The local root upper bound uses the retained superposition, while the assigned-fiber lower bound and whole-class earlier test refer to the full class before subdivision. Blocked use: ['Applying whole assigned-fiber lower bounds directly to every retained subdivision.', 'Discarding the retained-count deficit in the earlier score comparison.']
- **limit-saturation-row-uniformity** (nonconstructive): Saturation arrays have fixed analytic and domain bounds within each inner row; their outer sequence is not asserted to be one admissible small-parameter sequence. Blocked use: ['Using a universal modulus uniformly over growing outer bounds.', 'Treating a limiting saturated sequence as a finite maximizing measure.']
- **limit-restriction-deficit-budget** (hypothesis): Branch retention must control score deficits relative to the current event probability as well as preserve the incoming conditional probability cap. Blocked use: ['Assuming subpower event probability alone preserves saturation.', 'Reusing an incoming credit bound after restriction without its current-law retention cost.']
- **limit-repayment-prepared-cut** (hypothesis): Finite repayment requires a prepared boundary cut, controlled replacement and composition deficits, accumulated incoming-credit error, and the stated endpoint score comparison. Blocked use: ['Iterating repayment on arbitrary packet laws without preparing the cut.', 'Replacing the assembled endpoint marginal by independently conditioned localizer laws when using incoming credit.']
- **limit-complex-order-transfer** (hypothesis): Complex-order transfer requires a bounded positive real-order operator and a strictly larger real part; the infinite-exponent conclusion additionally requires an integrable real-order kernel. Blocked use: ['Applying the complex-order product bound at the base real order.', 'Using the infinite-exponent transfer without the kernel-integrability hypothesis.']
- **limit-no-discrete-runtime-certificate** (unknown): A discrete numerical error contract, implementation runtime bound, and computable value for the main operator constant are ABSENT. Blocked use: ['Using the analytic norm constant as a runtime estimate.', 'Treating a finite probability experiment as a certificate for the full analytic theorem.']

<a id="pm-s7"></a>
## 7. Complete mathematical paper


We prove the three-dimensional Bochner–Riesz conjecture in its strict-order formulation. The main result is boundedness of the Bochner–Riesz multipliers on $`L^3(\mathbb R^3)`$ for every positive order. Interpolation and duality then give the full conjectured strict range.

<a id="sec:introduction"></a>
### Introduction

We prove the Bochner–Riesz conjecture in three dimensions in its strict-order formulation. The main estimate is boundedness on $L^3$ for every positive order; interpolation and duality then give the full range of exponents.

For $f\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^3)$, use the Fourier transform $$\widehat f(\xi)=\int_{\mathbb R^3}f(x)e^{-2\pi i x\cdot\xi}\,dx,$$ where $\mathcal S$ denotes the Schwartz space. For $\delta>0$, define <a id="eq:main-multiplier"></a>$$T_\delta f(x)
 =\int_{\mathbb R^3}(1-\abs{\xi}^2)_+^\delta
       \widehat f(\xi)e^{2\pi i x\cdot\xi}\,d\xi .
 \label{eq:main-multiplier}$$

<a id="stmt-thm-bochner-riesz"></a>
<div id="thm:bochner-riesz" class="theorem">

**Theorem 1**. *For every $\delta>0$, there is a finite constant $C_\delta$ such that <a id="eq:main-bound"></a>$$\norm{T_\delta f}_{L^3(\mathbb R^3)}
 \le C_\delta\norm f_{L^3(\mathbb R^3)}
 \qquad(f\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^3)).
 \label{eq:main-bound}$$ Consequently $T_\delta$ has a unique bounded extension to $L^3(\mathbb R^3)$.*

</div>

<a id="eq:intro-full-range"></a>
Theorem <a href="#thm:bochner-riesz" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:bochner-riesz">1</a> gives $$\norm{T_\delta f}_{L^p(\mathbb R^3)}
 \lesssim_{p,\delta}\norm f_{L^p(\mathbb R^3)},\qquad
 \delta>\max\left\{3\left|\frac1p-\frac12\right|-\frac12,0\right\},
 \quad 1\le p\le\infty .
 \label{eq:intro-full-range}$$ Corollary <a href="#cor:full-bochner-riesz" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="cor:full-bochner-riesz">53</a> supplies the interpolation argument, including the bounds for complex orders. The order is fixed before choosing any constants. Dilation gives the same bounds for multipliers $(1-|\xi|^2/R^2)_+^\delta$ at every $R>0$; for finite $p$ in <a href="#eq:intro-full-range" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:intro-full-range">[eq:intro-full-range]</a>, these means converge to $f$ in $L^p$ as $R\to\infty$. This recovers Fourier inversion by arbitrarily mild spherical smoothing at the central exponents $3/2\le p\le3$.

<a id="pm-h-3"></a>
#### The problem and its development

The problem belongs to the theory of summability of Fourier expansions. Riesz’s work on one-dimensional summation methods (Riesz 1923) <a id="pm-cite-1"></a>[[Riesz1923](#ref-Riesz1923)] preceded Bochner’s spherical means for multiple Fourier series (Bochner 1935, 1936) <a id="pm-cite-2"></a>[[Bochner1935](#ref-Bochner1935), [Bochner1936](#ref-Bochner1936)]. The multiplier $(1-|\xi|^2)_+^\delta$ softens the boundary of the frequency ball; the question is how much smoothing is needed to preserve an $L^p$ norm. Radial inversion and radial summability were studied by Herz and Welland (Herz 1954; Welland 1975) <a id="pm-cite-3"></a>[[Herz1954](#ref-Herz1954), [Welland1975](#ref-Welland1975)]. For general functions the geometry of frequency directions is essential. Using a Kakeya construction, Fefferman proved that in dimension at least two the order-zero ball multiplier is unbounded on $L^p$ for $p\ne2$ (Fefferman 1971) <a id="pm-cite-4"></a>[[Fefferman1971](#ref-Fefferman1971)], while Carleson and Sjölin established the conjectured positive-order range in the plane (Carleson and Sjölin 1972) <a id="pm-cite-5"></a>[[CarlesonSjolin1972](#ref-CarlesonSjolin1972)].

Geometric decompositions connect this problem with the arrangement of long thin tubes and with Fourier restriction. Córdoba’s work on radial multipliers and Kakeya maximal functions developed this connection through rectangle decompositions and almost orthogonality (Córdoba 1975, 1977) <a id="pm-cite-6"></a>[[Cordoba1975](#ref-Cordoba1975), [Cordoba1977](#ref-Cordoba1977)]. Bourgain combined geometric maximal-function estimates with improved restriction and multiplier bounds in three dimensions (Bourgain 1991) <a id="pm-cite-7"></a>[[Bourgain1991RestrictionMultiplier](#ref-Bourgain1991RestrictionMultiplier)]. The bilinear restriction theorems of Wolff for the cone and Tao for the paraboloid and elliptic surfaces (Wolff 2001; Tao 2003) <a id="pm-cite-8"></a>[[Wolff2001](#ref-Wolff2001), [Tao2003](#ref-Tao2003)] led, through Lee’s multiplier reduction, to sharp-order Bochner–Riesz estimates for $\max\{p,p'\}\ge10/3$ (Lee 2004) <a id="pm-cite-9"></a>[[Lee2004](#ref-Lee2004)]; here $p'$ is the Hölder conjugate of $p$. The threshold exponent follows from Lee’s printed strict range by interpolation with $L^2$, keeping a positive margin in the order.

Polynomial partitioning and subsequent multiscale refinements brought further progress on restriction (Guth 2016; H. Wang 2022) <a id="pm-cite-10"></a>[[Guth2016](#ref-Guth2016), [WangBrooms2020](#ref-WangBrooms2020)]. For the multiplier itself, Wu obtained the conjectured strict-order range when $\max\{p,p'\}\ge13/4$ (Wu 2023) <a id="pm-cite-11"></a>[[Wu2023](#ref-Wu2023)]. Guo, Oh, Wang, Wu, and Zhang developed a pseudoconformal approach and an induction on two scales for transferring restriction methods to Bochner–Riesz estimates (Guo et al. 2025) <a id="pm-cite-12"></a>[[GuoOhWangWuZhang2025](#ref-GuoOhWangWuZhang2025)]. More recently, Gao, Wu, and Xi established the strict-order multiplier range $\max\{p,p'\}\ge22/7$ (Gao, Wu, and Xi 2026, Corollary 1.3) <a id="pm-cite-13"></a>[[GaoWuXi2026](#ref-GaoWuXi2026)]. Wang and Wu’s related diagonal extension estimate holds for $p>22/7$ (H. Wang and Wu 2024, Theorem 0.2) <a id="pm-cite-14"></a>[[WangWu2024](#ref-WangWu2024)]. The connection also runs in the other direction: Tao showed that the Bochner–Riesz conjecture implies the spherical restriction conjecture (Tao 1999) <a id="pm-cite-15"></a>[[Tao1999](#ref-Tao1999)]. Our argument directly establishes the scalar multiplier bound on $L^3(\mathbb R^3)$ for every fixed positive order. Zipeng Wang has also proposed a proof of the Bochner–Riesz conjecture in all dimensions (Z. Wang 2026, version 6, Theorem One) <a id="pm-cite-16"></a>[[ZipengWang2026](#ref-ZipengWang2026)].

Let $S^2=\{\omega\in\mathbb R^3:|\omega|=1\}$ and let $\sigma$ be surface area measure on $S^2$. For bounded measurable $g:S^2\to\mathbb C$, define $$Eg(x)=\int_{S^2}g(\omega)e^{2\pi i x\cdot\omega}\,d\sigma(\omega).$$ Tao’s implication applied to <a href="#eq:intro-full-range" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:intro-full-range">[eq:intro-full-range]</a> gives, for every real $p>3$, $$\norm{Eg}_{L^p(\mathbb R^3)}
 \le C_p\norm{g}_{L^\infty(S^2,\sigma)},$$ where $C_p<\infty$ depends only on $p$. This is the spherical extension estimate also proved in OpenAI (2026c, Theorem 1.1) <a id="pm-cite-17"></a>[[OpenAISphere2026](#ref-OpenAISphere2026)]. For the separate diagonal extension theorem on compact smooth positively curved surfaces, possibly with smooth boundary, see OpenAI (2026b, Theorem 1.1) <a id="pm-cite-18"></a>[[OpenAIDiagonal2026](#ref-OpenAIDiagonal2026)]; that general-surface statement is not deduced here from the spherical multiplier theorem.

An independent route through critical local smoothing gives the same full strict fixed-radius range in <a href="#eq:intro-full-range" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:intro-full-range">[eq:intro-full-range]</a>, uniformly in the radius (OpenAI 2026a, Corollary 11.2) <a id="pm-cite-19"></a>[[OpenAILocalSmoothing2026](#ref-OpenAILocalSmoothing2026)]. It also gives strong maximal Bochner–Riesz bounds and almost-everywhere summation for $3\le p<\infty$ and $\delta>1-3/p$ (OpenAI 2026a, Theorem 11.1) <a id="pm-cite-20"></a>[[OpenAILocalSmoothing2026](#ref-OpenAILocalSmoothing2026)]. These results are not inputs to the argument here.

The geometric input here is the sharp planar Furstenberg estimate of Ren and Wang (Ren and Wang 2025) <a id="pm-cite-21"></a>[[RenWang2025](#ref-RenWang2025)]. It belongs to a line of projection theory that includes the classical work of Marstrand and Kaufman (Marstrand 1954; Kaufman 1968) <a id="pm-cite-22"></a>[[Marstrand1954](#ref-Marstrand1954), [Kaufman1968](#ref-Kaufman1968)] and the discretized sum-product and projection methods of Bourgain (Bourgain 2010) <a id="pm-cite-23"></a>[[Bourgain2010](#ref-Bourgain2010)]. Oberlin formulated a sharp prediction for exceptional projection directions (Oberlin 2012) <a id="pm-cite-24"></a>[[Oberlin2012](#ref-Oberlin2012)]. Important advances toward the Furstenberg problem include the packing-dimension results of Orponen and Shmerkin (Orponen 2020; Shmerkin 2022) <a id="pm-cite-25"></a>[[Orponen2020Packing](#ref-Orponen2020Packing), [Shmerkin2022Packing](#ref-Shmerkin2022Packing)], their joint Hausdorff-dimension improvement (Orponen and Shmerkin 2023) <a id="pm-cite-26"></a>[[OrponenShmerkin2023Hausdorff](#ref-OrponenShmerkin2023Hausdorff)], and their proof of the conjectured bound when the associated family of affine lines has equal Hausdorff and packing dimensions (Orponen and Shmerkin 2026) <a id="pm-cite-27"></a>[[OrponenShmerkin2026ABC](#ref-OrponenShmerkin2026ABC)]. Building on that regular case, Ren and Wang removed the additional equality assumption. We use their finite incidence theorem. Section <a href="#sec:projection" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:projection">3</a> derives the form needed for probability weights, auxiliary tags that may share a slope, and incidence graphs of positive product mass; Section <a href="#sec:entropy" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:entropy">2</a> supplies the finite conditioning used in later applications.

<a id="pm-h-4"></a>
#### From geometric growth to oscillatory cancellation

The proof has two stages. We first control the information gained by observing positive masses moving along lines. We then transfer that control to wave packets, whose squared amplitudes are positive but whose superposition is oscillatory. The main obstruction is at the uncertainty boundary: an earlier packet cannot be assigned a position as precisely as a later observation requires. The second stage records this discrepancy as fine velocity information and shows that too much growth would make that information exceed its finite capacity.

<a id="pm-h-5"></a>
###### Positive masses on lines.

A particle $T$ carries bounded data $(V,A)\in\mathbb R^2\times\mathbb R^2$ and moves along $c\mapsto A+cV$. Fix a small parameter $\epsilon$. An aperture observation at duration $t$ records velocity in a rectangle of widths $\epsilon^b,\epsilon^a$, $b\le a$, and position in a transported rectangle of widths $\epsilon^{b+t},\epsilon^{a+t}$. Its orientation is also recorded. For $0<\gamma<1$, the weight $$w(b,a)=a+b-\gamma(a-b)$$ rewards fine resolution while penalizing eccentricity.
