Extra tags cost at most $\log_{1/\epsilon}\!\left(S\right)$. It follows that $$\mathsf H(O_r)\ge\mathsf H(J)+\mathbb E\log_{1/\epsilon}\!\left(N_{\rm all}\right)-e_{\rm pkt},\qquad
 \mathsf H(O_r\mid D_r)\ge\mathbb E[g-w(E)]-e_{\rm pkt}.$$ The second inequality uses the full assigned fibers in <a href="#eq:packet-assigned-fiber" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:packet-assigned-fiber">[eq:packet-assigned-fiber]</a>, with their actual probabilities under the uniform class law. If one earlier site appears with several coefficient tests, use the largest squared pairing there; this is still an admissible test. Thus its logarithmic mass is at least the corresponding $\log_{1/\epsilon}\!\left(m\right)-e_{\rm pkt}$. At $r=0$, <a href="#eq:packet-coeff-canonical" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:packet-coeff-canonical">[eq:packet-coeff-canonical]</a> gives the same conclusion with the canonical mass. Finally, the earlier aperture weight is $2b_*+w(E)$, by the rescaling computation. Substitution in the score proves <a href="#eq:packet-earlier-whole-score" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:packet-earlier-whole-score">[eq:packet-earlier-whole-score]</a>. ◻

</details>

<a id="pm-h-50"></a>
#### The preliminary growth bound

<a id="stmt-prop-packet-trivial-growth"></a>
<div id="prop:packet-trivial-growth" class="proposition">

**Proposition 40** (A finite upper bound for packet growth). *The supremum $\beta_{\mathrm q}$ is finite and $\beta_{\mathrm q}\le1$. This conclusion uses no identification of the original coherent mass with a positive particle law.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-prop-packet-trivial-growth"><summary>Proof of stmt-prop-packet-trivial-growth</summary>

<a id="eq:packet-coarsen-mass"></a>
*Proof.* Split into fixed aperture-width bins, at a cost tending to zero. Apply Lemma <a href="#lem:packet-decomposition" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:packet-decomposition">37</a> with $r=b_*=0$, then the class and winner construction. Restrict to the mass floor as justified above. Work within one tagged localizer and its retained class. By <a href="#eq:packet-winner-mass" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:packet-winner-mass">[eq:packet-winner-mass]</a>, the original conditional score is at most the score of the winning superposition plus $e_{\rm pkt}$. For the remainder of this conditional calculation, $m_O$ denotes the winning-superposition masses. They satisfy the inherited floor $$m_O\ge (1-q)^2S^{-2}\epsilon^{A_0}\|f\|_2^2.$$ The factor $3\log_{1/\epsilon}\!\left((1-q)^{-1}\right)$ is included in $e_{\rm pkt}$ by reducing $\epsilon_0$; for subpower tag counts the displayed floor still has a fixed polynomial exponent. Let $Z=(C_t,P)$, where $P$ records both velocity and back-transported position $X+(C_0-C_t)V$ isotropically at depth $a$. Set $m_Z=\sum_{O:O\mapsto Z}m_O$. The log-sum inequality on each fiber shows $$\mathsf H(O)+\tfrac12\mathsf H(O\mid D)+\tfrac32\mathbb E\log_{1/\epsilon}\!\left(m_O\right)
 \le \mathsf H(Z)+\tfrac12\mathsf H(Z\mid D)+\tfrac32\mathbb E\log_{1/\epsilon}\!\left(m_Z\right).
 \label{eq:packet-coarsen-mass}$$ For clarity, the unconditional log-sum inequality bounds $\mathsf H(O\mid Z)+\mathbb E\log_{1/\epsilon}\!\left(m_O/m_Z\right)$ by zero; the same conditional on $(Z,D)$, using a sum over a subset of the fiber, bounds its conditional counterpart by zero. Their sum with coefficients one and one half is precisely the displayed inequality.

<a id="eq:packet-contributor-mass"></a>
Let $\mathcal T_Z$ consist of all class atoms compatible with $P$ up to the enlargement in <a href="#eq:packet-transport" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:packet-transport">[eq:packet-transport]</a>. The earlier position uncertainty and the endpoint velocity uncertainty change these coarse columns by at most $C\epsilon^{-\eta}\epsilon^a$, since $a\le u_t\le u_0$. Discarding interactions outside $\mathcal T_Z$ is permitted by the quantitative tail lemma. After fixing the coefficient cutoff $B$, increase only the transport integration order so its error exponent $A_{\rm tr}$ also permits summation over this fiber and comparison to that coefficient floor. This does not require another coefficient truncation. Bessel at the fixed time $C_t$ then gives $$m_Z\le C\epsilon^{-\xi}m\,\#\mathcal T_Z
 \label{eq:packet-contributor-mass}$$ after absorbing those tails. More explicitly, before absorption the right hand side has an added term $C_{A_{\rm tr}}\epsilon^{2A_{\rm tr}-Q}\|f\|_2^2$; choosing $2A_{\rm tr}-Q>B+1$, and then reducing $\epsilon_0$, absorbs it whenever $\mathcal T_Z\ne\varnothing$. The output floor excludes a nonempty retained fiber with no potential contributor. The constant in <a href="#eq:packet-contributor-mass" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:packet-contributor-mass">[eq:packet-contributor-mass]</a> also absorbs the fixed factor from squaring the sum of a main term and its error.

<a id="eq:packet-contributor-identity"></a>
Only now introduce a positive auxiliary law: keep the given law of $(Z,D)$, and choose $T$ uniformly in $\mathcal T_Z$, independently of $D$ conditional on $Z$. Exactly, $$\mathsf H(T\mid Z,D)=\mathsf H(T\mid Z)
  =\mathbb E\log_{1/\epsilon}\!\left(\#\mathcal T_Z\right).$$ The chain rule gives the contributor calculation $$\begin{aligned}
 &\mathsf H(Z)+\tfrac12\mathsf H(Z\mid D)
                      +\tfrac32\mathsf H(T\mid Z)\nonumber\\
 &=\mathsf H(T)+\tfrac12\mathsf H(T\mid D)
                  +\mathsf H(Z\mid T)+\tfrac12\mathsf H(Z\mid T,D)\nonumber\\
 &\le\mathsf H(T)+\tfrac12\mathsf H(T\mid D)+\mathsf H(C_t\mid T)
                     +\tfrac32\mathsf H(Z\mid T,C_t).
 \label{eq:packet-contributor-identity}
\end{aligned}$$ Here $C_t$ is determined by both $Z$ and $D$. Thus $\mathsf H(Z\mid T)=\mathsf H(C_t\mid T)+\mathsf H(Z\mid T,C_t)$, and $\mathsf H(Z\mid T,D)\le\mathsf H(Z\mid T,C_t)$. This keeps exactly one conditional time entropy. The remaining term measures the uncertainty in the coarse observation after the contributor and time are known.

<a id="eq:packet-trivial-identity"></a>
In the present root-referred observation, $(T,C_t)$ locates $Z$ to at most $C\epsilon^{-C\eta}$ possibilities. Hence $\mathsf H(Z\mid T,C_t)\le C\eta+O(1/\ell)$. Combining <a href="#eq:packet-contributor-identity" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:packet-contributor-identity">[eq:packet-contributor-identity]</a> with <a href="#eq:packet-contributor-mass" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:packet-contributor-mass">[eq:packet-contributor-mass]</a> yields $$\mathsf H(Z)+\tfrac12\mathsf H(Z\mid D)+\tfrac32\mathbb E\log_{1/\epsilon}\!\left(m_Z\right)
 \le\mathsf H(T)+\tfrac32\log_{1/\epsilon}\!\left(m\right)+
       \tfrac12\mathsf H(T\mid D)+\mathsf H(C_t\mid T)+e_{\rm pkt}.
 \label{eq:packet-trivial-identity}$$

For a fixed aperture label $D$, its potential contributors lie in a $\epsilon^{-C\eta}$ enlargement of the root aperture of widths $(b,a)$ obtained by referring its rectangles back to $C_0$. The velocity error is at most $C\rho_t$; the position error is at most $C\epsilon^{-\eta}\sigma_0+C\rho_t$. Both are bounded by the corresponding enlarged coarse widths, because $a\le u_t$. Covering this enlargement and applying <a href="#eq:packet-cap-count" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:packet-cap-count">[eq:packet-cap-count]</a> gives $$\mathsf H(T\mid D)\le g-\mathbb Ew(D)+e_{\rm pkt},\qquad
 \mathsf H(T)\le\log_{1/\epsilon}\!\left(N\right),\qquad
 \mathsf H(C_t\mid T)\le t+O(1/\ell).$$ Adding the half-weight to <a href="#eq:packet-trivial-identity" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:packet-trivial-identity">[eq:packet-trivial-identity]</a> therefore bounds the conditional endpoint score by $A_J+t+e_{\rm pkt}$. Restoring $J$ adds $\mathsf H(J)$, with the recorded tag error; here $b_*=0$. Proposition <a href="#prop:local-root-comparison" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="prop:local-root-comparison">39</a> at $r=0$ gives $$P_t\le\mathsf H(J)+\mathbb EA_J+t+e_{\rm pkt}
 \le K_0+t+2e_{\rm pkt},$$ because $N\le N_{\rm all}$. First take $\epsilon\to0$ at fixed depths, $\eta,\xi$ and integration orders, then send $\eta,\xi\to0$. This proves $\beta_{\mathrm q}\le1$. ◻

</details>

<a id="sec:packet-composition"></a>
### Finite packet composition and the uncertainty boundary

The packet decomposition gives two different comparisons at an earlier time: an upper bound for the root score of a retained superposition, and a lower bound obtained by testing the original input on the whole cap class. Keeping these comparisons separate is essential. We first give a finite version of their composition, including the loss when the class is subsequently restricted.

<a id="pm-h-52"></a>
#### An error budget and a finite composition inequality

Write $\ell=\log(1/\epsilon)$; all entropies and all logarithms denoted by $\log_{1/\epsilon}\!\left(\cdot\right)$ in this section are divided by $\ell$. A fixed collection of bounds $\mathcal B$ will specify bounded ranges for $H_{\mathrm P},L,t,r$, bounded spatial and velocity domains, the phase and amplitude bounds, and a positive lower bound for each time gap to which a growth estimate is applied. In particular, $\mathcal B$ is fixed before $\epsilon$ tends to zero. Its size may change in a later outer sequence.

For an array of conditional systems these bounds, all grid and observation-count bounds, and every vanishing-error envelope are common deterministic bounds for the whole array. This condition is preserved here: the translated phase bounds are uniform over the localizers, the velocity supports are cut into a fixed bounded domain, and a single truncation order, coefficient threshold, depth mesh, and tag-count bound are used for every retained $J$. Thus every selection of one conditional system at each precision is an admissible sequence with the same bounds. Individual extendibility to unspecified vanishing-error envelopes would not suffice.

<a id="eq:packet-universal-modulus"></a>
There is a useful precise way of using the definition of $\beta_{\mathrm q}$. For systems obeying $\mathcal B$, let $$\label{eq:packet-universal-modulus}
 \omega_{\mathcal B}(\epsilon)
 =\sup\bigl(P_d-K_0-\beta_{\mathrm q}d\bigr)_+,$$ where the supremum also includes the bounded translated systems in Lemma <a href="#lem:packet-decomposition" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:packet-decomposition">37</a>, and $d$ ranges over the prescribed compact subset of $(0,\infty)$. Enlarging the fixed bounds slightly to accommodate rounded grids is understood. Then $\omega_{\mathcal B}(\epsilon)\to0$. Indeed, a failure would select a sequence of admissible systems with a fixed positive excess; a subsequence of their depth parameters converges, contradicting the definition of $\beta_{\mathrm q}$. This is a modulus for a fixed class, not a modulus uniform over growing values of $\mathcal B$. At duration zero the corresponding estimate is the definition of $K_0$, with zero error.

<a id="eq:composition-mass-floor"></a>
<a id="eq:composition-error-budget"></a>
Here is one error budget that will be used below. Choose a depth mesh $\xi>0$, a packet enlargement exponent $\eta>0$, and let $S_\epsilon\ge2$ bound the number of auxiliary choices at a localizer: shape bins, mass bins, cap-class tags, winning tags, and any prescribed further subdivisions. The geometric localizer itself is *not* one of these choices; its entropy will be kept. On the output tests under consideration assume $$\label{eq:composition-mass-floor}
 m_O\ge\epsilon^{A_0}\norm{f}_2^2.$$ Take the order of the packet truncation large enough that its amplitude error is at most $C_A\epsilon^A\norm{f}_2$, with $A>A_0/2$, and put $$q_\epsilon=C_A\epsilon^{A-A_0/2}<\tfrac12.$$ For a sufficiently large fixed $C_{\mathcal B}$, we may use $$\label{eq:composition-error-budget}
 \mathcal R=
 C_{\mathcal B}(\eta+\xi+\log_{1/\epsilon}\!\left(S_\epsilon\right))
 +C_{\mathcal B,\eta,\xi,A}
       \frac{1+\log(2+\ell)}{\ell}
 +3\log_{1/\epsilon}\!\left(\frac 1{1-q_\epsilon}\right)
 +\omega_{\mathcal B}(\epsilon).$$ Each occurrence below of a fixed enlargement of $\mathcal B$ is included in this choice. One may instead use the sum of the separate error bounds in Lemmas <a href="#lem:packet-decomposition" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:packet-decomposition">37</a> and <a href="#lem:cap-class" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:cap-class">38</a> and Proposition <a href="#prop:local-root-comparison" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="prop:local-root-comparison">39</a>; only their upper bound by $\mathcal R$ is needed.

With $S=S_\epsilon$ and $q=q_\epsilon$, the winner estimate <a href="#eq:packet-winner-mass" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:packet-winner-mass">[eq:packet-winner-mass]</a> gives the two contributions $3\log_{1/\epsilon}\!\left(S_\epsilon\right)$ and $3\log_{1/\epsilon}\!\left(1/(1-q_\epsilon)\right)$ to the loss in the score’s mass term. Its argument uses only $q_\epsilon<1/2$, so the present choice $A>A_0/2$ suffices. The other terms in <a href="#eq:composition-error-budget" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:composition-error-budget">[eq:composition-error-budget]</a> cover the tag entropies, cap enlargement and binning, bounded grid ambiguities, and the logarithmically growing root cutoff.

The floor also preserves saturation. After normalizing $\norm{f}_2=1$, the calculation at <a href="#eq:packet-output-floor" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:packet-output-floor">[eq:packet-output-floor]</a>, with the fixed weight bound from $\mathcal B$, lets us choose $A_0$ so that every low-mass law has score below $-1$, whereas $K_0\ge0$. The two-part split costs at most $3\log 2/(2\ell)$. For $\beta_{\mathrm q}>0$, the low-mass probability therefore tends to zero on a saturating sequence, and the complementary conditional law still saturates.

<a id="stmt-prop-finite-packet-composition"></a>
<div id="prop:finite-packet-composition" class="proposition">

<a id="eq:composition-A"></a>
**Proposition 41** (Finite packet composition). *Fix $0\le r<t$, a shape $0\le b\le a\le\min(L-t,u_t)$, and $0\le b_*\le b$. Choose $0<\eta<(u_r-b_*)/4$, and make the decomposition and cap-class construction of Section <a href="#sec:packet-structure" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:packet-structure">9</a>, with the mass floor <a href="#eq:composition-mass-floor" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:composition-mass-floor">[eq:composition-mass-floor]</a>. Within the localizer $J$, including its auxiliary tags, let $N_{\rm all}(J)$ be the size of the whole cap class, $N(J)>0$ its retained size, $m(J)$ its coefficient mass bin, and $g(J)$ its cap maximum bin. Set <a id="eq:composition-Kstar"></a>$$\begin{aligned}
 A_J&=\log_{1/\epsilon}\!\left(N(J)\right)+\tfrac32\log_{1/\epsilon}\!\left(m(J)\right)+\tfrac12g(J),
       \label{eq:composition-A}\\
 K_r^*&=\mathsf H(J)+b_*+
       \mathbb E\left[\log_{1/\epsilon}\!\left(N_{\rm all}(J)\right)
                    +\tfrac32\log_{1/\epsilon}\!\left(m(J)\right)+\tfrac12g(J)\right].
       \label{eq:composition-Kstar}
\end{aligned}$$ Let $K_J$ denote the canonical local root score, including its norm option, for the retained local superposition. Let $P_J$ be its score at duration $t-r$, with the conditional output law and the winning superposition masses. All expectations here use the current marginal of $J$ after the indicated preliminary split.*

<a id="eq:four-packet-deficits"></a>
<a id="eq:finite-packet-deficits"></a>
<a id="eq:retained-back-score"></a>
*With $\mathcal R$ as in <a href="#eq:composition-error-budget" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:composition-error-budget">[eq:composition-error-budget]</a>, enlarged by a fixed constant if necessary, the following four quantities are nonnegative: $$\begin{aligned}
 d_0&=K_0+\beta_{\mathrm q}r-K_r^*+2\mathcal R,\nonumber\\
 d_1(J)&=\log_{1/\epsilon}\!\left(N_{\rm all}(J)/N(J)\right),\nonumber\\
 d_2(J)&=A_J-K_J+\mathcal R,\nonumber\\
 d_3(J)&=K_J+\beta_{\mathrm q}(t-r)-P_J+\mathcal R.
       \label{eq:four-packet-deficits}
\end{aligned}$$ Up to the displayed error allowances, these are the deficits in growth before the cut, class retention, the local root comparison, and growth after the cut. The next inequality shows that saturation at the endpoint forces these four comparisons to be nearly sharp on average; the subsequent selection estimate specifies the branches on which this remains true. Writing $\Delta_t=K_0+\beta_{\mathrm q}t-P_t$, one has the finite bound $$\label{eq:finite-packet-deficits}
 d_0+\mathbb E(d_1+d_2+d_3)\le\Delta_t+5\mathcal R.$$ There is also an earlier test on the *retained uniform classes*, with that same current marginal of $J$ and the assigned cap labels, whose score satisfies $$\label{eq:retained-back-score}
 P_r^{\rm ret}\ge K_r^*
              -\tfrac32\mathbb Ed_1-\mathcal R.$$ At $r=0$ this is an actual test for the original canonical $K_0$; the norm option is not used in this lower bound.*

<a id="eq:packet-typical-selection"></a>
*More quantitatively, put $R_t=\Delta_t+5\mathcal R$. For an event $B$ measurable in $J$ with probability $p>0$ and any $\theta>0$, $$\label{eq:packet-typical-selection}
 \mathbb P\bigl(B\cap\{d_1+d_2+d_3>\theta\}\bigr)
       \le R_t/\theta.$$ In particular, taking $\theta=2R_t/p$ leaves at least $p/2$ of the current probability in $B$, and bounds each of the three local deficits by $2R_t/p$. If $R_t=0$, all three vanish almost surely.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-prop-finite-packet-composition"><summary>Proof of stmt-prop-finite-packet-composition</summary>

<a id="eq:finite-packet-split"></a>
*Proof.* The localizer consists geometrically of $C_r$, velocity at depth $b_*$, and position transported to $C_r$ at depth $r+b_*$. It is determined by both the endpoint observation and its aperture, up to the grid ambiguities already charged in $\mathcal R$. The phase and input rescaling in <a href="#eq:packet-rescale-coordinates" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:packet-rescale-coordinates">[eq:packet-rescale-coordinates]</a>–<a href="#eq:packet-rescaled-parameters" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:packet-rescaled-parameters">[eq:packet-rescaled-parameters]</a> give local Planck depth $H_{\mathrm P}-r-2b_*$ and horizon $L-r-b_*$. The returning aperture weight gains $2b_*$. Entropy chain rules and the winning-class estimate consequently give $$\label{eq:finite-packet-split}
 P_t\le\mathsf H(J)+b_*+\mathbb EP_J+\mathcal R.$$ Here the potentially large entropy $\mathsf H(J)$ has not been discarded. Only the extra ambiguity and choice tags have been charged to $\mathcal R$.

Proposition <a href="#prop:local-root-comparison" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="prop:local-root-comparison">39</a> gives $K_J\le A_J+\mathcal R$. Its whole-class earlier test gives $P_r^{\rm all}\ge K_r^*-\mathcal R$. The universal estimates $$P_r^{\rm all}\le K_0+\beta_{\mathrm q}r+\mathcal R,
 \qquad P_J\le K_J+\beta_{\mathrm q}(t-r)+\mathcal R$$ hold uniformly in $J$ by <a href="#eq:packet-universal-modulus" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:packet-universal-modulus">[eq:packet-universal-modulus]</a>. For $r=0$ the first is instead the exact inequality $P_0^{\rm all}\le K_0$. These facts prove nonnegativity in <a href="#eq:four-packet-deficits" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:four-packet-deficits">[eq:four-packet-deficits]</a>. Moreover, direct cancellation yields $$d_0+\mathbb E(d_1+d_2+d_3)
 =K_0+\beta_{\mathrm q}t-\mathsf H(J)-b_*-\mathbb EP_J+4\mathcal R.$$ Using <a href="#eq:finite-packet-split" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:finite-packet-split">[eq:finite-packet-split]</a> proves <a href="#eq:finite-packet-deficits" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:finite-packet-deficits">[eq:finite-packet-deficits]</a>. Markov’s inequality gives <a href="#eq:packet-typical-selection" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:packet-typical-selection">[eq:packet-typical-selection]</a>.

For clarity, the retained-class assertion has a finite proof that does not assume that every assigned fiber retains a fixed proportion. Fix $J$. Write $n_e$ and $r_e$ for the full and retained sizes of the fiber assigned to cap $e$, and $P_E,Q_E$ for the assigned-cap laws under the uniform full and retained populations. Terms with $r_e=0$ are omitted. The exact identity <a id="eq:retained-fiber-relative-entropy"></a>$$\label{eq:retained-fiber-relative-entropy}
 \mathbb E_{Q_E}\log_{1/\epsilon}\!\left(\frac{n_E}{r_E}\right)
  =\log_{1/\epsilon}\!\left(\frac{N_{\rm all}}{N}\right)
        -\frac{\mathop{\mathrm{KL}}(Q_E\Vert P_E)}{\ell}
  \le d_1(J)$$ and the assigned-fiber estimate $\log_{1/\epsilon}\!\left(n_e\right)+w(e)\ge g-\mathcal R$ show that $$\mathsf H_{\rm ret}(T\mid E)+\mathbb E_{\rm ret}w(E)
       \ge g-d_1(J)-\mathcal R.$$ The ordinary earlier entropy is $\log_{1/\epsilon}\!\left(N\right)$, and the coefficient mass exponent is $\log_{1/\epsilon}\!\left(m\right)$ up to the bin error. Returning to the original coordinates and allowing the bounded multiplicities gives <a href="#eq:retained-back-score" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:retained-back-score">[eq:retained-back-score]</a>; increasing the fixed constant in $\mathcal R$ absorbs its several geometric uses. The coefficient tests at $r=0$ are bounded by the canonical root tests, so the last assertion follows as well. ◻

</details>

<a id="pm-h-53"></a>
#### What saturation permits one to select

<a id="stmt-def-packet-saturation-array"></a>
<div id="def:packet-saturation-array" class="definition">

**Definition 42** (Successive saturation arrays). After normalizing duration to one, a saturation array consists of rows indexed by $j$, with small parameters $\epsilon_{j,n}\downarrow0$ within each row. Row $j$ obeys one fixed collection of analytic, domain, and depth bounds $\mathcal B_j$, and, for numbers $\Delta_j\downarrow0$, $$\limsup_{n\to\infty}
 \bigl(K_{0,j,n}+\beta_{\mathrm q}-P_{1,j,n}\bigr)\le\Delta_j.$$ The corresponding lower limit is nonnegative by the universal bound for that row. Bounds $\mathcal B_j$ may grow with $j$; the outer array is not asserted to be one admissible small-parameter sequence. All uses of a universal modulus are made in a fixed row, before the outer limit. For a finite construction, its mesh and truncation parameters are chosen within row $j$ before the inner precision; their limiting error budget can be prescribed as $\eta_j\downarrow0$. Such arrays exist by the definition of $\beta_{\mathrm q}$: choose a family with limiting rate within $1/j$ of the supremum, pass to a subsequence realizing that rate, and normalize its duration.

</div>

In the remainder of the packet argument, saturation and its successive limits have this meaning. The class of arrays includes the arrays obtained by the finite selections and fixed positive duration normalizations below. Here is the relevant closure justification. At a fixed cut, the four nonnegative composition deficits have total mean at most $\Delta_j+o_n(1)$ plus the chosen finite error budget. On any event of mass at least a fixed $p_0>0$, their conditional mean is bounded by this quantity divided by $p_0$. Markov selection therefore gives conditional local families whose outer deficits tend to zero. They obey fixed enlarged bounds $\mathcal B'_j$ within each row, independently of which localizer is selected. The earlier test retains its full selected localizer marginal and has the same conclusion by the retained-score inequality.

For each row, make only finitely many cuts with fixed positive gaps. Depth and score units have been divided by the initial duration. Then choose the depth meshes, packet enlargement exponents, and the permitted exponent of the additional tag count as small as required. Choose the truncation order after the mass floor and these parameters; finally choose $\epsilon$ small enough for <a href="#eq:composition-error-budget" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:composition-error-budget">[eq:composition-error-budget]</a> and all of the finitely many universal moduli to have the required size. Equivalently one may take the inner $\epsilon\to0$ limits first, then send the mesh and enlargement parameters to zero, and only afterwards take the outer extremizing sequence. No estimate here requires uniformity as $H_{\mathrm P}$, the aspect, or the phase bounds grow in that outer sequence.

If $\Delta_t\to0$ in this order, all four nonnegative deficits vanish in the sense of <a href="#eq:finite-packet-deficits" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:finite-packet-deficits">[eq:finite-packet-deficits]</a>. In particular $K_J=A_J+o(1)$ and $P_J=K_J+\beta_{\mathrm q}(t-r)+o(1)$ on selected typical conditional systems. The retained earlier law has deficit tending to zero by <a href="#eq:retained-back-score" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:retained-back-score">[eq:retained-back-score]</a>. To be explicit, its deficit is at most $$d_0+\tfrac32\mathbb Ed_1+\mathcal R
       \le\tfrac32 R_t+\mathcal R.$$ For this earlier test one keeps the whole marginal on $J$. Selecting a single value of $J$ is appropriate when testing a local growth bound, and does not replace that marginal in the earlier test.

Further splitting has an equally finite justification. If a label $B$ takes at most $S$ values, the score of a law and the average scores of its conditional laws differ by at most $\tfrac32\mathsf H(B)\le3\log_{1/\epsilon}\!\left(S\right)/2$; this follows directly from the two entropy terms in the packet score. The input and its canonical root score are the same in these comparisons. Add the uniform growth error to make the conditional deficits nonnegative, and use Markov’s inequality. Thus a split made *before* composition preserves saturation on typical branches, also within any event whose probability is bounded below. For an event of probability $p$ tending to zero, the required condition is explicitly that the available deficit and error be $o(p)$; subpower probability by itself is not this condition. More generally, if a sum of nonnegative shifted deficits has mean $D$, its mean on a current event of probability $p$ is at most $D/p$; outside a set of relative probability at most $q$ there, the sum is at most $D/(pq)$ pointwise. Polynomially many geometric localizers are handled by retaining their entropy, rather than by declaring the cost of fixing one negligible. The conditional local estimate, on the other hand, is pointwise and uniform in the inner limit, so a violating local system can always be selected without a probability loss argument.

One can also specify the probability of a chosen tag. If a union of tag branches has probability $p$, discard tags of probability below $p/(4S)$, losing at most $p/4$. If their total nonnegative shifted deficit is at most $R$, discard branches with conditional deficit greater than $4R/p$, losing at most another $p/4$. Some remaining tag has probability at least $p/(4S)$ and conditional deficit at most $4R/p$. Its logarithmic retention cost is at most $\log_{1/\epsilon}\!\left(4S/p\right)$. For fixed $p>0$ and $\log_{1/\epsilon}\!\left(S\right)\to0$, this is a subpower retention with a quantified deficit. Apply composition anew on that tag, keeping its marginal on $J$ for the earlier test. Repeating this argument a fixed number of times gives, for any prescribed accuracy $\vartheta>0$, a branch on which the endpoint deficit, the mean retained-count loss, the local root comparison deficit, the earlier retained-law deficit, and the upper error in each specified admissible score-replacement comparison are all at most $\vartheta$. For the last assertion, the universal bound for a competing endpoint test gives $P_t^{\rm new}-P_t\le\Delta_t+\omega_{\mathcal B}$. Here $p$ is the probability of the relevant event in the current normalized law. The displayed simultaneous selection divides the mean deficit by $p$, not by the probability of the individual tag; it requires no estimate of the form $R=o(1/S)$. For a subsequent event, apply the same rule to its probability in the then current law and choose the incoming errors accordingly. Thus a finite subsequent argument may use $\vartheta$ to denote the maximum of these selected errors; it need not identify it with the original unsplit deficit.

These rules also apply to any fixed finite list of observations and cuts, using the sum of their errors and a union bound. They concern score differences. They do not require the separate scores to have finite outer limits, or a uniform differentiability modulus for any limiting entropy profile.

<a id="pm-h-54"></a>
#### Faithful classical tests away from the boundary

<a id="stmt-lem-packet-boundary-slack"></a>
<div id="lem:packet-boundary-slack" class="lemma">

<a id="eq:active-packet-boundary"></a>
<a id="eq:off-boundary-finite-growth"></a>
**Lemma 43** (Exclusion of a fixed uncertainty slack). *Assume Theorem <a href="#thm:classical-growth" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:classical-growth">15</a> and $\beta_{\mathrm q}>\gamma/2$. A saturating packet law at any fixed positive duration has $$\label{eq:active-packet-boundary}
 a=u_t+o(1)$$ on its typical fixed-shape branches. More precisely, if $r=t-2h>0$ and $a+2h\le u_r-2\eta$, the construction above with $b_*=b$ gives $$\label{eq:off-boundary-finite-growth}
 P_t\le K_0+\beta_{\mathrm q}r+\gamma h
              +C\mathcal R+\tfrac12\omega^{\rm cl}_{\mathcal B}(\epsilon).$$ Here $\omega^{\rm cl}_{\mathcal B}\to0$ is the fixed-class error in the classical growth theorem, and the constant is fixed for this cut.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-lem-packet-boundary-slack"><summary>Proof of stmt-lem-packet-boundary-slack</summary>

*Proof.* Work within $J$ and use the earlier retained grid centers to define exact lines with velocities $V_T$ and positions $X_T$ at $C_r$. Coarsen the output to the isotropic observation $Z$ of velocity depths $a,a$, position depths $a+t,a+t$, and time label $C_t$. Let $\mathcal T_z$ consist of retained atoms compatible, under <a href="#eq:packet-transport" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:packet-transport">[eq:packet-transport]</a>, with at least one output in the $z$-fiber.

The earlier position tolerance is $C\epsilon^{-\eta}\epsilon^{r+u_r}$. Since $r=t-2h$, the hypotheses give $$\epsilon^{r+u_r-\eta}\le\epsilon^{a+t+\eta},
 \qquad \rho_t=\epsilon^{u_t}\le\epsilon^a.$$ Thus a fixed contributor and time locate $Z$ up to the ambiguities charged in $\mathcal R$. They also give the compatibility needed for positive transport after sampling. For every $T\in\mathcal T_z$ and every $D$ occurring over $Z=z$, choose an output $O_D$ paired with $D$ and an output $O_T$ compatible with $T$ in that fiber. They are in the same isotropic $z$-cell. The displayed tolerances therefore put the exact line and $O_D$ within $C\epsilon^a$ in velocity and $C\epsilon^{a+t}$ in position at $C_t$. These isotropic widths fit both axes of the rectangles of $D$. Use a fixed enlargement of those rectangles as the aperture represented by the same label $D$, at the same depths. The enlarged aperture is faithful for every such pair, as permitted by Definition <a href="#def:classical-aperture" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="def:classical-aperture">14</a>.

First sum the winning coherent masses over each $Z$. Bessel and the separately chosen transport-tail order give $$m_Z\le\epsilon^{-C\mathcal R}m\,\#\mathcal T_Z,$$ with the tails absorbed by the coefficient and output floors as in the proof of Proposition <a href="#prop:packet-trivial-growth" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="prop:packet-trivial-growth">40</a>. Only after this bound, keep the given law of $(Z,D)$ and choose $T$ uniformly in $\mathcal T_Z$, independently of $D$ given $Z$. The reverse determination above gives $\mathsf H(Z\mid T,C_t)\le C\mathcal R$ under this law. Equations <a href="#eq:packet-coarsen-mass" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:packet-coarsen-mass">[eq:packet-coarsen-mass]</a> and <a href="#eq:packet-contributor-identity" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:packet-contributor-identity">[eq:packet-contributor-identity]</a>, with the displayed mass bound, now give $$P_J\le\mathsf H(T)+\tfrac32\log_{1/\epsilon}\!\left(m\right)+
 \tfrac12\left[
    \mathsf H(T\mid D)+w_{\rm loc}(D)+2\mathsf H(C_t\mid T)
 \right]+C\mathcal R.$$

The classical horizon is $a-b+2h$. Its root cap menu fits the local packet menu: $a+2h\le u_r$ and $a+t\le L$ are precisely the required upper bounds after subtracting $b$ and $r$. For every root test $F$, cap counting gives $$\mathsf H(T\mid F)+\mathbb Ew(F)\le g+C\mathcal R,
 \qquad \tau(T)\le g-\mathsf H(T)+C\mathcal R.$$ This support bound holds for the possibly biased contributor marginal on $T$. Theorem <a href="#thm:classical-growth" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:classical-growth">15</a>, applied to the exact lines and the faithful enlarged aperture represented by $D$, gives $$\mathsf H(T\mid D)+w_{\rm loc}(D)+2\mathsf H(C_t\mid T)
 \le g+2\gamma h+C\mathcal R+
                       \omega^{\rm cl}_{\mathcal B}(\epsilon).$$ Since $\mathsf H(T)\le\log_{1/\epsilon}\!\left(N\right)$, we get $P_J\le A_J+\gamma h+C\mathcal R+
\omega^{\rm cl}_{\mathcal B}/2$. The whole-class earlier comparison and the finite split give <a href="#eq:off-boundary-finite-growth" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:off-boundary-finite-growth">[eq:off-boundary-finite-growth]</a>.

If $u_t-a$ had a fixed positive lower bound on a saturating branch, choose a fixed $h<t/2$ smaller than half that bound, and then choose $\eta$ smaller still. Let the finite errors tend to zero in the specified order. Equation <a href="#eq:off-boundary-finite-growth" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:off-boundary-finite-growth">[eq:off-boundary-finite-growth]</a> contradicts the positive gap $(2\beta_{\mathrm q}-\gamma)h$. ◻

</details>

<a id="pm-h-55"></a>
#### The two ways to continue backwards

<a id="eq:forced-root-gap"></a>
For a packet system write $K_0^{\ge u_0-\nu}$ for the supremum of its *actual root aperture scores* with smaller width $b\ge u_0-\nu$, excluding the total norm option. Call a duration-one saturation array in the sense of Definition <a href="#def:packet-saturation-array" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="def:packet-saturation-array">42</a> *forced at the root* if there are fixed $\nu,\kappa>0$ and an outer subsequence of rows on which $$\label{eq:forced-root-gap}
 K_0^{\ge u_0-\nu}\le K_0-\kappa$$ in each row’s inner limit. The quantifier ranges over all such saturation arrays, including arrays of normalized conditional systems. Thus the negation excludes a forced array obtained by selecting and rescaling local systems as well as an originally chosen one.

The constants $\nu,\kappa>0$ must be fixed across an outer subsequence of rows, with the asserted gap holding in each row’s inner limit (and with a smaller fixed gap if necessary). A window or gap tending to zero with the row index does not constitute a forced array. In the forced case the backward step $h$ is chosen once from these fixed constants and the fixed number of steps. In the absence of a forced array, a fixed cap excess at a fixed cut would produce one by the local-root comparison; hence the isotropic alternative applies with a step chosen once from its fixed time interval and the number of steps. In either case $h$ is fixed before $j\to\infty$, so the outer deficits are $o(h)$.

<a id="stmt-prop-boundary-alternatives"></a>
<div id="prop:boundary-alternatives" class="proposition">

**Proposition 44** (Boundary alternatives and finite chains). *Assume $\beta_{\mathrm q}>\gamma/2$. For every fixed integer $q\ge1$ and every fixed $M>0$, a saturation array approaching $\beta_{\mathrm q}$ admits $q$ successive backward cuts at times $$t_j=t_0-2jh>0\quad(0\le j\le q),\qquad u_{t_j}>h,$$ with $h>0$ fixed in the inner limits, satisfying one of the following alternatives.*

1.  *A forced array exists. One can use the same such array, choose a fixed $\nu>0$ from <a href="#eq:forced-root-gap" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:forced-root-gap">[eq:forced-root-gap]</a>, and take all the times early enough that the saturated tests satisfy $$a_j=u_{t_j}+o(1),\qquad
     a_j-b_j\ge\nu/2+o(1),\qquad
     a_j-b_j\ge M h/\gamma+o(1).$$ Every cut uses $b_*=b_j$ at its later endpoint.*

2.  *No forced saturation array exists. At all the indicated times one can use exact isotropic boundary tests $a_j=b_j=u_{t_j}$, and every cut uses $b_*=0$.*

*These assertions remain valid when a prescribed finite number of subdivisions with vanishing tag cost are made at each step, before the earlier test is constructed. In particular the earlier law is uniform on the retained classes produced by those subdivisions. For any prescribed positive accuracy, all the assertions about saturation hold at sufficiently small finite precision with that accuracy; the required precision can depend on the outer bounds, $q,h,\nu,M$, the subdivision costs, and the selected branch.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-prop-boundary-alternatives"><summary>Proof of stmt-prop-boundary-alternatives</summary>

*Proof.* Suppose first that <a href="#eq:forced-root-gap" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:forced-root-gap">[eq:forced-root-gap]</a> holds. A saturated fixed-shape branch at a positive time cannot have $b\ge u_0-\nu$ with a fixed inward margin: composition down to $r=0$ with $b_*=b$ and <a href="#eq:retained-back-score" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:retained-back-score">[eq:retained-back-score]</a> gives actual root aperture scores arbitrarily close to $K_0$, all with smaller widths at least $b$. This contradicts <a href="#eq:forced-root-gap" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:forced-root-gap">[eq:forced-root-gap]</a>. Allowing the shape mesh to vanish gives $b\le u_0-\nu+o(1)$. By Lemma <a href="#lem:packet-boundary-slack" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:packet-boundary-slack">43</a>, for $t\le\nu$ this yields $$a-b\ge u_t-u_0+\nu+o(1)
          =\nu-t/2+o(1)\ge\nu/2+o(1).$$ Start with a backward subdivision of the duration-one extremizer to a time $0<t_0<\min(\nu,1/4)$. Finite composition supplies a saturated earlier test there. Choose $$0<h<\min\left(\frac{t_0}{2(q+1)},
                    \frac{\gamma\nu}{4(M+1)}\right).$$ Since the original normalized Planck depth is at least one, these early times also have $u_{t_j}>h$. Repeated composition gives the claimed chain. Its first two comparisons are reapplied after every prescribed split, so the argument uses the actual retained classes.

<a id="eq:isotropic-cap-maximum"></a>
<a id="eq:nearly-isotropic-root-bound"></a>
For the second alternative, consider a cut $0<r<t$ from a saturated law and take $b_*=0$. Equation <a href="#eq:active-packet-boundary" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:active-packet-boundary">[eq:active-packet-boundary]</a> implies $$L\ge u_t+t-o(1)=u_r+r+(t-r)/2-o(1).$$ Hence the local root packet menu contains the exact isotropic test of depth $v=u_r$. We show that, on selected saturating branches, $$\label{eq:isotropic-cap-maximum}
 g=2v+o(1).$$ A single atom fits an isotropic cap at the natural root packet scale, so the cap-count bound gives $g\ge2v-C\mathcal R$. For the reverse inequality fix $\zeta>0$ and consider an excess $g\ge2v+\zeta$. A root cap with smaller width at least $v-\alpha$ contains at most $C\epsilon^{-4\alpha-C\mathcal R}$ earlier sites. The pointwise canonical mass bound is $\epsilon^{-C\mathcal R}m$: the cross-Gram kernel at the common root packet scale has a uniformly bounded absolute row sum, and every coefficient has size at most $\epsilon^{-\xi/2}\sqrt m$. This estimate is uniform over the canonical test amplitude. The total canonical mass is at most $\epsilon^{-C\mathcal R}Nm$. The two log-sum inequalities for the root score consequently give $$\label{eq:nearly-isotropic-root-bound}
 K_J^{\ge v-\alpha}
 \le\log_{1/\epsilon}\!\left(N\right)+\tfrac32\log_{1/\epsilon}\!\left(m\right)+v+2\alpha+C\mathcal R.$$ This estimates actual aperture scores, not the norm option.

By <a href="#eq:finite-packet-deficits" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:finite-packet-deficits">[eq:finite-packet-deficits]</a>, typical local systems satisfy $K_J=A_J+o(1)$ and $P_J-K_J=\beta_{\mathrm q}(t-r)+o(1)$. If a fixed positive excess $\zeta$ persisted on such selected systems, choose $\alpha<\zeta/16$ and then make their composition errors small. Equations <a href="#eq:composition-A" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:composition-A">[eq:composition-A]</a> and <a href="#eq:nearly-isotropic-root-bound" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:nearly-isotropic-root-bound">[eq:nearly-isotropic-root-bound]</a> would give $$K_J-K_J^{\ge v-\alpha}\ge\zeta/4.$$ Normalizing these systems by their fixed positive duration $t-r$ produces a forced duration-one saturation array, with root-width window $\alpha/(t-r)$ and gap $\zeta/(4(t-r))$. This contradicts the hypothesis of the second alternative. This duration normalization divides the depth exponents by $t-r$. The frequency $\lambda$, and hence the root cutoff $1+\log\lambda$, is unchanged.

Here is the selection detail in this argument. One first splits on a $g$-bin common across the geometric localizers, along with the other required tag bins, and reapplies composition using its conditional deficit bounds and its full marginal on $J$. Equation <a href="#eq:packet-typical-selection" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:packet-typical-selection">[eq:packet-typical-selection]</a> permits selection within any excess event of probability bounded below; otherwise that excess event has probability tending to zero. Since $g\ge2v-C\mathcal R$, one may therefore retain a saturating branch on which $|g-2v|\le\zeta+C\mathcal R$, and subsequently send $\zeta$ to zero. Thus no passage through expectations of unbounded outer values of $g$ is being used.

On this branch the exact isotropic test at $r$, using the retained uniform classes, has score at least $$\begin{aligned}
 P_r^{\rm iso}
 &\ge\mathsf H(J)+
       \mathbb E\left[\log_{1/\epsilon}\!\left(N\right)+\tfrac32\log_{1/\epsilon}\!\left(m\right)+v\right]
                   -C\mathcal R\\
 &=K_r^*-\mathbb Ed_1-\tfrac12\mathbb E(g-2v)-C\mathcal R.
\end{aligned}$$ Its conditional entropy term is merely nonnegative; no assigned-fiber entropy gain is needed. Finite composition and <a href="#eq:isotropic-cap-maximum" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:isotropic-cap-maximum">[eq:isotropic-cap-maximum]</a> show that this score saturates at $r$. The same construction works for the first cut even if its later endpoint test was not isotropic. Make that first cut to an early $t_0<1/4$, choose $h<t_0/(2(q+1))$, and repeat.

Finally fix $q$ and the requested finite accuracy. At each of the finitely many selections take the current deficit and error small enough relative to its retained probability and the next requested accuracy, using <a href="#eq:packet-typical-selection" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:packet-typical-selection">[eq:packet-typical-selection]</a>; for an earlier test use <a href="#eq:retained-back-score" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:retained-back-score">[eq:retained-back-score]</a> or the displayed isotropic bound. Choose the inner precision only after these finitely many requirements have been imposed. This proves the stated finite approximation and its stability under the additional subdivisions. In the elongated alternative the orientation precision of an aperture is $\epsilon^{a_j-b_j}$; thus the asserted aspect lower bound supplies any fixed separation between this precision and $\epsilon^{h/\gamma}$ needed in the subsequent orientation argument. ◻

</details>

<a id="sec:packet-repayment"></a>
### Finite packet repayment and closure

We complete the proof of Theorem <a href="#thm:packet-growth" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:packet-growth">35</a> by a finite backward iteration. A cut of length $2h$ records the loss from coherent superposition as fine velocity information. At a growth rate $\beta_{\mathrm q}>\gamma/2$, the repayment estimate forces this quantity to increase at each cut by $(4\beta_{\mathrm q}-2\gamma)h$, up to the finite errors specified below, while its capacity is at most $2h$ up to those errors. A sufficiently long finite chain is therefore impossible. The information carried between cuts is encoded by a uniform conditional probability bound, so it can be retained through the subsequent branch selections.

Write $\ell=\log(1/\epsilon)$ and divide all entropies by $\ell$. We use the finite budget of Section <a href="#sec:packet-composition" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:packet-composition">10</a>: a conditional list of size $\epsilon^{-\alpha}$ costs $\alpha$, and a fixed factor $C$ costs $(\log C)/\ell$. Depth bins have width $\xi$, and packet tails are cut at distance $\epsilon^{-\theta}$ in earlier packet units, with $\theta<h/10$ at fixed depths and $h>0$. Constants $C_*$ count finitely many geometric and entropy losses, independently of the aspect exponents and cut locations. Fixed phase and amplitude constants enter through their logarithms divided by $\ell$. We may increase $C_*$ a finite number of times.

Figure <a href="#fig:packet-cells" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="fig:packet-cells">3</a> explains the mismatch between the earlier packet’s transported uncertainty and the output position precision. The fine velocity information below accounts for this mismatch.

<figure id="fig:packet-cells">

<figcaption>One coordinate pair of packet uncertainty cells at a common output anchor, with $0 < h ≤ t/2$, $t ≤ H_{P}$ and $u_{t} = (H_{P}−t)/2$. The earlier packet has $u_{r} = u_{t} + h$: its velocity cell is finer by depth $h$, while its transported position uncertainty is coarser by depth $h$. Both displayed rectangles have the same area, $ϵ^{u_{t} + h}ϵ^{u_{t} + t − h} = ϵ^{u_{t}}ϵ^{u_{t} + t} = ϵ^{H_{P}}$. The rectangles are drawn concentrically to compare their scales and represent comparable widths after transport; fixed factors, shear and subpower tail enlargements are suppressed. An earlier packet can therefore contribute across several fine output position cells. Its transported center alone does not determine the fine output position label.</figcaption>
</figure>

<a id="pm-h-57"></a>
#### The incoming fine-velocity information

Here is the precise meaning of the velocity information carried between steps. At time $t$, let $$u_t=(H_{\mathrm P}-t)/2,\qquad
 P_f=(C_t,\text{isotropic velocity and position cells of width }
                  \epsilon^{u_t-h}).$$ The position width in this formula is $\epsilon^{t+u_t-h}$. Fixed dilations and translations of the grids are allowed. Additional tags are allowed only if their conditional number, given the geometric part of $P_f$, is at most $\epsilon^{-\alpha}$; their cost is included in $\alpha$.

<a id="eq:incoming-packet-credit"></a>
In the elongated case $n_f(P_f)$ is a unit normal, modulo sign, and the normal of the aperture $D$ is within $C\epsilon^h$ of $n_f(P_f)$. The label $W_f$ locates the velocity component along $n_f(P_f)$ in intervals of length $\epsilon^{u_t}$. In the isotropic case $W_f$ locates both velocity components at that precision. An incoming credit $k_f\geq0$, with error $\alpha_f$, means that on the normalized law being used, $$\sup_w\mathbb P(W_f=w\mid P_f=p)\leq
       \epsilon^{\,k_f-\alpha_f}
       \quad\text{for every \(p\) of positive probability}.
 \label{eq:incoming-packet-credit}$$ In particular $\mathsf H(W_f\mid P_f)\geq k_f-\alpha_f$. On the first step we set $k_f=0$ and impose no incoming direction or fine-velocity condition.

We will use the following exact retention rule. It specifies how <a href="#eq:incoming-packet-credit" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:incoming-packet-credit">[eq:incoming-packet-credit]</a> is maintained when selecting branches.

<a id="stmt-lem-packet-credit-retention"></a>
<div id="lem:packet-credit-retention" class="lemma">

**Lemma 45** (Retention of a conditional probability bound). *Suppose a finite law satisfies $\mathbb P(W=w\mid P=p)\leq\epsilon^{k-\alpha}$. Let $A$ have probability $p_A>0$, and let $\zeta>0$. Under the law conditioned on $A$, the set of fibers on which $$\mathbb P(A\mid P)<p_A\epsilon^\zeta$$ has probability at most $\epsilon^\zeta$. On every remaining fiber, <a id="eq:credit-retention"></a>$$\mathbb P(W=w\mid P,A)\leq
   \epsilon^{\,k-\alpha-\zeta-\log_{1/\epsilon}\!\left(1/p_A\right)}.
 \label{eq:credit-retention}$$ Removing the exceptional fibers does not change this conditional bound. The same assertion holds when $P$ includes other previously fixed labels.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-lem-packet-credit-retention"><summary>Proof of stmt-lem-packet-credit-retention</summary>

*Proof.* The exceptional probability, in the conditioned law, is $$p_A^{-1}\sum_{\{p:\,\mathbb P(A\mid P=p)<p_A\epsilon^\zeta\}}
       \mathbb P(P=p)\mathbb P(A\mid P=p)\leq\epsilon^\zeta.$$ On a remaining fiber divide $\mathbb P(W=w,A\mid P=p)\leq\mathbb P(W=w\mid P=p)$ by $\mathbb P(A\mid P=p)$. Conditioning subsequently on a set of $P$ values does not alter the conditional law given $P$. ◻

</details>

Every removal below is also a score split under Section <a href="#sec:packet-composition" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:packet-composition">10</a>; its probability alone does not control the remaining score.

<a id="pm-h-58"></a>
#### Constructing the finite cut

A prepared cut starts with a boundary step from $r=t-2h>0$ to $t$, with $u_t>h$, as supplied by Proposition <a href="#prop:boundary-alternatives" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="prop:boundary-alternatives">44</a>. The current endpoint law will be denoted by $\pi^{\rm in}$. It is a probability law on a finite sample space $\Omega$. A sample $\omega$ records $O(\omega),D(\omega)$, all incoming labels $P_f,W_f$ and their extra tags when present, and any auxiliary randomness already used to choose those labels. In particular, an incoming label need not be a deterministic function of $(O,D)$. For any endpoint law $\nu$ on $\Omega$, write $P_t(\nu)$ for the score of the original input with its original masses. If $k_f>0$, the bound <a href="#eq:incoming-packet-credit" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:incoming-packet-credit">[eq:incoming-packet-credit]</a> holds under $\pi^{\rm in}$, with its current error. On the first step $k_f=0$.

<a id="eq:repayment-eccentricity"></a>
<a id="eq:repayment-localizer-depth"></a>
The finite geometry is the following. The endpoint shape has $a=u_t$ to depth error at most $\eta$. In the isotropic alternative the apertures are isotropic and $b_*=0$. In the elongated alternative $b_*=b$, the endpoint aspect $e=a-b$ is at least $e_0>0$. In that case require $$C_*(h+\eta)<\gamma e_0 .
 \label{eq:repayment-eccentricity}$$ The grids and aperture menu admit all coarsenings below. We take $C_*\ge2$. Thus in the elongated case $b\le u_t+\eta-e_0\le u_t-h$, after increasing $C_*$ if necessary; in the isotropic case $b_*=0<u_t-h$. We will use $$b_*\le u_t-h
 \label{eq:repayment-localizer-depth}$$ when comparing the incoming coarse label with the localizer.

Use the fixed analytic, domain, depth, grid, and count bounds of Section <a href="#sec:packet-composition" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:packet-composition">10</a>. For supremum masses, fix at each site a test within a fixed factor of the supremum and call its mass $m_O(f)$. This changes any endpoint score by at most $C/\ell$, included in $\mathcal R$, and the Bessel bounds are uniform in these choices. Apply the floor $m_O(f)\ge\epsilon^{A_0}\|f\|_2^2$ of <a href="#eq:packet-output-floor" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:packet-output-floor">[eq:packet-output-floor]</a> and the fixed-shape score splits, recording their probabilities for credit retention.

Fix the depths, then $\theta<h/10$ and $\xi$. By <a href="#eq:repayment-localizer-depth" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:repayment-localizer-depth">[eq:repayment-localizer-depth]</a>, $\theta<(u_r-b_*)/4$, as required by Lemma <a href="#lem:packet-decomposition" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:packet-decomposition">37</a>. Choose its amplitude error $C_A\epsilon^A\|f\|_2$ with $A>A_0/2+1$. If $Q_0$ bounds all relevant count exponents, choose the coefficient cutoff <a id="eq:repayment-coefficient-cutoff"></a>$$B>2A+3Q_0+10 .
 \label{eq:repayment-coefficient-cutoff}$$ uniformly over geometric localizers. The later transport order may be increased after this coefficient family is fixed.

For one geometric localizer $J_0$, let $\iota$ range over its coefficient bins and greedy cap classes. The associated whole class is a finite set $\mathcal T_\iota^{\rm all}$ of earlier atoms, with coefficient mass bin $m(\iota)$, cap maximum bin $g(\iota)$, and assigned cap $E_\iota(T)$. Lemma <a href="#lem:cap-class" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:cap-class">38</a> gives the cap upper bound on this set and the lower bound on each of its whole assigned fibers. At this point $\iota$ indexes available classes; no class has yet been assigned to an endpoint sample as its final winner. The buffer used next is chosen for all possible contributors in this finite family, before any of its classes is subdivided.

During preparation, a replacement loss is the increase in score when the aperture is changed at fixed masses, evaluated on the specified current marginal. Section <a href="#sec:packet-composition" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:packet-composition">10</a> supplies these losses from the current deficits and charges each split. This also applies to the two-copy marginals in the next lemma, since adjoining the unsplit conditional copies preserves the old marginal.

For every possible contributor, the velocity difference from its output center is $O(\epsilon^{u_t})$. After referring the positions to $C_r$, their difference is $$O(\epsilon^{r+u_t})+
 O(\epsilon^{-\theta}\epsilon^{r+u_r})
       =O(\epsilon^{r+u_t}),
 \qquad u_r=u_t+h,\quad \theta<h/10.$$ Use isotropic cells with side $L_{\rm grid}$ times $\epsilon^{u_t}$ in velocity and $\epsilon^{r+u_t}$ in position, where $L_{\rm grid}$ is a sufficiently large fixed constant. A uniformly random translation places any output center farther than these possible differences from every face with probability at least $3/4$. Averaging over translations therefore gives one translation for which a part of at least that probability has the coarse label $$P=(C_r,V_{u_t},(X+(C_r-C_t)V)_{r+u_t})$$ in common with every possible contributing earlier atom. Retain this part as a score split and denote its normalized endpoint law by $\pi^{\rm buf}$. Its probability and deficit are charged by the finite selection rule above. This completes the geometric preparation in the isotropic case.

<a id="stmt-lem-orientation-prediction"></a>
<div id="lem:orientation-prediction" class="lemma">

**Lemma 46** (Prediction of a normal from isotropic replacements). *Assume the elongated geometry. On $\pi^{\rm buf}$, suppose the replacement losses for the isotropic apertures of widths $a$ and $b$ are included in $C_*\eta$. Take two copies $(O,D),(O',D')$, independent conditional on $P$, and set $$A_{\rm sep}=\{\angle(n(D),n(D'))\ge\epsilon^{4h}\}.$$ If this event has probability at least $1/4$, require the same replacement bounds on both marginals of the law conditioned on $A_{\rm sep}$. Then there is a deterministic normal $n(P)$, defined on every coarse cell used by the atom partition, such that $$\angle(n(D),n(P))\le C\epsilon^{4h}$$ on a part of $\pi^{\rm buf}$-probability at least $3/4$.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-lem-orientation-prediction"><summary>Proof of stmt-lem-orientation-prediction</summary>

<a id="eq:prediction-lower"></a>
<a id="eq:prediction-upper"></a>
*Proof.* Let $e=a-b$, and let $B_P$ be the isotropic coarsening of $P$ to width $b$. Grid list errors will be included in $C_*\eta$. Only $2h$ extra depth for time and $2h$ for each position coordinate are missing from $P$ in order to specify $O$, so <a id="eq:prediction-missing-data"></a>$$\mathsf H(O\mid P)\leq6h+C_*\eta.
 \label{eq:prediction-missing-data}$$ Replacing $D$ by the isotropic aperture of width $a$ gives $$\mathsf H(P\mid D)\geq(1+\gamma)e-6h-C_*\eta.
 \label{eq:prediction-lower}$$ Indeed the weight increases by $(1+\gamma)e$, and the new conditional observation entropy is nonnegative. Replacing $D$ by the isotropic width-$b$ aperture at $t$, which has at most $6h+C_*\eta$ information beyond $B_P$, gives $$\mathsf I(P;D\mid B_P)\leq(1-\gamma)e+6h+C_*\eta.
 \label{eq:prediction-upper}$$ Both inequalities are comparisons on the marginal law on which they are invoked.

Suppose $A_{\rm sep}$ has probability at least $1/4$, and condition the two-copy law on this event. For the resulting law, conditional dependence of the two copies given $P$ is at most $\log(1/\mathbb P(A_{\rm sep}))/\ell\leq(\log4)/\ell$. This follows by comparing its density with the original conditional product and using the chain rule for relative entropy. The marginal replacement estimates <a href="#eq:prediction-lower" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:prediction-lower">[eq:prediction-lower]</a>–<a href="#eq:prediction-upper" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:prediction-upper">[eq:prediction-upper]</a> continue to hold with their charged conditional deficits.

<a id="eq:prediction-intersection"></a>
Each aperture, referred to $C_r$, constrains both columns to a normal strip of width a fixed multiple of $\epsilon^{a-C_*\eta}$. Two such strips whose normals have angle at least $\epsilon^{4h}$ have intersection of diameter at most $C\epsilon^{a-4h-C_*\eta}$. Covering both columns by $P$ cells consequently gives $$\mathsf H(P\mid D,D')\leq16h+C_*\eta.
 \label{eq:prediction-intersection}$$ Here a strip intersection is used separately for velocity and root position, each in two dimensions; hence $4(4h)=16h$. The coarse label $B_P$ has bounded ambiguity given either aperture. The identity $$\mathsf I(P;D'\mid D,B_P)-\mathsf I(P;D'\mid B_P)
 =\mathsf I(D;D'\mid P,B_P)-\mathsf I(D;D'\mid B_P)$$ and conditional product comparison therefore imply that its left side is at most $C_*\eta$. The first term is at least $(1+\gamma)e-22h-C_*\eta$, by <a href="#eq:prediction-lower" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:prediction-lower">[eq:prediction-lower]</a> and <a href="#eq:prediction-intersection" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:prediction-intersection">[eq:prediction-intersection]</a>; the second is at most $(1-\gamma)e+6h+C_*\eta$, by <a href="#eq:prediction-upper" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:prediction-upper">[eq:prediction-upper]</a> for the other marginal. Thus $2\gamma e\leq28h+C_*\eta$, contrary to the eccentricity hypothesis after fixing $C_*$. It follows that the complementary angle-proximity event has probability at least $3/4$. For each $P=p$, choose one normal maximizing the conditional mass of a ball of radius $C\epsilon^{4h}$. Averaging the two-copy probability shows that the single-copy part predicted by these normals has mass at least $3/4$.

On coarse cells of zero probability choose an arbitrary normal. This extends the table $n(P)$ to every cell that will index an atom subdivision, without changing the asserted event. ◻

</details>

<a id="pm-h-59"></a>
#### The subclasses and the current endpoint law

Retain the buffered and, in the elongated case, predicted-normal parts just constructed. The table $n(P)$ and the translated grid are now fixed. Their selection probabilities, together with the earlier mass-floor and shape selections, are included in one preparation event $A_{\rm pre}$ in the original sample space $\Omega$. We will restore the incoming conditional probability bound after the atom partition and the winning map have been fixed.

For an earlier atom $T$, let $P(T)$ be its buffered coarse cell. In the elongated case first mark the atom according to whether the normal of its assigned aperture $E_\iota(T)$ lies within $2C\epsilon^h$ of $n(P(T))$. This divides each whole class into aligned and misaligned atoms; both parts remain available when the winner is chosen. In the isotropic case no such mark is needed.

<a id="eq:velocity-fiber-regularity"></a>
<a id="eq:prepared-velocity-probability"></a>
Let $W(T)$ record the velocity at depth $u_r=u_t+h$. It records the component along $n(P(T))$ in the elongated case and both components in the isotropic case. These are the original depth units; after subtracting $b_*$, the fine spacing is $\epsilon^{u_r-b_*}$. Within each marked part of $\mathcal T_\iota^{\rm all}$, and for each $P$, bin $$\log_{1/\epsilon}\!\left(\#\{T:(P(T),W(T))=(p,w)\}\right)$$ with mesh $\xi$. Among fibers in one such size bin, bin the logarithm of the number of represented $W$’s at $P$, again with mesh $\xi$. Write $k\ge0$ for this second numerical tag and $d=1$ in the elongated case, $d=2$ in the isotropic case. For each resulting subclass and every represented $P$, $$\epsilon^{-k+\xi}\leq \#\{W\mid P\}\leq\epsilon^{-k-\xi},
 \qquad k\leq dh+C\xi+\frac{\log C}{\ell}.
 \label{eq:velocity-fiber-regularity}$$ The last bound covers a velocity cell of width $C\epsilon^{u_t}$ by cells of width $\epsilon^{u_r}$ in $d$ dimensions. The sizes of two nonempty $(P,W)$ fibers in this subclass differ by at most $\epsilon^{-\xi}$. Hence its uniform atom law satisfies $$\mathbb P(W=w\mid P,J)\leq\epsilon^{k-2\xi}.
 \label{eq:prepared-velocity-probability}$$ Here $J$ will be the label of the subclass when it is chosen. The subdivision groups the numerical fiber-size and $k$ tags across different $P$’s; $P$ itself remains random in the subclass and is not appended as an auxiliary value of $J$. This distinction keeps the later conditional cost of $J$ small.

These are the final subdivisions that change atom sets. Later tags, such as total size, label a whole subclass. Let $S_\epsilon$ bound the number of available subclasses at a geometric localizer; at fixed depths $\log S_\epsilon=o(\ell)$. Their labels contain $J_0$, the $\iota$ tags, the alignment mark when present, the two numerical velocity tags, and any whole-subclass tags. The winner map will choose one such tuple $J(\omega)$. For its atom set $\mathcal T_J$, set $\mathcal T_J^{\rm all}:=\mathcal T_\iota^{\rm all}$, $E(T):=E_\iota(T)$, and $$N(J)=\#\mathcal T_J,\qquad
 N_{\rm all}(J)=\#\mathcal T_\iota^{\rm all},\qquad
 m(J)=m(\iota),\qquad g(J)=g(\iota).$$ Thus $N_{\rm all}$ still counts the whole greedy class before alignment and velocity subdivision. Its cap upper bound persists on $\mathcal T_J$; its assigned-fiber lower bound continues to refer to the whole class.

<a id="eq:repayment-winner-floor"></a>
Write $\mathfrak a_O(\varphi)$ for the normalized pairing with the fixed site test, so $m_O(\varphi)=|\mathfrak a_O(\varphi)|^2$, and $h_J=\sum_{T\in\mathcal T_J}c_Tg_T$. Put $$q_0=C_A\epsilon^{A-A_0/2}<\tfrac12.$$ Choose at each retained sample a subclass maximizing $|\mathfrak a_O(h_J)|$, breaking ties by a fixed rule. All atom sets, superpositions, and this map to $J$ are now fixed. Applied to these final subclasses, <a href="#eq:packet-winner-mass" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:packet-winner-mass">[eq:packet-winner-mass]</a> gives <a id="eq:repayment-original-winning"></a>$$\begin{aligned}
 |\mathfrak a_O(h_J)|
 &\ge\frac{1-q_0}{S_\epsilon}\sqrt{m_O(f)}
 \ge\frac{1-q_0}{S_\epsilon}\epsilon^{A_0/2}\|f\|_2,
 \label{eq:repayment-winner-floor}\\
 m_O(f)&\le (1-q_0)^{-2}S_\epsilon^2m_O(h_J)
          \le4S_\epsilon^2m_O(h_J).
 \label{eq:repayment-original-winning}
\end{aligned}$$ The mass-term loss $3\log_{1/\epsilon}\!\left(S_\epsilon\right)+3\log_{1/\epsilon}\!\left(1/(1-q_0)\right)$ is included in $\mathcal R$. In the elongated case both alignment marks participated in this choice.

<a id="eq:repayment-transport-order"></a>
After this finite menu, winner map, and coefficient cutoff are fixed, Lemma <a href="#lem:packet-decomposition" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:packet-decomposition">37</a> allows one common transport power $$A_{\rm tr}>(B+Q_0+1)/2
 \label{eq:repayment-transport-order}$$ for every retained subclass, without a new coefficient cutoff. Its constants depend only on the fixed data and $Q_0$. This order controls the alignment collapse and the later candidate truncation, and is unchanged by subsequent subclass selections.

Take the endpoint law conditioned on $A_{\rm pre}$. If $k_f>0$, apply Lemma <a href="#lem:packet-credit-retention" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:packet-credit-retention">45</a> to this event, using its probability under $\pi^{\rm in}$, and remove the exceptional $P_f$ fibers. This changes the endpoint law and its full $J$ marginal, while leaving the atom sets, counts, $g,m$, and winner map fixed. The pointwise geometric and mass comparisons persist. Apply Proposition <a href="#prop:finite-packet-composition" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="prop:finite-packet-composition">41</a> anew to this law; its new deficit inequality controls the mean $\mathbb E\log_{1/\epsilon}\!\left(N_{\rm all}/N\right)$ under its new $J$ marginal.

<a id="eq:repayment-credit-cost"></a>
For each later numerical-tag or alignment restriction $A$, use its probability $p_A$ in the current normalized law. When $k_f>0$, repeat the retention lemma and the exceptional-fiber score split. In either case reapply composition with the same frozen data. Each retention application adds $$\zeta+\log_{1/\epsilon}\!\left(1/p_A\right)
 \label{eq:repayment-credit-cost}$$ to the incoming error. Use the weighted tag rule of Section <a href="#sec:packet-composition" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:packet-composition">10</a> with its current union mass $p$ and shifted deficit $R$: it supplies probability at least $p/(4S_\epsilon)$ and conditional deficit at most $4R/p$. Only a prescribed finite number of these operations is used.

The following exclusion determines which marked subclasses can remain.

<a id="stmt-lem-orientation-alignment"></a>
<div id="lem:orientation-alignment" class="lemma">

<a id="eq:alignment-misaligned-mass"></a>
**Lemma 47** (Alignment of the selected earlier aperture). *For the elongated prepared cut, let $\nu$ be a current endpoint law supported on $A_{\rm pre}$, with the frozen winner map, and let $d_i,R_t$ be its deficits and bound from Proposition <a href="#prop:finite-packet-composition" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="prop:finite-packet-composition">41</a>. Let $B$ be a $J$-measurable event of misaligned winners, with $p=\nu(B)>0$, and put $\varrho=\nu(\,\cdot\mid B)$. In local coordinates write $e=a-b$ and $(j,l)$ for the assigned-cap widths. Assume the common shape bins satisfy $$l=e+h+O(\eta),\qquad l-j\ge e_0-O(\eta),$$ as supplied by the boundary alternative, and that the prepared packet, cap, and label errors are included in $C_*\eta$. Then $$p\,[2\gamma e_0-C_*(h+\eta)]
 \le \mathbb E_\nu\!\left[\boldsymbol1_B(d_1+3d_2+3d_3)\right]
 \le 3R_t .
 \label{eq:alignment-misaligned-mass}$$ Thus a positive bracket bounds the current probability of misaligned winners by the current finite deficit.*

</div>

<details id="proof-stmt-lem-orientation-alignment"><summary>Proof of stmt-lem-orientation-alignment</summary>

*Proof.* Because $B$ is $J$-measurable, $\varrho(\,\cdot\mid J)=\nu(\,\cdot\mid J)$ on $B$, so the local deficits are inherited. Work at a fixed $J$, subtract $b_*=b$ from widths, put $\delta_J=d_2(J)+d_3(J)$, and let $M_j$ be the earlier isotropic depth-$j$ cell.

For this comparison only, let $\mathcal O_J^\varrho=\{O(\omega):\varrho(\omega)>0,\ J(\omega)=J\}$. For fixed $P,C_t$, collapse the winning masses as $$m^{\rm buf}_{P,C_t}
 =\sum_{\substack{O\in\mathcal O_J^\varrho\\O\mapsto(P,C_t)}}m_O(h_J).$$ This sum counts each geometric site once, with the allowed bounded lattice multiplicity. Every tested site is buffered, so each of its possible contributors shares its $P$. Write $\mathcal T_{J,P}=\{T\in\mathcal T_J:P(T)=P\}$ and $N_{J,P}=\#\mathcal T_{J,P}$. The finite mass bound of Proposition <a href="#prop:packet-trivial-growth" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="prop:packet-trivial-growth">40</a>, with the fixed floor and tail comparison, bounds the collapsed mass by $mN_{J,P}$ with the stated finite error. Only then sample a contributor: $$\varrho^P(\omega,T)=\varrho(\omega)
   \frac{\boldsymbol1_{\{T\in\mathcal T_{J(\omega),P(\omega)}\}}}
        {N_{J(\omega),P(\omega)}}.$$ The floor and tail comparison ensure $N_{J,P}>0$ on the tested samples. This kernel preserves the whole endpoint sample; its atom marginal may be biased. The following entropies are conditional on $J$ under this law.

<a id="eq:alignment-biased-entropy"></a>
The entropy calculation of Proposition <a href="#prop:packet-trivial-growth" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="prop:packet-trivial-growth">40</a> bounds $P_J$ above by $$\mathsf H(T)+\tfrac32\log_{1/\epsilon}\!\left(m\right)+
 \tfrac12\{\mathsf H(T\mid D)+(1-\gamma)e\}
 +\mathsf H(C_t\mid T)+C_*\eta.$$ Here $\mathsf H(T)\le\log_{1/\epsilon}\!\left(N\right)$ and $\mathsf H(C_t\mid T)\le2h+C_*\eta$. For every sampled atom at $P$ and every aperture $D$ over that $P$, the buffered velocity and root-position columns differ from those of the paired output by at most the cell widths. Since $a=u_t+O(\eta)$, a fixed enlargement of the root-referred cap of $D$ contains all these atoms, with the charged depth error. The cap upper bound gives $\mathsf H(T\mid D)\le g-(1-\gamma)e+C_*\eta$. The definitions of $d_2,d_3$ give $$P_J=A_J+2\beta_{\mathrm q}h+2\mathcal R-\delta_J\ge A_J-\delta_J.$$ Comparing the two score bounds yields $$\mathsf H(T)\ge\log_{1/\epsilon}\!\left(N\right)-\delta_J-C_*(h+\eta),\qquad
 \mathsf H(T\mid D)\ge g-(1-\gamma)e-2\delta_J-C_*(h+\eta).
 \label{eq:alignment-biased-entropy}$$

<a id="eq:alignment-assigned-entropy"></a>
Before subdivision the number of distinct assigned $E$ labels is at most $\epsilon^{-\log_{1/\epsilon}\!\left(N_{\rm all}\right)+g-w(j,l)-C_*\eta}$, by the whole-class fiber lower bound of Lemma <a href="#lem:cap-class" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:cap-class">38</a>. Since $E$ is assigned deterministically to $T$, $$\mathsf H(T\mid E)\ge
 g-w(j,l)-d_1(J)-\delta_J-C_*(h+\eta).
 \label{eq:alignment-assigned-entropy}$$ The whole-fiber count has thus cost $d_1(J)$ for the retained, possibly biased law.

On $A_{\rm pre}$, the normal of $D$ is within $C\epsilon^{4h}$ of $n(P)$. A misaligned $E$ therefore makes angle at least $C\epsilon^h$ with it. Their two column intersections fit isotropic caps of depth $e-C_*h-C_*\eta$, so $$\mathsf H(T\mid D,E)\le g-2e+C_*(h+\eta).$$ Subtracting from <a href="#eq:alignment-assigned-entropy" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:alignment-assigned-entropy">[eq:alignment-assigned-entropy]</a> and using $l=e+h+O(\eta)$ gives, for fixed $J$, $$\mathsf I(T;D\mid E)\ge
 (1+\gamma)(e-j)-d_1(J)-\delta_J-C_*(h+\eta).$$ Average under $\varrho_J$, absorbing the common-bin errors: <a id="eq:alignment-information-lower"></a>$$\mathsf I_{\varrho^P}(T;D\mid E,J)\ge
 (1+\gamma)(e-j)-\mathbb E_\varrho(d_1+\delta_J)-C_*(h+\eta).
 \label{eq:alignment-information-lower}$$ As $E$ is a function of $T$ given $J$, and determines $M_j$ up to the charged lists, $$\mathsf I_{\varrho^P}(T;D\mid E,J)
 \le \mathsf I_{\varrho^P}(T;D\mid M_j,J)+C_*\eta.$$

For the reverse estimate, coarsen $D$ to widths $0,j$, using the center of $M_j$. Its normal projection is confined by the coarsened strip, and the tangent width is zero-depth, so the resulting labels form a charged list determined by $D$. Enlarge each rectangle by a fixed factor to contain the entire $M_j$ cell; its projections are bounded by its diagonal. The enlargement depends only on the rectangle label. Resample it conditional on $(M_j,J)$, independently of $T$, and call it $U$. It is faithful for every atom in that cell, has weight $(1-\gamma)j$, and the cap bound gives on each $J$ fiber $$\mathsf I(T;U)\ge \mathsf H(T)-g+(1-\gamma)j-C_*\eta.$$ Adjoin these kernels under $\varrho_J$, retaining the notation $\varrho^P$. The joint law of the enlarged coarsening and $M_j$ is preserved on each fiber. Since $M_j$ is a function of $T$ given $J$, $$\mathsf I_{\varrho^P}(M_j;D\mid J)
 \ge \mathsf I_{\varrho^P}(M_j;U\mid J)-C_*\eta
 =\mathsf I_{\varrho^P}(T;U\mid J)-C_*\eta.$$ Average the cap bound and the second inequality in <a href="#eq:alignment-biased-entropy" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:alignment-biased-entropy">[eq:alignment-biased-entropy]</a>. Combining them with this display gives <a id="eq:alignment-information-upper"></a>$$\mathsf I_{\varrho^P}(T;D\mid M_j,J)\le
 (1-\gamma)(e-j)+2\mathbb E_\varrho\delta_J+C_*(h+\eta).
 \label{eq:alignment-information-upper}$$ The lower and upper bounds imply $$2\gamma(e-j)\le
 \mathbb E_\varrho[d_1+3(d_2+d_3)]+C_*(h+\eta).$$ The common shape bins give $e-j\ge e_0-h-O(\eta)$. Multiply by $p$, use $p\mathbb E_\varrho[\cdot]=\mathbb E_\nu[\boldsymbol1_B\,\cdot]$, and use nonnegativity of the $d_i$ and <a href="#eq:finite-packet-deficits" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:finite-packet-deficits">[eq:finite-packet-deficits]</a>. This proves <a href="#eq:alignment-misaligned-mass" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:alignment-misaligned-mass">[eq:alignment-misaligned-mass]</a>. ◻

</details>

<a id="eq:repayment-selected-credit"></a>
For the elongated application, first select a branch with qualifying common earlier shape bins by the weighted rule, perform credit retention when needed, and recompose. Let $\nu$ be this current law and let $B$ be all its misaligned winners. This event is $J$-measurable. If $\nu(B)=0$, the law is already aligned; otherwise <a href="#eq:alignment-misaligned-mass" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:alignment-misaligned-mass">[eq:alignment-misaligned-mass]</a> applies to its entire current mass. At sufficiently small current deficit, the aligned complement has positive probability, tending to one with the positive gap fixed. Restrict to that complement, then apply the current-law retention and recomposition rule. In either alternative, apply the same rule to any remaining common numerical-bin selections and recompose after the last restriction. Denote the resulting endpoint law on $\Omega$ by $\pi$, and now set $P_t=P_t(\pi)$, the score of the original input with its original masses. Every final elongated winning class is aligned. The buffered property, and prediction when present, persist pointwise. The incoming bound is $$\sup_w\pi(W_f=w\mid P_f=p)
 \le \epsilon^{k_f-\alpha_f}
 \quad\text{for every \(p\) with \(\pi(P_f=p)>0\)},
 \label{eq:repayment-selected-credit}$$ where $\alpha_f$ includes the initial error and the sum of <a href="#eq:repayment-credit-cost" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:repayment-credit-cost">[eq:repayment-credit-cost]</a>. When $k_f=0$, this estimate will be replaced by nonnegativity of conditional mutual information.

<a id="eq:repayment-input-bridge"></a>
Every expectation in the rest of this cut uses the selected marginal $\pi_J$, unless a different law is explicitly displayed. In particular, set <a id="eq:repayment-benchmark"></a>$$\begin{aligned}
 d_1(J)&=\log_{1/\epsilon}\!\left(N_{\rm all}(J)/N(J)\right),\nonumber\\
 A_J&=\log_{1/\epsilon}\!\left(N(J)\right)+\tfrac32\log_{1/\epsilon}\!\left(m(J)\right)+\tfrac12g(J),\nonumber\\
 K_r^*(\pi)&=\mathsf H_\pi(J)+b_*+
   \mathbb E_\pi\left[\log_{1/\epsilon}\!\left(N_{\rm all}(J)\right)
                  +\tfrac32\log_{1/\epsilon}\!\left(m(J)\right)+\tfrac12g(J)\right],
 \nonumber\\
 B_r&=\mathsf H_\pi(J)+b_*+\mathbb E_\pi A_J
       =K_r^*(\pi)-\mathbb E_\pi d_1 .
 \label{eq:repayment-benchmark}
\end{aligned}$$ The last equality is exact. The number $B_r$ is a benchmark formed with retained counts; it is not asserted to be an earlier score. For the final composition law, put $\Delta_t=K_0+\beta_{\mathrm q}t-P_t$. Its current $d_0$ gives $$B_r+2\beta_{\mathrm q}h-P_t
 =\Delta_t+2\mathcal R-d_0-\mathbb E_\pi d_1
 \le\Delta_t+2\mathcal R .
 \label{eq:repayment-input-bridge}$$

<a id="eq:repayment-earlier-scores"></a>
<a id="eq:repayment-isotropic-score"></a>
The earlier whole-class law and the returned retained-class law are, respectively, <a id="eq:repayment-earlier-laws"></a>$$\mu^{\rm all}(J,T)=\pi_J(J)
   \frac{\boldsymbol1_{\{T\in\mathcal T_J^{\rm all}\}}}{N_{\rm all}(J)},
 \qquad
 \mu(J,T)=\pi_J(J)
   \frac{\boldsymbol1_{\{T\in\mathcal T_J\}}}{N(J)}.
 \label{eq:repayment-earlier-laws}$$ Both use the selected marginal $\pi_J$. Their observations are the sites of $T$ at time $r$, and their masses are coefficient tests of the original input $f$. With assigned caps $E(T)$, finite composition gives $$\begin{aligned}
 P_r^{\rm all}&\ge K_r^*(\pi)-\mathcal R,\nonumber\\
 P_r^{\rm ret}&\ge K_r^*(\pi)-\tfrac32\mathbb E_\pi d_1-\mathcal R
       =B_r-\tfrac12\mathbb E_\pi d_1-\mathcal R .
 \label{eq:repayment-earlier-scores}
\end{aligned}$$ In the elongated case $\mu$ continues the aligned assigned cap. In the isotropic case the same atom law uses the exact isotropic boundary aperture of width $u_r$. The horizon and packet menu include this cap by Proposition <a href="#prop:boundary-alternatives" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="prop:boundary-alternatives">44</a>. With $b_*=0$, the isotropic score satisfies the separate bound $$P_r^{\rm iso}\ge
 B_r-\tfrac12\mathbb E_\pi(g-2u_r)-C\mathcal R .
 \label{eq:repayment-isotropic-score}$$ This uses weight $2u_r$ and nonnegative conditional entropy, independently of the assigned-fiber gain. A charged selection fixed the common $g$ bin, and the final credit trim, when needed, preserved its pointwise support before $\pi$ was named. Thus $g-2u_r$ has the required small error under the displayed expectation.

<a id="eq:repayment-outgoing-credit"></a>
Finally, <a href="#eq:prepared-velocity-probability" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:prepared-velocity-probability">[eq:prepared-velocity-probability]</a> applies under $\mu(\,\cdot\mid J)$. Since the numerical $k$ tags are common bins under $\pi_J$, averaging in $J$ gives $$\mu(W=w\mid P=p)\le\epsilon^{k-C_*\eta}
 \quad\text{for every \(p\) with \(\mu(P=p)>0\)}.
 \label{eq:repayment-outgoing-credit}$$ This statement holds for either earlier aperture assignment under $\mu$, which is uniform within each retained class.

<a id="pm-h-60"></a>
#### From winning masses to candidate masses

Before stating the repayment estimate, we finish the finite comparison of masses that its proof will use. Work in the translated coordinates of a selected localizer $J$, put $u=u_t-b_*$, and write $$\rho=\epsilon^u,\qquad s=\epsilon^{u+h},\qquad
 \sigma=\epsilon^{u+2h}=s^2/\rho,\qquad \lambda_{\rm loc}=s^{-2}.$$ The buffered $P$ cell has width $\rho$. Let $Q=Q(J,O)$ record $P,C_t$, and the position cell of side $s$ at $C_t$.
